33 
 
 
ABANOUB EL-NEHISSY 
(The martyr) 
St. Abanoub was born in Nehissah, in the city of Talkha in the 4th Century. 
His parents were pious loving parents who raised him with Christian values 
and planted in him the love for God and the Holy Bible. He was only 12 years 
of age when both his parents departed to Paradise. Missing his parents was so 
devastating to the young Abanoub, that he was called the lamented boy for he 
was sorrowful for so long. Some might ask wonder how could he manage to 
withstand all the sufferings that he encountered later on and yet could not resist 
the loss of his parents. 
It is true that despite our faith in heavenly life, it will not strip us from our 
human feelings; instead, it would sanctify them. We can see an illustration of 
that in the presence of St. Paul, who wrote about the door being opened for 
evangelism in Troas, and yet he could not find peace in his soul, for he could 
not find his friend Titus, so he left the city. "Furthermore, when I came to Troas 
to [preach] Christ's gospel, and a door was opened to me by the Lord, I had no 
rest in my spirit, because I did not find Titus, my brother, but taking my leave 
of them, I departed for Macedonia” (2 Cor. 2:12-13). This situation shows the 
vulnerability of human nature, and God may allow those weaknesses to prevent 
us from boasting. Another example of weakness was with our  great father 
Abraham, who said that his wife Sarah was his sister for fear that the king 
might kill him to take her for a wife (Gen. 20:2). Also, our beloved St. Mark, 
who left Paul and Barnabas and caused them to have an argument and ended 
up separating from each other (Acts 13:3), and St. Peter, who was leaving 
Rome for fear of persecution and Jesus appeared to him too and kindly 
corrected him. Therefore, we should not be troubled when we show weakness 
despite the grace given to us, for it is beneficial in keeping us humble and 
urging us to ask God to work in us and with us. 
In the village's church: 
One day, Abanoub went to the church and heard the priest during the sermon 
encouraging the congregation to endure with joy the suffering and persecution 
they were getting for their faith. After the Holy Communion, the young 
Abanoub went home, while the priest’s words still ringing in his ears.  
At home, he knelt to pray, asking for God ’s guidance. Then, he stood up 
and started walking towards the city of Semeno od (about 12 miles away), 
while rejoicing in the spirit and desiring to have the heavenly crown. 
In Semenood:

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 35
passages.text:
35 
 
At this point, the governor asked Abanoub to pray for him so that he and his 
soldiers could be healed. Abanoub told him that God would heal them in Atrib. 
When they got there, Abanoub prayed for the governor and treated him in the 
Lord’s name in the presence of Atrib ’s governor. This miracle caused many 
pagans to believe in the Lord, and some were martyred. 
In Atrib (Banha) 
Regardless, the governor of Atrib tortured Abanoub with all kinds of torture 
methods and put him in boiling oil and cut up his feet and hands and b linded 
his eyes with hot rods. During all these trials, God did not leave Abanoub, but 
He always sent Archangel Michael to heal him. Many witnesses became 
Christians and gladly became martyrs, from watching the young Abanoub 
enduring all that suffering and still praising his God. 
In Alexandria 
After the governor of Atrib saw the multitude of people accepting 
Abanoub's faith, he tied him up with reliable chains and sent him to Alexandria. 
There, he met a woman who had an evil spirit, and he forced the spirit  out of 
her, and she became Christian. Consequently, the soldiers killed her because 
she said that she believed in Christ.  
Abanoub continued to confess his faith in our Lord Jesus before the 
governor Arminius of Alexandria who also tortured him and put him in a room 
filled with snakes and serpents and the Archangel Michael got him out of it, 
and the snakes followed him, and one of them coiled itself around the 
governor's neck. He cried out to Abanoub, and he saved him, which caused 
many to believe and become martyrs.  
Abanoub suffered more tortures and was finally beheaded outside the city 
on a high rock where he stood to pray, asking God to forgive him and to accept 
his soul.  
St. Julius El-Akfahsy took his body and buried him in his town Nehissah, 
and wrote his story. His body was moved from Nehissah to Semenood, and the 
church celebrates his martyrdom on the 24th of Abib. 
 
ABANOUB, THE CONFESSOR, ST. 
The word ‘Abanoub’ is derived from the Coptic word ‘Pi-Noub’ meaning 
(gold). This saint was a virtuous mon k in one of the monasteries of Upper 
Egypt in the days of Diocletian, who tortured and shed the blood of 80 martyrs 
in a single day. 
It so happened when the name of St. Abanoub was mentioned before 
Arianius, the governor of Ansena, that the governor called him and asked him 
to worship the idols. The saint answered, saying: “How can I forsake my Lord

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 52
passages.text:
52 
 
the entire night in the church, attending the Holy Liturgy in the early morning, 
partaking of the Holy Communion, and then he would go back to his cave. 
His Scribing: 
The saint was gifted with beautiful handwriting in both Coptic and Arabic 
languages. He preoccupied himself with copying so many ancient books. He 
also authored so many new books. Besides, he cared for binding the books and 
making leather gir dles and Eskeems. In addition to all those preoccupations 
and seclusion, he was the father of confession for all the monks of the 
‘Baramus’ monastery. 
Finally, Fr. ‘Abd-el-Mesih El-Masoudy’ reposed in peace on the 11th of Tout 
1621 AM (21 December 1905), at the age of 88 years. He was a monk for 71 
years in the monasteries of ‘Moharraq,’ ‘Baramus’ and in seclusion. 
[The Story of the Coptic Church, Bk 5, p. 106] 
 
ABD-JESUS THE BISHOP AND HIS COMPANIONS, SS. 
(The martyrs) 
In the days of the king of Persia ‘Shapur II’ (309-379 AD), around the year 
361 AD, five who carried the same name “Abd-jesus’ (Hebed-Jesus) were 
martyred: one of them was a bishop, three priests, a deacon and a monk. 
Bishop ‘Abdjesus,’ along with another bishop called ‘Abdas’ and a third 
bishop named ‘Dausas,’ were led captives to the area of ‘Zabde,’ where they 
were martyred. 
[A Dictionary of Christian Biography, Vol. II, p. 23] 
 
ABDON AND SENNEN, SS. 
(The martyrs) 
Two Persian Christians who were martyred in the days of Emperor ‘Decius’ 
(249-251 AD). Their biography could be found under the letter “S." 
 
ABE-FAM (Bifam/Phoebammon) EL-TAHAWY 
(The martyr) 
Pagan parents raised this saint in the city of ‘Taha’ in Upper Egypt. When 
he was 12 years old, his father gave many gifts to the prince to let his son join 
the army. Abe -Fam (Bifam/Phoebammon) eventually became a prominent 
officer, known for his love of justice and his defense of the oppressed and the

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 36
passages.text:
36 
 
Jesus Christ, and worship the idols made of stone?! ” Therefore, he tortured 
him severely, and then he sent him to the five western cities (the Pentapolis), 
where he was imprisoned for as long as seven years until Diocletian perished. 
When the righteous Emperor Constantine reigned, he gave his command to set 
free all those Christians who were in prisons and to bring them forth to him to 
have their blessing. He specified that in case it is difficult to bring them all, to 
bring only the prominent ones among them, such as ‘Zacharias Al-Ahnasy,’ 
Maximianus of Fayum, Agabius of ‘Dakhnin,’ and Abanoub of ‘Balaos.' The 
saints came out of their imprisonments, singing praises to God.  
At that time, St. Abanoub, the confessor, returned from ‘Pentapolis’ and 
dwelt on a mountain close to his homeland. When the Emperor’s envoy came, 
they took him on a boat to Ansena, where he encountered the believers, and 
the bishops ordained h im as a priest. And, it so happened that, while he was 
uttering: “The Holies are for the holy, ” that he saw the Lord Christ 
transfiguring in the church with His exalted glory.  
The Emperor’s envoy traveled together with 72 saints and put every two of 
them in a carriage, and while passing through one of the cities, where there 
was a nunnery of virgins, 700 of them came out singing hymns before them.  
When they reached the capital, the king sought from them to change their 
worn-out clothes to expensive new on es, but they declined his offer. He then 
kissed their wounds, honored them, and offered them precious gifts, which 
they also refused, except for some curtains and vessels for their churches, to 
which they returned, and St. Abanoub returned to his monastery. 
Finally, after fulfilling his strife, he reposed in peace. 
[Synaxarion, 23 Paona] 
 
ABASKHIRON AL-QUALINI 
(The martyr) 
The saint ’s name is derived from two words: The word ‘Abba’ means 
(Father) and the word ‘Skhiron,’ ‘Eskhirus,’ or ‘Eskaros,’ which means (the 
Strong). He was born in the town of ‘Qualin’ in the governorate of ‘Kafr El-
Sheikh’ in the Nile delta. He was a brave and beloved soldier, famous and 
appreciated by his leaders and fellow soldiers in the regiment that was camped 
in ‘Atrib’ (Benha). 
His position from the decree of Diocletian: 
Emperor Diocletian issued an order, mandating the sacrifice to idols by 
everybody all over his empire. When this decree was declared before the 
regiment’s soldiers, ‘Abaskhiron’ refused totally to obey. Then, the governor

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 29
passages.text:
29 
 
Besides, his brother ‘Aba-Bishai’ was martyred on the first day of the 
‘Nasie’ (The little month).  
 [The Synaxarion: 29 Paona] 
 
ABAHOR, THE MONK, ST. 
This father from ‘Abraht’ in the area of the ‘Ashmonein,’ was an elect monk 
who surpassed many saints in his worship. Loving solitude and living alone in 
the wilderness, he was envied by the devil who appeared to him and said: “In 
the wilderness, you can overcome me because you are there alone, but I 
challenge you if you are brave, go to Alexandria." He instantly set forth to 
Alexandria, where he stayed sometimes serving the prisoners. 
It so happened that some horses were galloping in midtown, and one of 
them knocked down a little kid who instantly died. As St. Abahor was standing 
at the place where that incident took place, the devil provoked some people 
around to shout aloud, claiming that it was the old monk who killed him. When 
many started to revile and to scoff him, St. Abahor calmly took the kid to his 
bosom, prayed in his heart t o the Lord Christ, and then made the sign of the 
cross on him. The kid came back to life, and he gave him to his parents. Those 
around him glorified God and started to make it up to the old monk, who, 
fearing from the vainglory, he fled to the wilderness, where he dwelt for days 
in a monastery. 
When it was time for him to depart from this world, he saw a group of saints 
calling him to join them, for which he greatly rejoiced, became joyful, called 
his spiritual disciples to inform them that he will soon depart to the Lord Christ, 
and provided them with his last commandment. Hearing that, they much 
grieved that they will be orphans after his departure. He felt sick for a little 
while, and then he delivered his soul in the Lord’s hand. 
 [The Synaxarion: 2 Kiahk] 
 
ABAHOR 
(The martyr) 
He was born in ‘Seriakos’ to a father who was a blacksmith. Deciding to die 
a martyr, he set forth to ‘Al-Farma’ (nowadays: ‘Port Said ’), where he 
confessed the Lord Christ before its governor. The governor tortured him but 
much astonished at how the Lord came to comfort him and heal his wounds. 
Therefore, the governor, together with his entire household, proclaimed their 
faith in the Lord Christ. Accordingly, they were martyred by the hands of the

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 4, p. 362
passages.text:
362 
 
youth of both genders . He also supported hundreds of advanced youth to 
complete their higher education. Then he got occupied with printing the 
lessons of Sunday schools and publishing the Ecclesiastical books. 
• In the year 1938, he contributed to establishing the “ Bookstore of el-
MaĥAbba” to publish and distribute all kinds of Coptic publications,  
through which he issued “The Message of el-MaĥAbbah,” and then “The 
Calendar of el-MaĥAbbah.” 
• Continuing on his spiritual strife , he established “The House of e l-
MaĥAbbah” in the year 1941 . He  annexed it by setting the church of 
Archangel Michael and St. Shenouda, which was dedicated on the 21 st of 
September 1957. 
• As though work led to more energy, so he established a building to embrace 
all the diverse activities of the Society of el-MaĥAbbah, then the House of 
el-MaĥAbbah in the year 1960. And adorned the building by an altar in the 
name of St. Anba Abram, which eventually turned into a church.  
• With his advanced age, his activity increased , and he set the foundation of 
a nursery and a house for the out -of-town female students, facing the 
building of the Society of el-MaĥAbbah on Jazerit Badran street. 
When the 116th Pope of Alexandria, St. Kyrillos VI (Cyril VI: 1959-1971) 
decided to establish a vast Cathedral in the name of St. Mark the Apostle on 
the land of Anba Roweis, the pope formed a committee to collect donations for 
such an enormous enterprise. He chose archon Younan Nakhla as one of its 
members. In the year 1972, the country president Anwar Sadat (1970 -1981) 
bestowed on him the highest medal of Imtiaz (excellence) of the first grade . 
And, the governor of Cairo gave him a letter of appreciation on the day of 
Social Labor as an appreciation of his endless strife. After such shining 
conflict, he departed Paradise to enjoy the company of the Saints in the 1970s. 
     [The Faithful Synaxarion: 24 Toba] 
 
YOUNAN, THE MONK, ST. 
Cf. St. Jonah (Younan), the Monk. 
 
YOUSEF ABU-DAQN EL-MANUFI 
Yousef (Joseph) Abu-Daqn el-Manufi was one of the great Coptic archons 
in the 17 th century. A contemporary of the 101 st Pope of Alexandria, Abba 
Marcos VI’ (1646-1656). He authored a book entitled “ The True History of 
the Copts in Libya, Nubia, and Ethiopia.” In this book, he gave some details 
about the social and spiritual conditions  of those Copts  as well as their

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 50
passages.text:
50 
 
who granted his parents another son, and they called him ‘Hanna.' 
In the year 1914, ‘Samaan’ set forth to Abba Macarius monastery in the 
‘Scetis’ wilderness, where he became a monk by the name of ‘Abd-el-Mesih.' 
There, he was attached to Fr. ‘Abd-el-Mesih Salib El -Massoudy’ of the 
‘Baramus’ monastery and his brother Fr. ‘Yacob.' On hearing about the virtues 
of this saint, Fr. ‘Abd-el-Mesih El-Macary’; the 113th Pope of Alexandria Abba 
‘Yoannes XIX’ (1928-1942) planned to ordain him as a bishop. However, as 
the saint did not want to be raised to that rank, he pretended to be crazy and 
half-wit that the pope had to expel him from the papal residence. From that 
time on, he kept on that pretense, whenever he intended to escape from any 
vainglory. Fr. ‘Abd-el-Mesih Salib El -Massoudy’ counseled him to leave the 
monastery and to keep on following the same behavior. Therefore, he often 
pretended that he wanted to get married.  After he left the monastery, he lived 
in the village of ‘El-Manahra’ in his home district of ‘Matai’ in ‘El-Minya.' 
Therefore, he acquired the new title ‘El-Manahry.' 
His Worship: 
Nobody knows about his prayers, but he used to live in seclusion praying in 
his cell for periods extending to several weeks. He used to tie a rope to the 
ceiling of his cell and tie its other end around his waist to pull him up in case 
he would fall asleep while praying. He memorized all the praises and the 
church hymns by heart. He ate only once every day at sunset.  
He always gave alms generously to the needy, yet in his own crazy and half-
wit ways. He never had two mantles at the same time, and he lived in a cell 
built with mud bricks and not painted from the inside. In that manner, he gave 
a great example of monastic life. 
God honored him by the gift of performing miracles. And spiritually, he 
reached the rank of the hermits, as testified by the 116th Pope St. ‘Kyrillos VI’ 
(1959-1971). Besides, this saint has prophesied in advance about the ordination 
of Fr. ‘Mina El-Motawahid’ (St. ‘Kyrillos VI’) as a pope over the See of St. 
Mark. 
He finally reposed in peace on the morning of the Great feast of the 
Resurrection (the Easter) on the 6 th of Baramouda 1679 AM (14 April 1963). 
Moreover, since the Palm Sunday, before he reposed, the saint kept saying, “I 
shall be crowned and rejoice the day of the Feast. ” However, at the time, 
nobody paid attention to that statement, because it was also taken lightly as 
one of his usual crazy way of talking. 
[Abba Mena, bishop of Girga: The Biography of a Contemporary Saint: Fr. Abd -
el-Mesih St. Macar]

80 
 
that if he wanted to be healed , he should promise God to forsake the 
priesthood for the rest of his life and to repent regretting his horrible 
behavior. As the priest did promise, the saint came out to pray for him, until 
he was wholly healed of his sickness with true repentance. 
2- A man came to him with his son to get his blessing. But, it happened that 
the son fell from the mountain and died. The father carried him to the cave 
of the saint, placed him in front of the entrance, and without telling the saint 
about what happened, he asked him to bless him. The saint made the sign 
of the cross on the boy, and said to him, “Get up, go to your father, and hold 
his hand.” So the boy did. In great joy, the father cast himself on the ground 
before the saint, thanking him and glorifying God who pe rforms miracles 
through His saints. 
3- Getting to know the day of his repose, he asked the priest to come over to 
perform the Holy Eucharist. He had communion standing on his swollen 
feet, bid farewell from the brethren, blessed them, sought their blessing, 
prayed, and delivered his soul in the hands of the Lord on 25 Amshir. 
His Monastery in Delga: 
A monastery was built in his name close to ‘Beni Khaled, a village of 
‘Delga’ about 20 kilometers south of the province of El-Ashmonein. 
[Nabil Selim: Monasteries of the Fathers (9): St. Epiphanius (Abu Fana) on Mount 
Delga; an annex of his book on ‘The Monasteries of the Fathers (8) on SS Bishai 
and Basentaos of the Tod] 
 
ABU SAAD MANSOUR 
He was among the 11th century Copts. His name was ‘Ebn-Abu- Al-Yomn.' 
He was an eloquent writer and a courageous man. He became a minister in the 
days of Calipha El-Mostanser; but had to quit when the Turkish soldiers sought 
their wages, and there was not enough money in the treasury to fulfill their 
requests. But when their leader  ‘Naser Al -Dawlah’ rebelled against the 
Calipha, then ‘Abu-Saad,’ supported by pro-Calipha regiment, bravely fought 
against him and defeated him. His loyalty and courage had a massive effect on 
the Calipha, who loved him very much. 
[Fr. Manasseh Yohanna: History of the Coptic Church; 1983; p. 398] 
 
ABU SALEM AL-MALATY 
He was among the 18th century Copts. A Coptic physician, by the name of 
‘Abu-Salem El-Nasrany El-Jacoby El-Malaty.' It was claimed that he was not

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 77
passages.text:
77 
 
given to the poor” (Ps. 112:9). 
He was called ‘Mematy’ on account of that when a famine dwelt on Egypt 
in his time, he gave plenty of wheat to the poor; and when the little children, 
knowing of his love, used to beg him calling him by this name; he used to give 
them with compassion. 
[Fr. Manasseh Yohanna: History of the Coptic Church; 1983, p. 399]  
[Martyr Abu Nagaah the Great; cf. Yohanna Abu Nagaah – Synaxarion 19 
Baramouda] 
 
ABU EL-SAIID AL-KATEB 
He was the chief of the archives department in the Fatimid era (in the 11 th 
century). He renovated the church of ‘The Five and their Mother’ (St. Rifka), 
at ‘Manial Shiha,’ in Giza. 
 
ABU AL-TAYEB 
He was among the 11th century Copts. He worked as a Secretary of ‘Naser 
Al-Dawla,’ the leader of the Turkish regiment in the days of Calipha ‘El-
Mostansir.' At that time, the Turks rebelled against the Calipha. They spread 
corruption, robbed the monasteries in Egypt, and kidnaped Pope Christodolus 
seeking to get a ransom for him from the Copts. Abu El -Tayeb hastened and 
used his influence to set him free from their hands. 
[Martyr Abu El-Elah Fahd Ebn Ibrahim: Synaxarion 19 Baramouda] 
 
ABU AL-YOMN YOUSEF 
He was among the 13 th century Copts. His full name wa s ‘Abu-Al-Yomn 
Yousef Ebn Macroah Ebn Zanbour,’ and he was known as the ‘chief treasurer.' 
He worked as the treasurer of the storehouses of the Caliph. Moreover, because 
of his unusual honesty, he was given the responsibility for the collected taxes 
of the entire area of Lower Egypt. 
To express his thanks to God and his love for his brethren, he built a great 
monastery in ‘Tamoah’ in Giza in the name of the martyr ‘Abu-Sifein’ (St. 
Marcorius). He planted vast gardens around it; that the minister ‘Badr Al-
Gamali’ used to spend most of his free time relaxing there. 
 [Fr. Manasseh Yohanna: History of the Coptic Church; 1983; p. 398]

54 
 
 [Nabil Selim and Guirgis El-Meniawy: St. John the Herculean & the Three Saintly 
Abe-Fams, June 1966] 
 
ABE-FAM (Bifam/Phoebammon) OF AUSIM, ST. 
(The martyr) 
St. ‘Abe-Fam’ was born in ‘Ausim’ to a father by the name of Anastasius 
and a pious mother by the name of Susanna. They raised him on the spirit of 
piety, worship, and the love of the poor. When he was nine years old, his father 
sent him to a virtuous priest by the name of ‘Ausanius’ to explain to him the 
Holy Bible and the teachings of the Church. 
One day, while he was on his way to the priest accompanied by another boy, 
he met with a leprous who asked him for a donation. Stretching his hand to 
give him something, the leprous was instantly healed. All the people were 
astonished and felt that this boy would have a great future, that even the priest 
himself sought from the boy to bless him. On the same night, an angel of the 
Lord appeared to tell the priest what would happen to the boy. As for Abe-Fam, 
he increased in repentance before God, fasted every day until evening,  and 
turned his bedroom to a cell for worshipping God. 
The Lord Christ appears to him: 
Worshipping God with piety and faithfulness, the Lord Christ appeared to 
him, and with Him, St. Mary the Virgin, the Mother of God, and the Archangel 
Gabriel. The Lord told him that he would receive the crown of martyrdom. In 
the morning, he was seen with an illuminated face, and a sweet fragrance came 
out of his room. The saint told his friend ‘Tawadros’ what he has seen. Later 
on, ‘Tawadros’ became the bishop of Ausim a nd wrote the biography of the 
saint. 
His Love of Virginity: 
In the feast of the Virgin Mary, his parents made a banquet for the poor, as 
it was their custom every year. They asked him about his intention concerning 
marriage. He answered them: “I intend to remain a virgin until I stand before 
the throne of the Lord Christ my God,” and his parents kept silent. After a few 
days, his father passed away, and the son practiced the works of mercy he 
inherited from his father. 
The Vision had seen by Abba Serapion: 
A saintly hermit by the name of ‘Serapion’ had told ‘Tawadros’ about a night 
vision he saw concerning his friend ‘Abe-Fam.' In that vision, he saw an angel 
who carried him to ‘Ausim,’ and on its west side, he showed him ‘Satanael’ 
(Satan) and his hosts in fearful and terrifying forms. He heard ‘Satanael’

records.question: How did St. Moses the Black come to faith?
records.answer:
St. Moses the Black, originally a notorious gangster, experienced a profound transformation that led him to faith in Jesus Christ. His journey began when he was deeply troubled by his sinful life, which included robbing and killing, and he felt a yearning for redemption. Despite his extreme evil deeds, he looked towards the sun, believing it represented the true God, and sought a way to escape his past. This longing prompted him to seek out the monks of Scetis, known for their holiness and spiritual wisdom [3].

Upon arriving in the wilderness, he encountered St. Isidore, a monk who recognized Moses's desire for change. Moses confessed his sins and expressed his wish to be saved, demonstrating a sincere heart seeking repentance. St. Isidore took him under his wing, teaching him about the Christian faith and the importance of humility and spiritual repentance. He emphasized that true victory over sin comes not from one's own efforts but through God's grace [1][3].

Moses's commitment to his new faith was further solidified through his struggles against temptation and his dedication to ascetic practices, which involved rigorous self-discipline and prayer. He faced intense spiritual battles, often being tormented by thoughts of his past life. However, with guidance from his spiritual father, he learned to rely on God's strength to overcome these challenges [5]. His transformation was so profound that he eventually became a respected monk and was later ordained as a priest, dedicating his life to serving others and preaching the Gospel [1][4]. 

Thus, St. Moses's journey to faith was marked by a deep recognition of his sins, a sincere desire for repentance, and the transformative power of God's grace through the guidance of wise spiritual mentors.

Once four thieves tried to rob his cell, but he tied them together and 
carried them to the church. When the thieves r ealized that he was Moses, 
who used to be the head of a gang of thieves, they repented and wanted to 
become monks. St. Moses preached them with words that moved their hearts.  
Because of his great strife, the devils were stirred more against him, that 
his mentor Abba Isidore counseled him to moderate in his ascetic practices to 
keep them from causing him more troubles. He sought from him to deliver 
himself to God, and He alone would be able to alleviate that fight on him. 
Abba Isidore told him that, to keep  him from thinking that by his ascetic 
efforts, he could overcome the demons, but by humility and spiritual 
repentance, God would fight on our behalf.  
Ordained as a Priest: 
Because of his strife and virtues, they decided to ordain him as a priest. 
They arranged that the ordination would be performed at the patriarchate in 
Alexandria. However, the patriarch wanted to test Moses before ordaining 
him, so he ordered his priests that once they see him about to enter into the 
sanctuary, to drive him out saying: “Get out of here, O you with the 
blackface.” When they did that to him, the patriarch sent a deacon after him, 
and he heard him saying: “They did what you deserved Moses, for you are 
not a human, but dared to mix with men. Why then would you venture to sit  
among them?” St. Moses was ordained as a priest by the hand of the 23 rd 
Pope St. Theophilus (385 -412 AD), who heard at the time a voice saying: 
“Worthy, Worthy, Worthy,” and after putting the white robe on him, they said 
to him: “There you became all -white Moses.” He responded by saying with 
humility: “I wish this to be true on the inside as it is on the outside.” 
His Virtues: 
He lived denying himself that a governor, hearing about his virtues, 
longed to see him. When Moses knew about that, he ran away, bu t it 
happened that the saint passed by the governor in his way to the monastery, 
and he inquired from him about the location of father Moses' cell. St. Moses 
told him: “What do you want from such an old man, who is far from being 
upright.” The governor was disturbed and went to the monastery and told the 
monks about what happened. On understanding the monks how that monk 
looked like, they knew that it was no one but Fr. Moses, who denied himself.  
Because of his love, humility, strife, and intense asceticis m, he was 
granted by God to perform miracles and signs.  
A monk fell into a specific iniquity, and a meeting was held to discuss an 
appropriate penance. Moses was invited to attend, but he refrained from

passages.text:
256 
 
in the form of a girl. She managed to convince him to  spend the night at her 
place. Then, she claimed to him that she was the daughter of one of the kings 
and that she wanted him to marry her, quoting the honor of the marriage of 
the fathers: Ibrahim, Isaac, and Jacob. He accepted her request. Then, she 
claimed that she was a Jew, and he had to convert to her religion to be able to 
marry her. So, Moses was blinded, and he denied his Christ. Then, she (the 
deceptive devil) took him back to the wilderness, where a whole gang of 
devils ridiculed him and made so much fun of him. Finally, the hermit woke 
up and cast himself on the dust and kept crying and supplicating to the 
Compassionate God to forgive him. God sent him Abba Samuel, who told 
him that he would be departing after three days. Then, he took him to the  
church, where he gave him Communion in the Holy Sacraments after 
confessing all that the devil has done to him. St. Moses, the hermit, reposed 
in peace and was buried by Abba Samuel, who wrote his biography, and 
handed it to someone traveling to Alexandria for the benefit of the believers.  
 [The Hermit Fathers, Part 2, p. 25] 
 
MOSES, THE LIBYAN, ST. 
This saint was from Libya. He was so humble and compassionate all the 
time that God granted him the grace to perform the miracles of healing the 
sick. He once said: “When I was young, I lived in a monastery. There, it 
happened that eight monks dug a well, and seventy others built a wall around 
it, in the hope that they would get water from it. They dug it down to the 
depth of about twenty yards, but no water was found. They were very much 
grieved and intended to fill it up with dirt. However, by noontime, w hen 
Abba Pieour came over suddenly to the location of the well and was 
informed about what they were doing, he rebuked them saying: ‘Why did you 
despair, O you of little faith? ’ Then, he went down to the bottom of the well, 
and he prayed there. Afterward, he pushed an iron rod in the well bottom 
three times, saying: ‘O God of the saints, I pray, do not waste the effort of 
these men, but send them plenty of water.’ In a short while, the water erupted 
from the well and wetted everyone around.  
After praying a  thanksgiving prayer, Abba Pieour intended to go in his 
way. They tried to make him have a meal with them, but he said: ‘I have 
accomplished what I came here to do, I did not come here to eat.’”  
This was a good lesson for the brethren about faith and the trust in God.  
 [The Paradise of the Saints, p. 69]

250 
 
master got rid of him. He turned into a gangster who lived on robbing and 
killing people. He had a large, muscular stature, which helped him to become 
the head of an evil gang.  
Having Faith in the Lord Jesus Christ: 
Even though an extreme evil -doer, yet he kept raising up his eyes towards 
the sun, believing that it was the true God, seeking fr om it to proclaim itself 
to him. Then, he heard a voice telling him to go to the wilderness to 
encounter the monks of the Scetis, whose fame was widely spread all over 
the area at that time. He went there, carrying his sword, where he happened 
to meet with  St. Isidore (The Priest of the Cells ) coming out of his cell and 
heading to the church. Terrified by his appearance, the saint asked him: 
“What do you want from here, O brother?” Moses answered: “ I heard that 
you are a good servant of God . Therefore, I es caped and came to you to let 
God save me the way he saved you.” He continued in persistence and with 
submission, saying: “I want to remain with you, despite my countless sins 
and my great evils.” 
St. Isidore kept asking him about his past life and where he  has been. 
Moses confessed to him all the sins he committed. On seeing how he opened 
his heart to him, St. Isidore started to teach him and preached him at length 
the word of God, he told him about the judgment to come and then left him to 
contemplate.  
For hating evil and deciding to rid himself of it, Moses shed so many 
tears, and deep remorse swept his soul and disturbed his sleep, like a dreadful 
ghost. Then, he went to St. Isidore, prostrated himself before him, and in a 
loud voice, he confessed all hi s evil crimes again, with such contrition of 
heart that drew his compassion. He took him to Abba Macarius the Great, 
who put him under his care, taught him and guided him, gave him the grace 
of baptism, then put him back under the supervision of St. Isidore.  
His Monastic Life: 
After a while, Moses sought from Abba Isidore to make him a monk. 
However, Abba Isidore started to explain to him how tough the monastic life 
is with the constant fight against the demons and the other physical needs. He 
told him as a way of testing him: “It is better for you son, to go and live in 
the populated areas,” but after seeing his real intention and solid stand, St. 
Isidore sent him back to Abba Macarius the Great, the father of the 
wilderness.  
Moses stood in the church and  confessed publicly about all his sins and 
evil deeds. Abba Macarius said afterward that he saw during Moses 
confession a whiteboard with black writings, and with every sin Moses

passages.text:
258 
 
Emperor Valens sought to hold a treaty with queen Mavia and her people, the 
queen accepted on one condition, that the Emperor would see to it that the 
Egyptian monk Moses would go to Alexandria to be ordained as a bishop by 
the patriarch there. Although the queen was not yet converted to Christianity, 
she still made that condition to reflect the wish of her people. Emperor Valens 
accepted her situation because of his strong desire to make peace with those 
united tribes.  
Moses Refused to be Ordained by Arian Hands: 
On arriving at Alexandria, Moses found there Lucius the Arian archbishop 
who took over St. Mark's throne by force from the 20 th Pope St. Athanasius 
the Apostolic (328-373). All the other Orthodox bishops were in exile. Then , 
St. Moses stood amid St. Mark Cathedral and said with a loud voice: “Even 
though I am not worthy of the honor of a bishop, yet I consented in response 
to the love of those who chose me and gave me their trust. Yet, I shall never 
accept to be ordained by the hand of one of the deniers of the Divinity of my 
beloved Lord and Savior. If you let me be ordained by an Orthodox bishop, I 
shall accept from his hand this great honor. However, if you do not agree, 
then let me go back to my seclusion in the desert.” 
The Emperor's men tried in vain to make Moses change his mind, and they 
failed in trying to convince queen Mavia to stop her support for the monk 
Moses or to make her people choose somebody else. Finally, they had to take 
the monk to the nearest location o f the exiled Orthodox bishops, where he 
was ordained amid the exultation of the people. The people's joy was mixed 
with admiration of monk Moses, who bravely refused to submit to his tyrant 
opponents and exposed the falseness and helplessness of the Arians.  
Bishop Moses went to the flock that loved him and respected him, 
dedicated his life and effort to serve those who supported him against the 
opponents of Orthodoxy. He kept on moving from one place to another, not 
having a steady residence, teaching, preach ing, and converting multitudes to 
Christianity, and queen Mavia finally accepted the faith. He also managed to 
establish peace between his people and the Romans. Since then, the land of 
Arabia came under the St. Mark umbrella. Finally, St. Moses reposed in  the 
year 372 AD.  
 [The Story of the Coptic Church, Bk 1, p. 347] 
 [Baring-Gould: February 7] 
 
MOTIUS, FR. 
A brother once asked Fr. Motius, saying: “If I abandon the world to dwell 
somewhere else, how would you like me to live?” The elder father answered

251 
 
proclaimed, an angel wiped it out off that board until the board became all -
white. After Abba Macarius instructed him, he sent him back to the priest 
Isidore who clothed him in the monastic attire. He advised him: “Remain, my 
son in this wilderness and never depart from it, because the day you would 
leave it, all evil will come bac k to you. Stay here all your life, and I am sure 
God will do mercy and grace on you and will crush the devil under your 
feet.” 
His Strife: 
St. Moses started by dwelling among the monks. Yet, because of the 
multitudes of visitors, he sought from Abba Macari us to find for him a 
secluded place, and he guided him to a separate cell, where he dwelt 
tirelessly with such tremendous spiritual strife, in an attempt to make up for 
his previous sins and evil deeds. Even though the devil kept reminding him 
of his dark past, but his spiritual guide Abba Isidore counseled him to stand 
firm in opposing the old habits which were planted deep in his soul. He 
mainly complained against the evil carnal desires of Abba Isidore, who kept 
counseling him to stand fast until the dev il would get tired of him. He gave 
him an example of a stray dog that kept standing before the shop of a butcher, 
seeking to get something from him, but when the butcher did not respond to 
it, the dog had to go somewhere else. St. Moses was painfully attacked by the 
thoughts of adultery, so viciously that he could not stay in his cell. So, he 
went to ask help from St. Isidore, who told him to go back to his cell, but he 
refused, saying to the saint: “I cannot endure any more of it. ” Father. Abba 
Isidore too k him up to the roof and asked him: “Look towards the west.” 
There, he saw an uncountable crowd of demons, in great chaos, as though 
preparing for war. He then asked him: “Look towards the east.” There, he 
saw a great number of hosts of glorious saintly an gels, about whom the saint 
said to Moses: “Look, these have been sent by God to help the saints, against 
those in the west. Those who are on our side are far more than those who are 
against us.” Afterward, Moses was encouraged, gave thanks to God, and 
returned to his cell.  
Obeying the counsel of his father of confession, Moses fatigued his body 
by standing a long time in prayers, fasting, and doing metanoias. To 
discipline his body further, he used to go around the cells of the older monks 
at night, take t heir water pots and fill them with water from a well at a far 
distance from the monastery. Getting fed up with his harsh strife, the devils 
caught him once at the well, beat him so violently, and left him unable to 
move, until some brethren happened to com e to the well, and they carried 
him to the church to Abba Isidore. He cared for him for three days until he

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 3, p. 240
passages.text:
240 
 
giving his sister Sarah in marriage and handing their whole wealth to her. 
However, when he discussed the idea with his sister, she responded to him by 
saying: “If you get married first, then I would follow suit.” He told her: “I 
have committed so many sins, which I intend to atone for by leading a 
monastic life, for I cannot get married and care for my salvation at the  same 
time.” She answered him: “How would you cast me in the snares of this 
world, and care only for your salvation?” Then, he answered her: “Whatever 
you choose will be yours.” She responded: “All that you would do, I shall 
also do, for we are of one fath er and one mother.” Then, they distributed all 
their wealth to the poor and the needy. St. Moises brought his sister Sarah 
into a house of virgins, and he joined a monastery near Alexandria, and for 
the following ten years, they did not see one another.  
Their Martyrdom: 
Then, when Emperor Decius (249-251 AD) incited persecution against the 
Christians, in the days of the 14 th Pope St. Dionysius the Great (246 -264 
AD), so many believers were martyred. At that time, St. Moises sent to his 
sister to bid her fa rewell, and let her know of his decision to be martyred in 
the Name of the Lord Jesus Christ. She hastened to her mother -superior, 
sought to be released, got the blessings of her sisters, and joined her brother 
on his way to Alexandria. There, they both co nfessed together the Lord Jesus 
Christ, and after being tortured by many tools, they had their heads cut off by 
the sword, and they received the crowns of martyrdom.  
 [The Synaxarion: 26 Mesra] 
 
MOISES, BISHOP OF OSIM, ST. 
St. Moises (Moses) was one of th e prominent fathers and saints of the 
church in the 8 th century AD. He was raised on the love of virginity and 
purity since his childhood, and he studied the church's various subjects.  
St. Moises became a monk, since his youth in the wilderness of the Sce tis, 
where he lived in the obedience of a great hermit for eighteen years, during 
which he walked along the road of virtue and harsh asceticism. He became 
known for his virtues that he was chosen to be the bishop of Osim (Ouseem), 
in the district of Embaba in the Beĥeira governorate. His life as a bishop was 
an extension of his monastic one in the wilderness. He was living in a life of 
deprivation and was known for his piety, courage, and zeal on the Orthodox 
faith. He used to spend most of his time in wors hip, that it was said that he 
did not see anyone, except on Saturdays and Sundays.

that of his neighbor. 
To die about your neighbor means to worry about your sins and not to 
care for the sins of any man, good or bad. You should not do wrong to 
anyone, or think bad about anyone else in your heart or despise anyone for 
doing wrong. You should not obey anyone who harmed his neighbor or 
rejoice for him. You should never slander anyone, but always say that God 
knows everybody's heart. Do not go along with the man who talks bad 
about his neighbor, because it would  make you fall in condemnation. Do 
not have hatred against anyone. Do not have a grudge in your heart against 
anyone, and do not hate the man who is hostile toward his neighbor. This 
would bring you peace. 
[Sayings of the Strong Saint Abba Moses, Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria-
Diocese of Los Angeles]

MOSES THE HERMIT 
St. Moses, the hermit, was born in Alexandria. Once he reached the age of 
thirteen years, he set forth to the wilderness of the Scetis. There, he dwelt for 
twenty years in a small cell next to one of the older monks. Then, he went 
deep in the wilderness an d lived for thirty -five years in a spot having olive 
and palm trees. There, he ate according to his needs whatever would fall from 
the trees, drank from the rainwater, dressed in palm leaves, and befriended 
the wild beasts.  
His Multiple Falls and Repentances:  
Satan envied this hermit, so he appeared to him in the form of an older 
man. The older man told him that he used to live a corrupt life, but he 
repented and distributed his wealth to the poor. He lived in one of the Five 
Western Cities (Pentapolis) near Cyrenaica (Barqa), and that God revealed to 
him that the hour of his death was approaching. They walked together in the 
wilderness until they reached a grand mansion. Then, the older man told the 
hermit that after his death, that mansion would be his, if he would marry his 
daughter. Moses was deceived and thought that the older man was on the 
brink of extinction, so he accepted his offer. However, once he declared his 
acceptance, he found himself amid the wilderness, hungry and afraid. He 
could not see any mansion there, and he realized that it was a trick from the 
devil. He felt how he was so weak and offered sincere repentance.  
Once St. Moses also went to Alexandria, where the devil appeared to him

MOSES, THE CONFESSOR 
This St. Moses (Moyses) was a Roman priest of Jewish roots. He was one 
of the main members of a congregation of confessors in the time of Cyprian, 
at the start of the heresy of Novat ian.1 The rest of the confessors were: Fr. 
Maximus, the priest, the two deacons Nicostratus and Rufinus, the laymen 
Urbanus, Sidonius, Macarius, and Celerinus. According to Cyprian, they 
were the first group of confessors in the days of the persecution st irred up by 
Emperor Decius (249 -251 AD). At the time of the persecution, they wrote 
down a message to exhort the confessors in Carthage to be committed to the 
system and wrote another message to Cyprian.  
After spending about a year in prison (eleven month s and few days), St. 
Moses reposed in January 251 AD, and was counted as a confessor, and even 
as a martyr. It was said that a little while before his departure, Moses refused 
to have any contact with Novatian or the five priests who were supporting 
him and followed his views. St. Moses was considering their faith and views 
as unorthodox.  
 [A Dictionary of Christian Biography, Vol. III, p. 948] 
 [Baring-Gould: November 25] 
 
MOSES, THE RECLUSE BISHOP , ST. 
The Tribes of Saracens: 
The Arabian tribes populatin g the area of Rhinoclura in -between the 
eastern Egyptian border and the Asian shores, used to worship the stars. Then 
in the year 226 AD, these tribes embraced Christianity through the efforts of 
Origen (184-253 AD). Then, those tribes 2 joined forces toge ther and formed 
one State under the reign of a queen called Mavia. By their unity, they 
created a power block that brought fear to the Arian Emperor Valens (364 -
378 AD) and forced him to seek a peace treaty with them.  
Choosing Moses as a Bishop: 
Those Chr istian tribes having united together, they felt the need for a 
bishop to shepherd them. It happened that in those days, there was a recluse 
monk named Moses in the eastern desert, he was so beloved by those 
tribesmen that they decided to choose him to be t heir bishop. Then, when

was given by the Greeks and the Romans to the nomadic tribes in the ‘Sino-Arabian’ desert…

records.question: Who was St. Bishoy?
records.answer:
St. Bishoy, also known as Abba Bishoy, is a revered figure in the Coptic Orthodox Church, celebrated for his deep spirituality and ascetic life. Born around 320 AD in the village of Shansa, he was one of six brothers raised by a pious mother who dedicated him to God after an angel indicated he was chosen for a special purpose. Despite his frail physical condition, he became a significant monastic figure, embodying the virtues of humility, prayer, and dedication to God [3].

At the age of twenty, St. Bishoy moved to the wilderness of Scetis, where he became a disciple of Abba Bemwah, a follower of St. Macarius the Great. He spent three years in seclusion, focusing on prayer and spiritual growth [3]. His life was marked by intense ascetic practices, including fasting and prayer, which he undertook with great fervor. He was known for his extraordinary ability to endure hardships and his deep love for the Scriptures, particularly the Book of Jeremiah, which he often read with profound reverence [6].

St. Bishoy's relationship with God was characterized by frequent divine encounters. He reportedly had visions of Christ, who assured him of His presence and support in his spiritual endeavors. These experiences reinforced his commitment to monastic life and the care of his fellow monks [6]. He was also known for his humility; when faced with the temptations of the world, he acknowledged the power of God in overcoming such challenges, famously stating that no one could withstand the tricks of Satan without divine assistance [1].

St. Bishoy's legacy includes his role in the early monastic community, where he was instrumental in guiding and nurturing other monks. He reposed in the Lord in 417 AD at the age of 97, and his body remains incorrupt to this day, a testament to his holiness [2][3]. His life and teachings continue to inspire many within the Coptic Orthodox Church and beyond, symbolizing the ideal of a life devoted to God through prayer, humility, and service.

His Love for the Salvation of All Souls: 
Saint ‘Bishoy’ had a disciple named ‘Isaac,’ who descended to the world 
and was seduced by a Jewish woman to forsake his faith, and he was converted 
to Judaism and lived with her . When he happened to encounter some monks, 
he asked them to tell St. ‘Bishoy’: “Your son, the Jewish ‘Isaac,’ has fallen and 
seeks from you to pray on his behalf to God to save him.” On hearing that, the 
woman said: “Even if ‘Bishoy’ come to me, I shall seduce him.” On returning 
to the monastery, the monks forgot what happened. Then, they were asked by 
the saint: “Has someone asked you to tell me something? ” They answered in 
the negative. The saint asked them whether they have encountered the Jewish 
‘Isaac,’ so they told him what happened and what ‘Isaac’ and the Jewish 
woman said. At that moment, they saw the saint retreat three steps backward 
and make the sign of the Cross on himself at each stage. Astonished, the monks 
said; “Even you, father, fear that woman?” St. ‘Bishoy’ humbly answered: “My 
children, the woman was the cause of the fall of ‘Adam,’ ‘Samson,’ ‘David’ 
and ‘Solomon.’ Who would be the poor ‘Bishoy’ to challenge her?!  Nobody 
can overcome the tricks of Satan in wo men, except that one whom God is 
with.” He kept praying and fasting for the sake of his son ‘Isaac’ until God 
saved him, and he came back and repented. 
Forsaking Scetis: 
In the year 407 AD, the first attack of the Berbers on the wilderness of 
‘Scetis’ took place. At that time, the monks escaped from the desert. St. ‘John 
the Short ’ asked St. ‘Bishoy’: “ Do you fear death, O man of God? ” He 
answered him: “No, but I fear a Berberian would kill me and goes to hell 
because of me!” 
St. ‘John the Short ’ went to mount ‘Kalzam,’ near the monastery of Abba 
‘Anthony’ where he reposed . Whereas, St. ‘Bishoy’ went to ‘Ansena’ (the 
village of ‘Sheikh Abbadah’ near ‘Mallawy’), and he lived in the mountain . 
There, he formed a close relationship with ‘St. Abba ‘Paul of Tamouh,’ and 
sought from the Lord not to be separated from him when they would repose , 
and God granted them their wish. 
St. ‘Bishoy’ remained in his expatriation until he reposed on the 8th of Abib 
in the year 417 AD, after reaching 97 years of age. He was buried in the castle 
of ‘Meniat el-Saqar’ near ‘Ansena.’ When St. ‘Paul of Tamouh’ reposed, St. 
‘Athanasius’ of ‘Ansena’ gathered the two saints'  bodies and buried them 
together in the monastery of abba ‘Bishoy’ in ‘Ansena’ (Monastery of El -
Bersha). The bodies of these two saints were returned to the wilderness of 
‘Scetis’ during the patriarchate of the 52nd pope Abba ‘Yusab I’ (831-849 AD).

he regretted it badly and was in bitterness for his disobedience. 
As the monks knew that the saint would see the Lord now and then; they 
sought from him to intercede for them to enjoy seeing Him as well, so the Lord 
promised to appear to them on the mountain at a particular time. The brethren 
greatly rejoiced , and all of them set forth toward the mountain . The saint, 
because of his old age , was at the rear . There, he encountered an old er man 
overcome with weakness and frailty, not able to walk, and none of the passing-
by monks cared to help him. Saint ‘Bishoy’ asked if he may carry him, and he 
did carry him and walked without feeling any labor . However, the older man 
started to get heavier and heavier; and the saint perceived that He was no one 
but the Lord  Jesus Christ Him self. He then looked at Him and said: “The 
heaven is not wide enough to accommodate You, and Your majesty shakes the 
earth; how can a sinner like me carry You? ” To this, the Lord  Jesus Christ 
smiled at him and said: “Because you carried Me, My beloved ‘Bishoy,’ your 
body will never see decay!” Then, He disappeared. St. ‘Bishoy's’ body is still 
kept in his monastery without de terioration up to this very day . Once the 
brethren knew about what happened, they grieved deeply for passing by that 
Old Man and not gaining the blessing of carrying Him. 
An Encounter with St. Ephraim the Syrian: 
By a Divine arrangement,  Mar ‘Ephraim the Syrian ’ came once to meet 
with Abba ‘Bishoy.’ As St. ‘Ephraim’ talked in the Syrian tongue, while St. 
‘Bishoy’ talked in the Cop tic tongue; the later sought from God to give them 
both the ability to understand each other without the need for an interpreter, 
and God granted them that, and they managed to spend a tremendous spiritual 
time together. St. ‘Ephraim’ learned from St. ‘Bishoy’ about the monast ic 
experiences of the Egyptian fathers, particularly of St. ‘Macarius the Great.’  
After a week, St. ‘Ephraim’ left. Then, a brother came to seek St. 
‘Ephraim's’ blessing, but when St ‘Bishoy’ told him that he just left, the brother 
started to run to catch him. St. ‘Bishoy’ called him and said he would never be 
able to because St. ‘Ephraim’ was carried away by a cloud. It was also said that 
St. ‘Ephraim’ has left behind his stick, in front of the cave of St. ‘Bishoy.’

he was talking, he answered: “Emperor Constantine came to visit me and told

 [Nabil Niseem: SS. Bishai and Pasentaos in Mount ‘Tod.’ 1967] 
 
BISHOY, ST. ABBA 
Our great saint abba ‘Bishoy’ represents the simple life striving in the Lord, 
that was founded upon the love fellowship with the Lord Jesus Christ. He had 
a personal relationship with Jesus that broke the obstacles down to open up the 
heart by the Holy Spirit that the Heavenly Groom would transfigure within it 
and reign with power and dominion! 
St. ‘Bishoy’ was born in ‘Shansa,’ a village in the governorate of ‘El-
Menufyia,’ around the year 320 AD. He was one of six brothers, whose father 
reposed when they were relatively young, and their mother raised them  up. 
One day the mother saw an angel who came to tell her: “The Lord says to you: 
‘Give Me one of your children to serve Me all the days of his life. ’” She 
answered: “Sir, they are all for the Lord. Let Him take whomever He chooses.” 
The angel put his hand on this saint, and said: “This is a good laborer for the 
Lord.” Being weakly built and frail in the body, his mother asked the angel to 
choose another one; but he answered her: “The Lord said ‘My strength is made 
perfect in weakness.’” (2 Cor. 12:9). 
In Scetis (Shiheet): 
Having reached twenty years of age in the year 340 AD, the young ‘Bishoy’ 
set forth to the wilderness of ‘Scetis,’ where he became a disci ple of Abba 
‘Bemwah’ (Bemen), the disciple of St. ‘Macarius’ (300-391 AD). There, he 
worshipped in seclusion for three years without going out of his cell. He grew 
in virtue and had his heart inflamed with love for God. 
Life in Seclusion: 
When Abba ‘Bemwah’ reposed in the Lord, his two disciples Abba ‘Bishoy’ 
and Abba ‘John (Yeĥness) the Short,’ spent the whole night praying to seek the 
guidance of God . An angel appeared to them and said that Abba ‘John the 
Short’ should remain alone in that location . In obedience, Abba ‘Bishoy’ left 
the place forsaking his friend, and d ug for h imself a cave near the southern 
rock, about two miles away from Abba ‘John the Short.’ 
His Strife: 
As he loved prayer, he made a hole in a high spot on the cave wall, then he 
fixed a wedge in it and tied one end of a rope around it . Then, he used to tie 
the long hair of his head with the other end of that rope; so that whenever his 
head would get heavy and drop down due to sleepiness, the rope would pull it

passages.text:
356 
 
 
BISHAI OF ANTIOCH, ST. 
(The martyr) 
‘Bishai’ (Abshai) was the brother of St. ‘Hur’ (Abahur) of Antioch. He was 
ordained as a priest because of his piety . His brother and his mother went to 
Alexandria, where they were martyred. Their brother, the priest, went there to 
take care of their bodies . Then, he felt the longing to partake in  their crowns. 
So, he set forth to the governor to proclaim his faith, endured sufferings until 
he died. In vain, the governor attempted to burn their bodies. 
The Church celebrates his feast on the 1st day of the short Coptic month: 
‘Nasie’ (the forgotten days). 
 
BISHAI, THE HERMIT, ABBA 
The biography of Abba ‘Bishai the Hermit ,’ known as Abba ‘Bishai’ the 
dweller of the two graves at the entrance of ‘Tod’ (Mount Tod, east of the Nile 
river opposite to ‘Armant’), was linked to those of SS. ‘Pasantaos’ and ‘Sorus.’ 
The three of them were considered among the first monks who became 
disciples of St. ‘Pachom,’ the father of the ‘Koinonia’ (Coenobite). 
He was a hermit who worshipped God from his early age and labored in his 
prayers day and night . He was also known for his love of the book of the 
prophet ‘Jeremiah;’ so that it was said that every time he read it, he would find 
the prophet ‘Jeremiah’ himself before him, kiss his head, then watch him 
ascending to heaven (which also happened to him when he read the other books 
of the prophets). 
Giving his body no rest, he loved doing metanoias and long watching of the 
nights. After completing his strife, he reposed in the Lord on the 25th of Kiahk. 
His body was buried in his church, from which many signs and wonders 
appeared. 
 
BISHAI, ST. ABBA 
The story of this saint reveals the fantastic plan of God for the salvation of 
every soul; how He uses every tool to draw them to Him, and how He sets 
them on the highest level if they receive His call and respond to it. 
This saint, also (called ‘Peter’), was born in the village of ‘Epsona,’ a suburb 
of ‘Akhmim.’ In his youth, he walked in an evil path; but God did not leave 
him there but allowed for him to fall ill, and in a night vision , He revealed to 
him the place of the eternal sufferings  which he was heading to . He bitterly

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 357
passages.text:
357 
 
wept, and raised his eyes to heaven and cried out: “My Lord and my God! If 
you heal me of this illness; I shall repent, return to You and worship You 
with all my heart .” ‘Bishai’ (Peter) was healed,  and he  did not forget his 
promise to the Lord, but he was inflamed in his heart with an intense longing 
to experience the monastic life. He forsook the sheep he was shepherding, and 
set forth to the monastery where he met with St. ‘Bigol,’ the uncle of St. 
‘Shenouda’ (who was to become the Archimandrite in Mount Adriba). 
His Monastic Life: 
God used the illness to bring that young man out of the covetousness of the 
body, which would destroy the soul . Once he tasted the real spiritual life, his 
heart got filled with so much joy to set forth firmly and be willing to do so 
many labors enduring daily so many harsh sufferings with a joyful heart.  
He lived with St. ‘Bigol’ in a  fantastic friendship, partaking together in 
monasticism and worship without ever getting bored, watching the nights, and 
opposing the temptations of the devil. 
God granted him an exalt ed capability beyond the limits of human 
endurance; he used to fast, in a way that defied imagination, for a whole month 
not tasting anything, and by a fantastic Divine allowance, he would stand the 
entire night praying. God, in His love, granted him to ha ve the deeds of other 
people revealed before his eyes, which he used to support them on the life of 
true repentance. Because of God's grace working in him, many people came to 
him from all over Egypt to seek his blessings . They benefited greatly by his 
spiritual sermons, and he also wrote essays for the monks and those in the 
world. 
Through the friendship of th is saint with St. ‘Bigol,’ he was present when 
the young Abba ‘Shenouda the Archimandrite;’ St. ‘Bigol's’ nephew, first came 
out in the wilderness in  his 7th year of age. He was clothed by his uncle the 
holy monastic Eskeem, in obedience to an angelic proclamation, and the 
presence of St. ‘Bishai.’ The three of them, despite the difference in age, 
worked with one spirit in a fantastic fellowship, realizing the saying of the wise 
‘Solomon’: “A threefold cord is not quickly broken.” (Eccl. 4:12). 
Each of them built for himself a cell on the mountain and another one near 
the church . I t so happened that while th ey were setting forth to visit A bba 
‘Jehnes’ (John) on Mount ‘Assiut,’ they heard a voice from heaven saying: “I 
have chosen you, O ‘Shenouda’ an Archimandrite.” 
St. ‘Bishai’ reposed in the Lord on the 5th of Amshir, and was shrouded by 
St. ‘Shenouda.’ From his body, many signs and wonders appeared, which were 
all documented by Abba ‘Shenouda,’ who wrote his biography and described 
his ascetic life.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 359
passages.text:
359 
 
up, resulting in keeping him awake in prayers. As for fasting, he trained himself 
to fast the whole week and eat only on Saturdays. His prayers and fasting got 
to hand in hand with his intense love for the word of God. He memorized most 
of the Holy Bible by heart. The Book of ‘Jeremiah’ had a special place in his 
heart; that it was said that he used to se e the prophet Jeremiah during his 
reading of his Book; that he was called ‘Bishoy the Jeremian.’ 
He considered hand-work as a significant part of building his spiritual life. 
He believed in the saying : “If anyone will not work, neither shall he eat. ” (2 
Thess. 3:10). His friend Abba ‘John the Short’ said about him that when a rich 
man brought to him plenty of gold as a donation, he told him: “The dwellers 
of the wilderness have no need of gold and should not have any of it. Go instead 
to the villages of Egypt and distribute it to the poor. God bless you.” After the 
man went his way, and the saint returned to his cell, Satan came to him, saying: 
“You fatigued me so much, O Bishoy .” And, the saint answered him: “Since 
your fall, and all your fatigue is in vain.” 
His Fellowship with our Lord Jesus; 
Through his pure heart, he used to meet often with the Lord Jesus Christ on 
a friendship level . He used to see Him, to talk with Him , and to enjoy His 
Divine proclamations. It was said that, having been so persiste nt in his great 
ascetic life and prayers that the Lord Jesus Christ appeared to him, saying: “My 
chosen vessel ‘Bishoy,’ peace be with you; I saw your labor and strife, and 
behold, I shall always be with you!”  
Another time, as our saint remained a long time fasting, the Lord appeared 
to him, saying: “You labored too much, My chosen vessel Bishoy!” The saint 
answered Him: “It was You O Lord who labored for me, but I have not labored 
at all!” 
A third time, the Lord appeared to him, saying: “Rejoice, My chosen vessel 
Bishoy. Do you see this mountain? I shall send you monks to fill that mountain 
to worship Me.” The saint asked Him: “Will You sustain them, Lord, in such a 
barren wilderness?” The Lord answered: “If they love one another and keep 
My commandments, I shall sustain them in everything!” The saint asked Him: 
“Will You save them from all the anguishes and afflictions mentioned in the 
Gospel?” The Lord answered: “Whoever fears, obeys Me and keep My 
commandments; I shall save him from all temptations! ” He then blessed him 
and ascended. 
Again the Lord appeared to him surrounded by angels. The Lord comforted 
him and blessed him . The saint worshipped Him and washed His feet with 
water in a basin, then the Lord ascended . St. ‘Bishoy’ drank from that water 
and left a portion for his disciple . The saint sought from him more than once 
to drink it, but the disciple was too slow. Then, when St. ‘Bishoy’ went to check

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 75
passages.text:
75 
 
around, he decided to leave and returned home. He visited on the way some 
Asian cities, in Syria, Mesopotamia, and Nissibin; and God worked through 
him, wherever he w ent. The saint prepared a tomb for himself, on which he 
engraved the sign of the fish, a symbol of the Christian faith, and wrote a 
concise account of God’s work through him in the imperial palace. He reposed 
in the Lord around the year 167 AD. 
[Butler’s Lives of the Saints; Oct. 22] 
 
 
ABSADI, BISHOP OF EBSAY 
(The martyr) 
The word ‘Absadi’ (Bisada) means “the Humiliated." St. ‘Bisada’ was a 
bishop on ‘Ebsay’ (Monshaa), east of ‘Akhmim.’ 
In the days of emperor ‘Diocletian’ (284-305 AD), ‘Arianius,’ governor of 
‘Ansena’ called him for hearing how he was very vigilant in shepherding his 
people and holding them fast on the Christian faith. 
The bishop called his congregation and advised them to strive. He held a 
Divine Liturgy for them, in which all had the commu nion of the Holy 
Sacraments; then, he bid them farewell and delivered himself to the 
messengers of ‘Arianius.’ At first, ‘Arianius’ treated him decently on account 
of what he saw how awesome the bishop looked. He tenderly asked him to 
obey the orders of the emperor, to spare himself of the ’troubles, but the bishop 
bravely refused to burn incense before the idols. 
Therefore, the saint suffered long by the hinbazeen and by being cast in a 
furnace of fire, where the Lord kept him safe; and he ultimately recei ved the 
crown of martyrdom on the 27th of Kiahk. 
A monastery by the name of St. ‘Bisada’ is still there east of ‘Monshaa.'  
 
ABU AL-HASSAN AL-AMAH 
He was among the 11 th century Copts. He was a secretary of Calipha ‘Al-
Hafez.' He was known for his piety and  his care for reconstructing the 
churches. 
[Iris Habib Al-Masry: The Story of the Coptic Church; V. 3; 1981, p. 144]

146 
 
the Consuls down. The case ended up by punishing and firing the judge and 
the governor, in addition to all those who took part in torturing the saint. 
And to calm the Christians down, the khedive gave the order to hold an 
official funeral for Sidhom Bishai. He also allowed the Cross to be raised in 
public at the front of the saint's funeral procession 1. That display was 
prohibited by the Egyptian rulers for so many centuries. They put the pure 
saint's body in a gasket covered with tin at the expense of the State. His burial 
was celebrated by all sects and was preceded by priests in their priestly attire 
and by deacons carrying banners and crosses. They brought him to the Church, 
where they prayed on him, then buried  his body in a unique tomb on the land 
of the Church, which was originally a cemetery for the Copts. On the night of 
his burial, a shining pillar of light was seen over his tomb and so many people 
took ashes from his tomb for the blessing. 
Finally, the relics of St. Sidhom Bishai were moved to St. George Cathedral 
in Damietta. And, it happened that in the year 1848, they intended to widen the 
church, so they had to move the body of the martyr to a special place on the 
south-west side of the Church, next to that of muåallem Banoub Farag and all 
the rest of his family. There, it remained until the year 1986. The feast of his 
martyrdom was continuously celebrated; until the day the Lord, intending to 
honor His Saint; the committee of the Church decided to move his blessed 
body with a grand celebration into a particular tomb in the court of the Church, 
in the days of the 116th pope Abba Kyrillos VI (1959-1971). One of the toes of 
the right foot of the Saint was placed in a tube in St. Mary Church in Dayrut. 
The Wonders of God through the Saint: 
Many signs appeared from the body of this saint, among which was that a 
rosary which was found in the hand of the saint after moving him, was offered 
to the bishop Abba Aghabius, who carried out the consecration of the blessed 
body. To get its blessing, a brother borrowed it from the bishop, but intending 
in secret to cut a portion of it, St. Sidhom Bishai appeared to him, unknown to 
the man and ordered him to bring it b ack; and so he did, confessed and got 
absolution. 
It happened once that a priest, while sick, came to receive the blessing of 
the martyr, and on leaving, before he reached the door of the Church, he was 
completely healed of his illness. Many other miracles were performed with so 
many visitors of the city and the Church.  
 [The Synaxarion: 17 Baramhat] 
 
1 Later on, this was allowed all over the country during the papacy of the 110th pope Kyrillos IV (1853-
1862), as well as on all the churches and in all the funerals of the Christians…

Abu el-Bishr ibn el-Muqaffaå, the Clerk: 
Sawires ibn el-Muqaffaå ascended the ladder of the State jobs in the era of 
the Ikhshidid dynasty (935-969) who ruled Egypt under the Abbasid Caliphate 
(750-1258), until he became a prominent clerk . He occupied a very high  
position that required a good knowledge of the Arabic language, beside the 
Coptic and the Greek languages. At that time, Sawires was known by the title: 
Abu el -Bishr el -Muqaffaå The Clerk . This did not imply that he had a son 
called El-Bishr, but indicated that he was a prominent and respectable man, as 
it was the custom in those days. 
His Monastic Life: 
After reaching the highest of jobs, Sawires forsook the glory of the world 
and his job, to become a monk in one of Egypt’s monasteries. He managed to 
get much benefit during his monastic life, since he perfected his religious 
education which was based mainly on the Holy Bible and the writings of the 
Fathers. Abu el-Bishr became distinguished in both fields. 
His Knowledge of the Holy Bible: 
According to the researchers, Sawires knowledge of the Holy Bible was 
amazing, so has been his knowledge of the writings of the Fathers; he 
surpassed that of all his contemporaries. This was obvious from his book: “The 
Precious Pearl in Explaining the Religious Doctrine”1 (this is different from 
another book almost with the same title 2), which indicated his extensive 
knowledge of the Holy Scriptures. It could be said that no other author in the 
Arabic language had his knowledge of the Holy Bible; and that his theological 
writings indicated his in-depth knowledge of the works of the Fathers of the 
Church, whether in Greek or Arabic. 
 
Ordained as a Bishop: 
He was chosen as a bishop on the city of El -Ashmonein, which was at the 
time a great bishopric rich in churches and monasteries. Nowadays, it is a small 
village affiliated with the province of El-Roda in the Assiut governorate, to the 
north-west of Mallawy. He was probably ordained by the 59 th Pope of 
Alexandria St. Macarius I (932-952 AD). 
His Debates:

realized when he reposed in peace on the 14th of October 1959.

SIDHOM BISHAI (The martyr) 
On the 17th of Baramhat in the year 1561 AM (25 March 1844), the Coptic 
Church celebrates the martyrdom of St. Sidhom Bishai. 
Sidhom Bishai was a trader of wood in the city of Alexandria. He used to 
go twice every year to Damietta to purchase lumber, which was imported 
through its harbor. Being an archdeacon who loved the old churches, Sidhom 
Bishai on hearing that the wooden roof of St. George el -Muzaĥem Church in 
the town of Basat in the district of Sherbin had collapsed; he took on himself 
the responsibility of repairing the damage done and provide d a full ship load 
of wood for that purpose. At the same time, during his visits to Damietta, he 
used to attend the Holy Liturgies in St. George Church. One time, it happened 
that a non -Christian stroked shoulder against him on his way to the church 
aiming to block him from going to the Church. But, seeing how muåallem 
Sidhom Bishai paid little attention to that evil man, he was provoked to anger 
and paid some street boys to insult him. Then, it happened that the Mofti 1 of 
the town was passing by; and thes e boys falsely accused Sidhom Bishai of 
insulting Islam, its “Prophet” and the “Quran.” Those false accusations, 
finding the expected fertile soil in the Moftis ears; he chose two of equally evil 
people around as witnesses. Through these people, they rigged the case against 
muåallem Sidhom Bishai. He was then 40 years of age, well known for 
meekness, kind-hearted and loving for all, not at all expected to utter what they 
falsely claimed that he has done. 
Torturing Him: 
Then, Sidhom Bishai was called in for trial. And, on his way to the court of 
Justice, he was beaten and insulted by every passerby; until he came before the 
judge. The judge ordered torturing him in every way. The mob kept beating 
him violently, plucking the hair of his head, spitting on his f ace, until he fell 
unconscious. When it happened that he was seen in that condition by a 
prominent Copt in the city, called muåallem Banub Ibrahim Farag; Banub 
moved by zeal for his brother, and he cried out loudly at them, saying: “Is it 
not enough for yo u to beat him, that you drag him over on his face?” When

records.question: Who was St. Anthony, the Father of the Monks?
records.answer:
St. Anthony, known as the Father of the Monks, is a pivotal figure in Christian monasticism and is widely recognized for founding the monastic movement. He was born around 251 AD in the village of Kom Al-Aros in Egypt to wealthy parents. After the death of his father, he experienced a profound spiritual awakening, particularly after hearing the Gospel passage: “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow Me” (Matthew 19:21) [1][2]. This message deeply impacted him, leading him to sell his possessions and dedicate his life to God, while placing his sister in a convent.

St. Anthony initially lived as an anchorite, which means he practiced asceticism in solitude, focusing on prayer and spiritual discipline. He spent time in a small hut and later retreated to the desert, where he faced numerous spiritual battles, including temptations from demons [3][4]. His life of seclusion did not isolate him from the world; he often came down from the desert to support the Church and its members, particularly during times of persecution, such as visiting martyrs in prison [2][7].

He is credited with establishing the principles of monastic life, emphasizing both solitude and community. His teachings and lifestyle inspired many followers, leading to the formation of monastic communities. St. Anthony's influence extended beyond his lifetime, as his teachings were foundational for later monastic leaders, such as St. Pachomius, who developed communal monasticism [2][4].

St. Anthony's legacy is marked by his deep spirituality, commitment to asceticism, and the establishment of a monastic tradition that has endured for centuries. He passed away in 356 AD, and his feast day is celebrated on the 20th of Bashons in the Coptic Church [6]. His life exemplifies the balance between solitude and community, as he sought to live a life dedicated to God while also caring for the spiritual needs of others.

‘Anthony,' among whom are: 
ANTHONY, THE SYRIAN The martyr: 
He was a 20 years old Syrian, a stone builder who was known for his great 
zeal against the idol worshipping. He lived as an anchorite for two years; then 
he returned to his hometown. There, he found the people worshipping the false 
gods. So, he went into their temple and broke all the idols down. He was 
expelled from the city, and he went to ‘Apamaea'. And, when its bishop 
assigned him to build a Ch urch, the pagans were stirred up against him and 
killed him. 
ANTONIUS AL-BEBAWY: The martyr: 
St. ‘Anthony’ (Andona) was born in ‘Beba’ in Upper Egypt by pious and 
merciful parents. Hearing about the sufferings of the martyrs, he set forth to 
‘Arianus,' the governor of ‘Ansena.’ and confessed the Lord Christ before him. 
The governor ordered his men to throw spears at him, but he was not harmed. 
Then, for the fear of that the audience would be encouraged to believe in his 
Christ, he ordered him chained and se nt him to ‘Armanius,’ the governor of 
Alexandria. He sent with him ‘Abimachus’ and two other saints. ‘Armanius’ 
put the three in prison, crucified ‘Anthony’ upside down and tortured him, but 
God was glorified in him. Then, he was sent to the governor of ‘Al-Farma,' 
where he met with ‘St. Mina’ in the prison and both rejoiced by seeing each 
other. The governor of ‘Al-Farma’ ordered combing ‘Anthony’s body with 
sharp iron-teeth combs, and then he cut his head off by the sword. The saint 
received the crown of martyrdom. 
 
ANTHONY, FATHER OF THE MONKS, ST. 
He is considered worldwide as ‘The Father of the Monastic Family ’ and 
‘The Founder of the Monastic Movement ’ in the whole world, even though 
there have been some monastic movements prior to his. 
The saint was born in the village of ‘Komn Al-Aros’ – Beni-Sweif around 
the year 251 AD, to wealthy parents. When his father died, he stood before his 
corpse, contemplated in the mortality of the world, and his heart kindled 
toward eternity. In the year 269 AD, entering into the church, he heard the 
gospel saying: “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have and give to 
the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow Me ” (Matt. 
19:21). Anthony considered it a personal message for him, and it touched  his 
life. Moreover, when he returned home to his young sister ‘Dios,' he 
proclaimed to her his decision to sell his portion of the inheritance and give its 
proceeds to the poor, to dedicate his life to worship God. On her part, his sister 
also insisted on joining a convent in Alexandria.
