old, after leading an angelic life on earth, St. Anthony the Great met him. St. Paul addressed 
him by name, and they talked about the wonders of God and praised Him. At sunset, a raven 
flew down from a palm tree and brought a full loaf of bread to them, even though it was the 
raven’s habit to bring only half a loaf to St. Paul. On the third day, St. Paul asked St. Anthony 
to bring him St. Athanasius’ vestment, which he then gave to St. Anthony to bury him in it. 
When St. Anthony returned, he found that St. Paul had departed while bowing down in 
prayer. Then, two lions came and dug in the sand to bury St. Paul. 
St. Anthony the Great:  He was born around 251 A. D. in the city of Coma, Egypt 
(Qiman El-Arous). When he was eighteen years old, he heard the Gospel reading: “If you 
want to be perfect, go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in 
heaven; and come, follow Me” (Matt. 19:21), and so he sold his possessions, placed his sister 
in a house of virgins, and dwelt in a small hut to learn from a saintly hermit there. After some 
time, he went into the western desert to struggle on his own in a tomb, that was carved in the 
mountain. At the age of thrity -five, he settled at the eastern bank of the Nile at Pispir ( Dayr 
al-Maymūn), where he lived as a hermit, so many came to him and became his disciples. He 
went into the inner desert at Mount Colzim to live in peace and silence. Nonetheless, his love 
compelled him to visit Alexandria to support the martyrs in 316 A. D., and to support St. 
Athanasius against Arianism in 352 A. D. Many people came to be his disciples, and he 
departed in 352 A. D. 
St. Pachomius (Father of the Koinonia):  He was born in upper Egypt around the year 
290 A. D. He became Christian in the city of Esna in Upper Egypt because of their generosity 
and their love for their enemies. He left the army and was baptized around the ye ar 290 A. 
D. He became the disciple of St. Palamon the hermit, till an angel appeared to him and guided 
him to establish the system of the monastic communal life (coenobitic monasticism). He was 
a successful leader who loved the salvation of souls, so he e stablished many monasteries in 
Upper Egypt following strict rules. He also established a convent for nuns under the 
leadership of his sister. His monastic rules were translated to Greek and Latin. St. Basil the 
Great used them, and they were used in the Gaul in the fifth century. They were also adopted 
by Benedict, the father of western monasticism, and by Caesarius of Arles. 
St. Ammonas: He was contemporary of St. Anthony. He was born in 275 A. D., and 
when he was twenty-two years old, his uncle forced him to get married, so he lived with his 
wife as ascetics in Nitria. After eighteen years, his wife asked him to live in solitude away 
from her, so he went out to Mount Nitria and many gathered around him. So, he established 
the semi-eremitic monasticism, in which the monks are not required to have daily fellowship 
in worship or in meals, except for Saturdays and Sundays only. Usually, the monks of this 
order lived in cells or caves that were close to each other, around the church. 
St. Macarius the Great: (around 300–390 A. D.) He is the founder of the semi-eremitic 
order of monasticism in the wilderness of Scetis. He visited St. Anthony at least twice. His 
father forced him to get married, but then God allowed his virgin wife to depart

passages.text:
197 
 
The young man dwelt beside the River Nile and spent all his time praying 
in strict asceticism. Yet, when thoughts of boredom attacked him, he cried out 
to the Lord to guide him. An angel of the Lord appeared to him in the form of 
a man wearing a long robe, with leather cross-like Eskeem and a cover on his 
head. He sat weaving palm leaves for some time, got up to pray, then returned 
to work, and so on. The angel said to Anthony: “If you do so, you will never 
get bored." That  came to be the attire of the monks, and the work of hand 
happened to be one of the basics of the monastic life. 
One day, a woman and her maidservants came down to the river to wash 
their feet. Turning his head away, waiting for their departure, they start ed to 
undress to bathe. When the saint admonished her on such a behavior, she 
answered him: “If you are a monk, you should dwell in the inner wilderness, 
for this is not a place befitting for monks." On hearing these words, the saint 
said to himself, “This is the voice of the angel of the Lord rebuking me." He 
instantly forsook the location and set forth to the inner wilderness. That was 
around the year 285 AD. The saint dwelt in a cave on Mount ‘Al-Kalzam’ to 
practice the life of seclusion, North-West of the Red Sea. However, in that new 
location, the demons kept fighting against him, sometimes in the form of 
women and other times in the way of horrible wild beasts. 
His Order of Seclusion: 
In about the year 305 AD, he had to break his seclusion to meet with  some 
beginners who came to him longing to be trained under his supervision. He 
helped and guided them, then resumed his life of seclusion later on. Thus he 
was the founder of the movement of monasticism, his life revealed the concept 
of the Christian monasticism, particularly the order of seclusion: 
4- St. Anthony came out to be a monk without any intention to become a 
member of the clergy. His movement was a civic one, not a clerical one; he 
did not want to interfere with the ecclesiastical structure. Even, when 
Emperor Constantine I sent to him seeking his blessing, he delayed his 
response to the message, and when asked by his disciples why he did so, he 
said, “I am preoccupied to respond to the message of God, the King of 
kings." However, when he was pressu red, he answered the emperor’s 
message, for the sake of the Church peace. 
5- His intense love of seclusion did not close his heart toward the holy 
congregation, but, in his seclusion, he believed in being a member of the 
Church. That is why he eventually came  down to help Pope Athanasius 
the Apostolic (who was once one of his disciples). Moreover, on his 
entrance into Alexandria, the whole city was shaken, and its inhabitants 
came out exultant to welcome the man of God; that even some Arians 
came back to the Church.

up, approached the saintly hermit, kissed him , and greeted both the king and 
the queen. After that, all stood with submissive and a contrite heart to pray and 
worship. Then, the monk came to give each of them what was needed for their 
hand-work. They worked in silence while singing praise until the ninth hour, 
when a servant brought food to them, which they ate after giving thanks to 
God. The hermit came to know that the king and the queen ate only once daily 
at sunset; watch the night praying  until midnight and live together  with a life 
of virginity. After having dinner with them, the saint bid them farewell, and the 
king, the queen, and the monk did not let him go until they had his blessings . 
St. Yusab returned to Scetis (el-Esqeet), beating his chest.  
And, he lived rejoicing until he reposed in peace. 
 [The Hermit Fathers, p. 25]  
 
YUSTUS ST. ANTHONY, THE MONK 
The monk Yustus (Justus) St. Anthony was born in the village called Zarabi 
near the M uĥarraq monastery in the province of Assiut in the year 1910 . He 
was given the name Naguib. He worked with his father as a tailor , and he 
learned and mastered the Coptic language . He was ordained as a deacon . 
Naguib went to the monastery of St. Paul in the Eastern desert. There, he spent 
two years as a novice. Then, he moved to the monastery of St. Anthony, where 
he was ordained as a monk in November 1941. 
He was always Expecting the Coming of his Master: 
From the very beginning, in his spiritual strife , he rarely closed his eyes . 
Still, he stayed all night wandering around inside the monastery, as though he 
was anticipating the coming of his Lord. And, whenever he needed some rest, 
he would sit underneath a tree for a short nap. In his early stages of strife, he 
used to lie down on the stem of a fallen tree on the ground, to keep himself 
from a comfortable sleeping, and to remain awake for praying all night long. 
Whenever he met with someone, he would ask him: “ What is the time 
now?” as though anticipating the time of his departure. At the beginning of his 
monastic life, he was fighting against evil thoughts. He was able to overcome 
them by staying awake and reciting the Lord’s Prayer in a loud voice, on and 
on, until they would go away. 
Concerning the Holy Bible, he memorized the Psalms and the epistles of 
Paul the Apostle by heart. And, he loved to read the Holy Bible in the Coptic 
language. Concerning his food, he used to eat just a little amount, mainly from 
the bread crumbles, which would fall off the main dinner table, after he would 
soak them in the water while he would give the rest of his food portion to the 
workers and the stray cats . Monk Yustus always lived poor. He never carried

of St. Paul, and shook their heads as if they were asking St . Anthony what to 
do. St. Antony knew that they were sent from God. He marked the place on 
the ground and they dug the grave with their claws ; according to St. Antony's 
directions. St. Anthony then buried the holy body. 
St. Anthony carried the garment of palm t ree fibers and presented it to 
Pope Athanasius who gr eatly exulted to have it, and kept wearing it every 
year in the feasts of Christmas, Theophany , and Resurrection . Many signs 
were shown by that garment. 
In the location where St . Paul the First Hermit used to live, a monastery 
was built where earthly angels dedicated all their lives to that of joyful praise 
for the Lord. 
 
PAUL, THE MONK 
About Abba Ur (Hur), we know that he had a disciple by the name of Paul 
(Boulus) who cared much for the life of prayers, even though he 
misunderstood its meaning . He considered his prayers as a race to recite the 
greatest number of church praises. H e was eventually corrected by St . 
Macarius.  
About him it was said: 
He did not approach the hard handworks or the assignments of selling and 
buying; except for the littl e things he eats every day . However, he was very 
advanced in one thing, which was praying without ceasing. He set for himself 
a rule; to pray 300 prayers every day. He used to put some little pebbles in his 
pocket, and then he used to hold in his hand one of them for every prayer he 
prayed. One day, he came to St . Macarius, saying: “Father, I am very sad .” 
When the elder monk asked him the reason for his anguish, he answered: “I 
heard about a virgin who spent thirty years of her monastic life, reciting 500 
prayers every day . On hearing that, I despised myself, for I am not able to 
pray more than 300 prayers every day.” 
Here, St. Abba Macarius told him: “I lived for sixty years in the monastic 
life, reciting only fifty prayers every day; work ed for  what was e nough to 
earn my need of food; and receive d the brethren who come to seek my 
counsel. Now, here you are who pray 300 prayers every day, condemned by 
your thoughts. You probably, either do not pray them with purity; or you can 
do more of other things and you do not want to.” 
 [The Diocese of Beni-Suef: The Garden of Monks; pp. 24-25] 
 [Budge: The Paradise, vol. 2, art. 356]

162 
 
According to St. Athanasius, while Abba Anthony was sitting one day by 
his monastery, he saw somebody ascending to heaven, and a multitude of saints 
was welcoming him. Inquiring about him, he was told that he was Abba Amon. 
Thirty days later, some hermits came over from Mount Nitria, to inform St 
Anthony that their father has departed to heaven. 
The C optic Church celebrates his feast on the 20 th of Bashons; and the 
Greek Church on the 4th of October. 
 
 
 
 
AMON, THE RYTHIAN, FR. 
He was called that way because he lived in the region of ‘Rythio’ by the city 
of ‘El-Tur’ in Sinai. He was an Egyptian monk who lived as an anchorite in the 
region of ‘Kanub’ (Abu Quir) at the beginning of the fourth century AD. When 
the persecution was stirred up by Emperor ‘Valens’ (364-378 AD), he was 
exiled to Palestine, and from there, he returned to the wilderness of Sinai. He 
witnessed by himself the invasion of the pagan Arabs on the monasteries of 
Sinai when they destroyed the monasteries and dispersed their monks. At that 
time, Amon set forth to ‘Rythio,' which became the center of a gathering of the 
monks of Sinai. He li ved there for a long time until Rythio ’ was invaded as 
well. And, he then left it and set forth to ‘Manf,' then to Scetis to live among 
its hermits as a disciple to Abba Bemen. When he once asked Abba Bemen 
about the evil thoughts; his answer was: “It is within the power of the enemy 
to bring them to our minds, but it is within our power not to accept them!” 
 
AMON, ABBA 
This saint was the disciple of Abba ‘Poemen’ (Bemoa). He came once to 
visit Abba ‘Sisoes’ (Shishoy) in wintertime. And he noticed that Abba  Sisoes 
was very sad and depressed after he left the life of seclusion in the wilderness, 
so he said to him: “Why are you so sad, O father? How could you have 
managed to live alone in the wilderness at your advanced age? ” The old man 
looked at him with admonishment and said: “What are you saying Amon?! Is 
feeling freedom in the desert not better than anything else?!” 
 
AMON, THE BISHOP OF HERMOPOLIS

6- Another time, he came down to Alexandria to support the confessors in 
prison and accompany them to the arena of martyrdom. 
7- With his great love of seclusion, he took St. Macarius the Great, who 
founded the system of congregations; as one of his disc iples and greatly 
rejoiced to hear the news of St. Pachomius, the founder of the order of 
fellowship and commended him for it. He carried no prejudice to any 
particular order. 
8- His seclusion did not have a feeling of boredom; for all were amazed to 
see his outer cheerfulness and inner exultation. He enjoyed good health 
until the day he reposed, having reached 105 years of age. 
9- Even though he was illiterate and did not know how to read or write, yet 
he could overcome the Greek philosophers by his pure heart, and also 
drew some of them to faith. Moreover, when he was asked how he could 
find comfort in the middle of the mountains without having a book, he 
answered that God comforted him through the mind, which preceded the 
written text. 
When he was asked about the meaning of a verse that came in the Book 
of the Hebrews, he raised his eyes toward the wilderness, and then cried out 
seeking from God to send the prophet Moses to interpret its meaning to him. 
Instantly, a voice was heard talking to him; and according to Abba 
Ammonius, they also heard the voice, though did not comprehend it. 
Of His Words: 
 Our life and death are with our neighbor. If we gain our neighbor, we have 
gained God; and if we offend him, we sinned against Christ. 
 Some have burdened their bodies with asceticism; but because of the lack 
of discernment, they stayed away from God. 
 There will come a time when men are so inflicted with craziness, that if 
they see someone prudent, they attack him, saying: You are crazy; you are 
not like us. 
 Obedience and forsaking worldly pleasures grant men the authority over 
the beasts of the wilderness. 
The Church celebrates his departure on the 22nd of Toba. 
 [The Biography of Abba Anthony by Abba Athanasius the Apostolic -- Translated 
by Hegumen Marcos Daoud]

(The martyrs)

161 
 
at the ninth hour and would reach it before sunset. Shortly after, those pious 
monks started to build cells there, and the region was called ‘the cells’ zone. 
His Personality and the Role of Nitria; 
Abba Amon did not achieve such exalted fame like that of St. Anthony or 
St. Macarius, who started after him, because of his personality. He was 
characterized with great humility and shyness and had a tendency to fly away 
from the crowd and refrained from performing a ny miracles, claiming that he 
was not given that gift. However, that does not lessen in any way the high value 
of his vital role in developing the monastic movement. He was its founder in 
that region, and so many of his disciples became great fathers. The closeness 
of ‘Nitria’ zone to the inhabited area, along with the fame of its fathers, caused 
so many problems for the church. The Arians and the Chalcedonians attempted 
to impose their authority on the church through the submission of those fathers. 
Hence, after those two zones (Nitria & the Cells) have flourished, a counter 
migration movement of monks started from it right after the repose of Abba 
Amon. 
St. Palladius visited the region of Nitria, about a half a century after the 
repose of Abba Amon, where he estimated the number of the monks to be 5000, 
among whom there were 600 recluses; all practicing handiwork. And, he also 
found there a considerable church and next to it a house of retreat for the 
guests, with eight priests to minister in the church.  
His Miracles: 
Some farmers once came to Abba Amon, carrying a little child mauled by a 
dog and suffering severe pain. The saint asked them: “Why should you come 
to me to do something beyond my worthiness, when, in your hands, you have 
the healing medicine f or this child?! Now, give the stolen cow back to its 
widow owner, and the child will be healed." Having perceived that the saint 
revealed their hidden sin, they presented repentance and gave the cow back to 
its owner. The saint then prayed for the child, and the Lord healed him. 
St. Athanasius told that story about St. Amon: He was once with his disciple 
‘Tadros,’ and they needed to cross a river. Known for his great shyness, he 
sought from his disciple to go away from him, for each of them to take his 
clothes off and swim. Despite doing that, Abba Amon was too shy to take his 
clothes off, even in the absence of his disciple. In the middle of his confusion, 
he found himself all of a sudden on the other shore of the river. When his 
disciple saw him there with  his dry clothes, he was persistence to know how 
he crossed over. The saint told him, seeking from him not to tell it to anyone 
before his repose. 
His repose:

two brothers; Paul decided to take the matter to court . However, on his way 
to court, he encountered a very wealthy man's funeral procession, happened 
to be passing by . St. Paul asked himself: “Has t hat rich man taken anything 
from this world with him?” Then, he had a complete change of heart and he 
totally despised the temporal life . His heart was so i nflamed with the Eternal 
inheritance, that instead of going to the court, he got out of the city and  
entered into a deserted tomb where he spent three days praying and seeking 
the Divine guidance. 
Then, an angel appeared to St . Paul and guided him to the wilderness in 
the East Desert, where he dwelt in mount Nimra, near the Red Sea . There he 
lived for eighty years. During all these years he saw no one, clothed himself 
in a tunic made of palm tree leaves and God sustained him with a daily ration 
of half a loaf of bread, which was carried to him by a raven . The saint lived 
all that time on that bread with s ome dates from the palm trees or herbs from 
the mountain, and he drank water from a nearby spring. 
An Encounter with Abba Anthony: 
One time, St. Anthony the Great was thinking that he was the first man to 
dwell in that wilderness . Then, an  angel of the Lor d appeared to Abba  
Anthony and told him about the presence of a very special man, whom the 
world was unworthy of his footsteps; and for the sake of his prayers , God has 
lifted the drought from the world and has granted it plenty of rain. 
On hearing that Heavenly testimony, St . Anthony set forth  with Divine 
guidance, to the cave of St . Paul. When he got there, St . Paul called him by 
his name and they sat together talking about the great works of God in their 
lives. At sunset, the raven came as usual  but carrying a whole loaf of bread . 
St. Paul then said: “Now I know for sure that you are a man of God; for all 
along eighty years the raven kept providing me with only half a loaf of bread, 
but today it came with a whole loaf. God sent you your food.” 
At the end of their talk, Abba Paul sought from Abba Anthony to hasten to 
bring him the priestly garment of the 20th Pope of Alexandria, St. Athanasius 
the Apostolic (328-373 AD); for his departure time was approaching . Abba 
Anthony returned greatly affected, brought the garment , and headed back to 
St. Paul's cave. On his way, he saw a group of angels carrying his s oul to 
Paradise, while joyfully singing praise to God. 
On reaching the cave of Abba Paul, Abba Anthony found him kneeling . 
For a moment, he assumed that he was praying, so he waited for him to 
finish. Finally, he realized that he has reposed in the Lord and he intensely 
mourned him. This happened on the 2nd of Amshir in the year 343 AD.  
When St. Antony wanted to bury St . Paul, he wondered how he could dig 
the grave, then two lions entered the cave, bowed their heads before the body

151 
 
This saint was born in the year 294 AD near Marriott; and like his colleague 
‘Anthony,' he was of a wealthy pious family. He lost his parents while still in 
his youth and became under the guardianship  of his uncle. He desired to live 
as a virgin; his uncle betrothed for him a rich girl against his will. Not able to 
disobey his uncle ’s wish, he kept talking to his betrothed girl with spiritual 
conviction and through his holy behavior, he managed to have a good impact 
on her and made her love purity and planted in her heart the desire to dedicate 
her soul to be a bride for the real Groom Jesus Christ. The couple agreed to go 
along with the wedding plan, yet persisted on living together like brother and 
sister. They remained for 17 years, strict ly keeping their virginity. After that 
period, the wife departed to the eternal kingdom. In a night vision, the saint 
saw Abba Anthony calling him to put on the monastic ‘Eskeem.' Waking up, 
he went to St. Isidore who put on him the holy Eskeem. He stayed with him 
for some time; then, he set forth to Mount Tuna, where St. Anthony was 
dwelling. He lived a period with St. Anthony and became his disciple. He 
learned from him the holy monastic rules, then the saint built for him a cave in 
Mount Tuna and strove there in so many ways.  
The devil envied him and came to him in the form of a nun knocking at his 
door. When he opened the door and sought her to pray, the devil turned into a 
flame of fire and went away. Then, the devil seduced a loose woman to try to 
make the saint fall in sin. So, she put on her best attire and came at sunset and 
knocked on the saint’s door, saying: “I am a stranger traveler, who lost my way. 
It is now close to night time. Do not leave me outside, lest a beast may devour 
me, and you shall be responsible for my blood." The saint opened the door for 
her and recognized the trick of the devil who sent her, so he began to preach 
her from the Bible, to warn her about the suffering in hell prepared for the 
sinners and told her about the happines s prepared for the righteous. God 
opened up her heart; she understood his sayings and threw herself at his feet, 
weeping and supplicating to him to help her save her soul. He made her discard 
her luxurious clothes, had her head shaved, clothed her in a woo len garment 
and called her ‘The Naïve.' He taught her the way of virtues, and she followed 
it very well. She surpassed some saints by her fasting and persistent prayers. 
When the devil kept failing in his attempts to trip up the saint, he tried 
another trick. He took the form of an elderly monk, and he went from one 
monastery to another, claiming while pretending to be weeping that Abba 
Ammonius the hermit has gotten married to a woman, whom he kept in his 
cave. And, the devil proclaimed that by so doing, he had brought a disgrace on 
the monks and a reproach to the holy ‘Eskeem.' On hearing that, the angel-like 
Abba Apollo took with him Abba Yousab and Abba ‘Nuhi’ and set forth to the 
cave of Abba Ammonius in Mount Tuna, to investigate the matter. They

records.question: Who was Pope Cyril I of Alexandria?
records.answer:
Pope Cyril I of Alexandria, also known as "Cyril the Great" and "Cyril the Pillar of Faith," was the 24th Pope of Alexandria, serving from 412 to 444 AD. He is a significant figure in the history of the Coptic Orthodox Church and is best known for his role in the Christological debates of the early Church, particularly during the Second Ecumenical Council held in Ephesus in 431 AD. This council was crucial in defining the Orthodox understanding of the nature of Christ, where Cyril's theological insights were instrumental in condemning the teachings of Nestorius, who proposed that Mary should be called "Christotokos" (Mother of Christ) rather than "Theotokos" (Mother of God) [6][9].

Cyril was born in Jerusalem around 315 AD and received a thorough education in both classical and theological studies, which was typical for someone from a prominent background in that era. He was ordained as a deacon and later as a priest, gaining a reputation for his knowledge and eloquence in preaching [6][9]. His papacy began during a time of relative peace, but he faced significant challenges, including conflicts with the Jewish community in Alexandria and the ongoing theological disputes with the followers of Nestorius.

Cyril's leadership was marked by a strong defense of the Orthodox faith, and he was known for his courage and steadfastness in the truth. He actively worked to consolidate the authority of the Church and was involved in various ecclesiastical and political matters of his time. His theological legacy is profound, as he contributed significantly to the development of Christology, which is the study of the nature and work of Jesus Christ [5][6][9]. Cyril I reposed in peace in 444 AD, leaving behind a lasting impact on the Church and its teachings.

CYRIL II, The 67th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA 
Pope of Alexandria (1078-1092 AD): 
After the bishops, the clergy and the archons discussed the election of the 
pope in the monastery of St. ‘Macarius’ for two months without coming to a 
decision, they moved to a neighboring monastery ‘Yuannis Kama,’ where they 
selected a saintly elder monk by the  name of ‘Bisus.’ However, he protested 
that he was a common man unfit for that dignity and began banging his chest 
with a stone. He told them that the one who was worthy of this honor would 
be the monk ‘George’ (Gawargius) of the monastery of St. ‘Macarius,’ and that 
he was recommended by the reposed 66th Pope abba ‘Christodolus’ (1046-1077 
AD). So the delegation moved back to the monastery of St. ‘Macarius,’ and 
they found ‘George,’ a middle-aged monk of great sanctity, from ‘Qalaqa’ in 
‘Beĥeira.’ They settled on him as their candidate. They took him against his 
will, clothed him with the patriarchal garb, then they took him to Alexandria, 
where he was formally ordained by the name ‘Cyril II’ in the year 1078 AD. 
He was known as ‘The Sengarian,’ about the cell in which he dwelt as a hermit, 
known by the name ‘Sengara.’ 
He was ordained in the days of the Fatimid Caliph ‘Al-Mustansir’ (1029-
1094 AD), by a decree of a Council of the bish ops and Archons held in 
Alexandria; and all the departments of the government well welcomed his 
ordination. 
The new pope visited the Caliph ‘Al-Mustansir’ in his palace in Cairo, 
where he was greatly welcomed, and the caliph asked him to bless his mother, 
his sister, and the whole palace. The pope also visited the house of his vizier 
‘Badr el-Din Al-Gamali,’ who issued a special decree for his administration to 
execute all the patriarchal wishes.  
This pope sat on St. Mark's throne, while Egypt enjoyed comp lete peace, 
thanks to the rule of vizier ‘Badr el-Din Al-Gamali,’ the Armenian minister, 
during whose time Egypt enjoyed progress and prosperity. The position of the 
church thus became secure, after the hardships it had sustained under Fatimid 
caliph ‘Al-Ĥakim bi-Amr Allah’ (996-1021 AD). 
His Knowledge and Piety: 
Pope ‘Cyril II,’ has been of little education when he was chosen, did what 
the 12th pope ‘Demetrius’ the Vinedresser (188-230 AD) do. And he acquired 
so much learning on his own and was able to leave us a great heritage, which 
testifies to the depth of his knowledge. of God’s grace on him was that, when 
he consecrated the Holy Myron, it flo oded over from the vessel during the 
prayers.

and there he exhorted the Coptic priests to draw the children to the Coptic 
Orthodox schools; and to defend the Upright Faith. All that becau se of the

the arrival of American preachers in Egypt in the year 1854, they started to

Two Trips to Sudan: 
In March 1904, His Holiness traveled to Sudan to be received there by the 
statesmen, the Muslim sheikhs and the Coptic congregation with honor and 
reverence. He laid the cornerstone for the Coptic Cathedral in ‘Khartoum,’ in 
the presence of the British governor of Sudan; the commander of the Egyptian 
army; Abba ‘Yoannes’ the metropolitan of ‘Beheira and Menoufia; ’ Abba 
‘Marcus’ the metropolitan of ‘Esna and Luxor ’ and Abba ‘Pachomius’ the 
bishop of the monastery ‘El-Moĥarraq.’ 
In the year 1909, the pope visited Upper Egypt and went back to Sudan, 
where he consecrated the church in ‘Khartoum’ and laid the cornerstone of a 
tremendous Coptic school there. 
Pope ‘Cyril V’ was a contemporary of the khedives ‘Ismaåil Pasha’ (1867-
1879), ‘ Tewfik Pasha ’ ( 1879-1892), ‘ Abbas Pasha II ’ ( 1892-1914), sultan 
‘Hussein Kamel ’ ( 1914-1917) and sultan/king ‘Fouad’ ( 1917-1936). His 
Papacy lasted for about 53 years, longer than any of the previous  popes. He 
reposed in peace in the year 1927. 
 [Patriotism of the Coptic Church and its History, p. 384] 
 [The Coptic Encyclopedia: Cyril V, by Mounir Shoucri; p. 679] 
 
CYRIL VI, The 116th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA 
The amount of material which has been written ab out this saintly pope in 
several languages after his departure was vastly more than what was written 
about him during his life. Many people in Egypt, Sudan, Ethiopia, Lebanon, 
and Syria got to know him as a man of God, a man of prayer who has the gift 
of performing signs and miracles. 
After the repose of the 115 th pope ‘Yusab II’ (1946-1956) on the 13th of 
November 1956, St. Mark's throne remained vacant until the 10th of May 1959; 
the day this pope was ordained. In that transition period, prayers, fasting,  and 
counsels continued, seeking from the Lord to give His church a good shepherd. 
The election was held and of the three who had the highest votes, Hegumen 
‘Mina the Recluse’ won. On Sunday the 10th of May, he was ordained, and was 
called ‘Cyril VI.’ Even though all expected him to be called ‘Mina,’ yet the 
new pope, having seen pope ‘Cyril V’ in a night vision, sought to be called by

Moreover, it is for all to admire the churches, the sanctuaries and the altars, 
and to forbid the laymen from entering into the sanctuaries. 
 
One of the pope’s bishops by the name of Abba ‘Marcus’ took upon himself 
to organize the church readings during the services of the Passion Week, and

Pope ‘Cyril II’ sent bishops to consecrate the Church of the Resurrection in 
Jerusalem when it was reconstructed after being burnt in the days of the caliph

Pope Cyril II reposed in peace on the 12th of Paona 808 AM (July 1092).

CYRIL III, The 75th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA 
The controversy around his Ordination: 
The 74 th pope ‘John VI ’ (Yoannes: 1189-1216 AD) happened to repose 
while grieving for the conversion of the Five Western Cities (Pentapolis) 
inhabitants in Libya away from Christianity, even though he ordained a bishop 
for them. Before this pope ’s departure, he prophesied that tribulations were 
going to dwell on the land and the people until the Lord would send someone 
to them from somewhere they do not know. Indeed, that happened after the 
papal throne remained vacant for about 20 years. 
During the papacy of the pope, ‘John VI,’ the throne of the metropolitan of 
Ethiopia became vacant, and a delegate came to the pope to seek the ordination 
of a new metropolitan. Somebody by the name of ‘Abu el-Fetouĥ,’ also known 
by the title (Ibn al -Miqat), was the Coptic chief scribe of the Ayyubid sultan 
‘Al-Ăadel’ (1200-1218 AD) and was well connected with the administration. 
This ‘Abu el-Fetouĥ’ sought to appoint a close friend of his, a priest by the 
name of ‘Dawud, (David),’ known by the title of ‘ibn Loqloq’ from the city of 
‘Fayyum’ to that metropolitan position. So, ‘Abu el-Fetouĥ’ hastened to go to 
the sultan ‘Al-Ăadel’ carrying precious gifts, to seek from him to put pressure 
on the patriarch to ordain ‘Dawud’ as a metr opolitan in Ethiopia. However, 
pope ‘John VI’ refused, declaring that he was not the right man for the post. 
Although, ‘Dawud’ was knowledgeable in religion, yet the pope was content 
neither with him nor with his associate ‘Abu el-Fetouĥ.’ 
Once pope ‘John VI’ reposed, ‘Abu el -Fetouĥ’ sought again to have

 His body became a trap for death. That when the beast was hoping to 
swallow Him; instead he brought forth from his belly those he has a lready 
swallowed. Since death if strengthened would swallow us; God wipes out 
the tear from every eye1 (Rev. 7:17). 
 Do not marvel that the whole world could be saved; for He is not just a man, 
but the Only-begotten Son of God, who died for the world's sake. 
 Indeed, by the sin of one person (Adam), death reigned upon the world. So, 
if by the guilt of one death ruled the world, how much more Life would 
reign by the righteousness of One?! 
 If they were driven out of Paradise because of the tree they ate its fru it; 
would it not be easier for the believers to enter into Paradise because of the 
tree (Cross) of Jesus?! 
 If the first man, who was made of earth, brought death to the earth; would 
it not rather be easier for his Creator to bring him eternal life since He , 
Himself, is the Life?! 
 If ‘Phinehas,’ in his zeal made the plague stop among the children of Israel 
(Numbers 25:6-12); how much more would be Jesus, who killed no one, but 
“delivered Himself as a ransom” to take the wrath of God the Father, away 
from a man?!2 
 
CYRIL I, The 24th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA 
This pope was given the title “Cyril the Great” and also “Cyril the Pillar of 
Faith.” Pope ‘Cyril I’ (Kyrillos) name is forever linked to the second great 
conflict about the theologies concerning the identity of the Lord Jesus Christ 
(Christology3). St. ‘Cyril’ led the 2nd Ecumenical Council in Ephesus in the 
year 431 AD, which condemned ‘Nestor,’ the patriarch of Constantinople. 
‘Cyril’ is reckoned as one of the outstanding fathers and theologians of the 
Church. The patristic understanding of the Incarnation owes more to St. ‘Cyril 
of Alexandria’ than to any other individual theologian4. 
His Upbringing: 
Not much is known about his early life. His pious and wealthy grandparents 
lived in the town of ‘Memphis’ which was called ‘Arcadia’ (nowadays ‘Mit 
Rahena,’ south of Giza). On the death of his grandparents, an Ethiopian

Christology is the part of theology that is concerned with the nature and work of Jesus, including such 
matters as the Incarnation, the Resurrection and His Human and Divine natures and their relationship…

nursemaid who was heathen but heartily loved Christianity took care of their 
two children ‘Theophilus’ (Cyril's uncle) and his younger sister (Cyril 's 
mother).  
Once, the nanny took the two children along with her to visit the temple of 
‘Artimus and Apollon. ’ On their arrival, many idols crashed down for no 
apparent reason, and the nursemaid became so afraid. She fled to Alexandria 
with the kids, wher e she met with the 20 th Pope St. ‘Athanasius.’ She was 
surprised when the pope told her about what happened to her in the temple, 
and she proclaimed her faith in the Lord Jesus Christ and got baptized, along 
with the two children. 
‘Theophilus’ was eventually ordained as the 23rd Pope of Alexandria (385-
412 AD), and his younger sister was placed in a house of virgins until she got 
married to a pious man from ‘Mahalet el-Burg’ (Didoyscya), north of the city 
‘El-Mahalla el-Kubra.’ 
Born between the years 375 and 380 AD, ‘Cyril’ got a great deal of learning 
in both the classical and theological knowledge, at the time when Alexandria 
was a great educational center. This in addition to what he was taught by his 
own uncle Pope ‘Theophilus.’ He was raised knowledgeab le in the religious 
books, the Holy Bible, the sayings, and biographies of the fathers. He had, as 
well, the talent of memorizing the Church hymns by heart and singing them 
with his steady voice. 
His uncle made him join the Theological School of Alexandria to study the 
philosophical sciences, which would help him in defending Christianity 
against the heretics and the innovators.  
In the Wilderness of Scetis: 
His uncle sent him, as well, to Abu -Maqar Monastery in the wilderness of 
the Nitrian Valley to becom e a disciple to Abba ‘Serapion,’ who was the 
disciple of abba ‘Maqar the Great, ’ to teach him all the ascetic and 
ecclesiastical knowledge. During the five years that he spent with his mentor 
in the Nitrian Valley, he managed to absorb all the books of the  Church, and 
God granted him the amazing grace of understanding, that by reading a book 
only once, he would be able to memorize it by heart. 
Ordained as a Deacon, then as a Priest: 
After all those studies, ‘Cyril’ returned to Alexandria, to his uncle, who 
commended his great early prominence and ordained him as a deacon. It so 
happened that whenever he started to sing the Holy Gospel in the church, with 
his incredible sweet voice, the believers wished that he would never stop. 
Despite his young age, his unc le the pope ordained him as a priest and 
entrusted him to give the sermons, and ‘Cyril’ earned the admiration of the

did show their consent to ‘Dawud’s ordination out of fear of ‘Abu el-Fetouĥ.’ 
So, ‘Dawud’s ordination was halted. During the following 20 years, which 
the papal throne remained vacant, several of the bishops who opposed the 
ordination passed away. During those long years, however, both ‘Abu el -
Fetouĥ’ and ‘Dawud’ were able to manipulate the church congregation and the 
authorities to emerge as winners in the battle of gaining St. Mark’s throne.  
Since the sultan ‘Al-Kamel’ was in urgent  need for funds to meet the 
expenses of war and repair the harm done to the economy of the land, so he 
ordered his statesmen to bring the Copts to support the ordination of ‘Dawud’ 
as a patriarch, in exchange of taking the money he needed from ‘Abu el -
Fetouĥ’ and ‘Dawud.’ In this way, ‘Dawud’ sat on the patriarch throne by force 
as the 75th pope of Alexandria under the name ‘Cyril III,’ and the ordination 
rite was performed in St. ‘Sergius’ Church in the year 1235 AD, in spite of the 
opposition of most of the bishops and the cry-outs of multitudes of the Copts. 
His Simonism: 
‘Cyril III,’ who was known as ‘ibn-Loqloq,’ needed significant funds, partly 
to enable him to pay the sultan ’s court for its support of his ordination. He 
raised the money by applying the ‘Simoniacal’ practice and by the sale of the 
empty episcopal seats to the highest bidders. Many of these seats had fallen 
vacant during the long interregnum. This practice alarmed the community of 
the faithful, who protested against these practices. The rebellious congregation 
found a leader for their opposition movement in the person of a monk named 
'Imad’ (Hamid) of Anba ‘Macarius monastery. ’ The change was further 
strengthened by a Coptic archon named ‘Saniy al -Dawlah ibn al -Thu’ban,’ 
who insisted that  ‘Cyril’ was pope only by bribery and corruption, and he 
raised serious doubts about the legality of ‘Cyril's ordination. In light of these 
circumstances, it was decided to hold a general council of the clergy and the 
archons to look into the situation and  make recommendations. The Islamic 
administration of the country favored the suggestion and sultan ‘Al-Malik al-
Saliĥ Najm al-Din Ayyubi’ (1239-1249 AD) took the initiative and summoned 
that council where, according to the Islamic historian of the Copts ‘Al-Maqrizi’ 
(1364-1442 AD), the patriarch was sharply criticized. Nevertheless, Cyril, who 
prevailed upon the Coptic scribes of the administration while bribing the 
sultan’s court with 12,000 dinars, was able to swing the verdict in his favor. In 
this way, the opposition to the patriarchal party was stifled, and ‘Cyril III ibn-
Loqloq’ was able to hold his own and rule the church in his approach and a 
wave of relative peace until his death.  
Offending the Patriarch of Antioch: 
This pope, after all, what he di d against his bishops, he turned his offense 
toward the patriarch of Antioch, with the excuse of that many Copts lived in

CYRIL V , The 112th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA 
This pope of Alexandria lived in an agitated political atmosphere. However, 
he managed to steer the ship by a patriotic spirit without disregarding the 
spiritual and church aspects.  
In the Paramus Monastery: 
‘Yoĥanna’ was born in the village of ‘Tizmant’ in ‘Beni-Sweif’ province in 
the year 1824, and when he grew up, he was known as ‘Ĥanna al-Nasikh’ (the 
Script) because of his beautiful handwriting. He became a monk in the year 
1844 in the ‘Paramus’ monastery in ‘Wadi al -Natrun,’ by the name of: 
‘Yoĥanna of Paramus.’ At that time, the financial situation of the monastery 
was terrib le, and they had only four monks residing there. Due to the 
tremendous spiritual life and asceticism of the monk ‘Yoĥanna’ and his great 
interest in reading and inscribing, the Holy Bible drew so many to the monastic 
life. Two years after he became a monk, his fellow monks sought from the pope 
to have him ordained as a priest. The 111 th pope ‘Demetrius II’ (1862-1870) 
ordained him. When the pope sensed his seriousness and spirituality, he was 
planning to keep him in the patriarchate to help him. However, th e ‘Paramus’ 
monks wrote to the pope asking him to send their priest back to them, and he 
went along with their request. 
Again, the pope called Fr. ‘Yoĥanna’ later on, ordained him as a Hegumen 
(proto-priest), and kept him to serve at the Cathedral of ‘Azbakieh’ in Cairo. 
When again the monks wrote to the pope begging to send him back to them, 
he still responded to their request. 
Ordained as Pope of Alexandria (1874-1927): 
After the repose of pope ‘Demetrius II’ in 1870, the papal throne remained 
vacant for four years and nine months, although everybody was expecting that 
Fr. ‘Yoĥanna of Paramus’ would fill it. 
Finally, the ‘General Congregational Council, ’ which ran the church ’s 
financial affairs, presented a request to the government about his ordination. 
Then, Hegumen ‘Yoĥanna’ was ordained as a patriarch on the 1st of November 
1874, by the name of Pope ‘Cyril V .’ The sons of khedive attended the 
celebration: ‘Ismaåil Pasha, ’ ‘ Tewfik Pasha, ’ ‘ Hussein Pasha Kamel, ’ and 
‘Hassan Pasha;’ along with a number of government ministers. 
The Political Situation: 
Due to huge accumulated debts after the Suez Canal construction, Egypt at 
that time was passing through a horrible political struggle. Khedive ‘Ismaåil 
Pasha’ (1863-1879) was exiled, and his son ‘Tewfik Pasha’ ruled in his place.

St. ‘Cyril’ was born in Jerusalem or one of its villages in the year 315 AD. 
He has ordained as a deacon in the year 335 AD, then as a p riest in the year 
345 AD. Despite his young age, he was entrusted by the bishop to teach the 
catechumens to qualify them to get the Sacrament of Baptism; and to give 
sermons on the Sundays and feasts. 
Ordained as a Bishop (350-386 AD): 
In the year 348 AD, because of St. ‘Cyril's’ knowledge and piety, he was 
chosen by ‘Acacius,’ the bishop of Caesarea, to succeed Abba ‘Maximus III’ 
the bishop of Jerusalem ( 334-348 AD). Unfortunately, as ‘Acacius’ was an 
Arian, doubts dwelt upon ‘Cyril.’ However, he soon ente red into severe 
conflict with ‘Acacius’ and the Arians, while defending the Orthodox teachings 
concerning the Divinity of the Lord Jesus Christ. 
His Disagreements with ‘Acacius,’ Bishop of Caesarea: 
A controversy happened between him and ‘Acacius’ bishop of Caesarea, 
concerning their dioceses and “Who has the priority right over the other .” St. 
‘Cyril’ assumed that the priority would be to his diocese ‘Jerusalem,’ being the 
See of St. ‘James,’ one of the twelve apostles of the Lord Jesus Christ.  
Taking the chance of that, St. ‘Cyril’ took the liberty of selling some of the 
Holy Vessels of the church to feed the needy during a severe famine that dwelt 
upon Palestine. Because of that, ‘Acacius’ tried here and there until he got a 
decree to exile St. ‘Cyril’ out of ‘Jerusalem,’ without giving him the chance to 
defend his case. 
In the year 359 AD, St. ‘Cyril’ appealed before the Council of ‘Selucia.’ As 
‘Acacius’ was called to attend, and he declined, the Council deposed him and 
restored ‘Cyril’ back to his throne. 
‘Acacius,’ supported by the Arian bishops, soon seduced Emperor 
‘Constantius II’ (337-361 AD) to hold a Council in Constantinople in the year 
360 AD, which issued a decree to exile ‘Cyril’ again. 
When ‘Constantius II ’ died, and his successor ‘Julian’ ( 360-363 AD) 
ordered the return of the exiled bishops to their thrones, St. ‘Cyril’ returned to 
Jerusalem in the year 362 AD, and resumed shepherding his people faithfully 
and uprightly. 
Resuming his opposition against the Arians, they sought from the Arian  
Emperor ‘Valens’ (364-378 AD) to annul the decree of the return of the exiled 
bishops to their thrones; and ‘Cyril’ was exiled for the third time. When 
Emperor ‘Valens’ died in the year 378 AD, he was followed by Emperor 
‘Theodosius I’ (379-395 AD), who r eleased the saint from exile and held a 
Council of 150 bishops in Constantinople in 381 AD against ‘Macedonius.’ 
That council was attended by St. ‘Cyril,’ who opposed ‘Macedonius,’

and they received the crowns of martyrdom. 
Here, 640 pagans shouted aloud, proclaiming their faith in the Lord Christ, 
and they all, as well, received the crowns of martyrdom. 
 
DIOSCORUS I, The 25th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA 
St. ‘Dioscorus’ was the 25th Pope on the See of St. Mark (444-454 AD). He 
was a revered man, who beside s his spirituality and in-depth theological 
knowledge, enjoyed courage, steadfastness in the truth, and the willingness to 
sacrifice until death for the sake of the Orthodox Faith . Therefore, the 
Orthodox Church gave him the title: “The Hero of Orthodoxy.” 
His papacy started in a relatively peaceful time of the church, although he 
encountered many troubles after the death of emperor ‘Theodosius II’ (402-
450 AD) in the year 450 AD . This emperor, who was called by the church: 
‘The Orthodox Emperor ,’ was replaced by an unfriendly emperor ‘Marcian’ 
(450-457 AD) and his wife ‘Pulcheria.’ At that time, the theological debate 
about the issue of “Christology”1 flared up, after had been somewhat settled 
during the first three Ecumenical Councils. On the arrival of Emperor Marcian, 
plots were woven against the Church of Alexandria and her great bishops; these 
plots were led by ‘Leo I,’ the Pope of Rome (440-461 AD), who was a close 
friend to the emperor ‘Marcian’ and his wife. 
The Greatness of the Alexandrian Church: 
St. ‘Dioscorus’ succeeded the 24th Pope St. ‘Cyril the Great ’ on the 
Alexandrian Throne of the See of St. Mark . He should be regarded as one of 
the chief architects of Coptic Christianity and the Alexandrian Church. Owing 
to his devotion to the faith and his genuine character in defense of his high 
principles, he was chosen by Pope ‘Cyril I ’ (412-444 AD) to be his close 
companion in his religious meetings. ‘Cyril’ made him an archdeacon, and he 
served as the dean of Alexandria ’s Catechetical School. Pope ‘Cyril’ became 
‘Dioscorus’ chief mentor, and together they attended the famous Ecumenical 
Council of Ephesus I in 431 AD, where Cyril’s Christological formulas were 
accepted as the Orthodox definition of the Nature of Jesus Christ . We 
might assume that the archdeacon ‘Dioscorus’ must have contributed in the 
formulation of those decisions of the Council, being a power behind the throne 
of Pope ‘Cyril’ who presided over the Council . It was on such occasions that 
the personality of ‘Dioscorus’ became recognized within his church and 
throughout the Byzantine empire . This fact would explain the ease and

records.question: Who was St. Takla Haymanot?
records.answer:
St. Takla Haymanot is a significant figure in the Ethiopian Orthodox Church, revered as one of the pillars of Ethiopian monastic life. He lived from approximately 1215 to 1313 and is celebrated for his deep commitment to a life of purity, chastity, and asceticism. His early life was marked by a strong desire to live a celibate life, which he maintained even when pressured by his parents to marry. After marrying, he lived with his wife in a chaste manner until her death, after which he was ordained as a priest by the metropolitan of Ethiopia [1][4].

His transformation into a saintly figure began when the Archangel Michael appeared to him, urging him to abandon hunting and instead dedicate his life to prayer, studying the Holy Bible, and teaching. This divine encounter also revealed to him his gifts of healing and performing miracles, prompting him to change his name from Fish Hazion to Takla Haymanot. Following this revelation, he distributed his parents' wealth to the poor and began his missionary work, preaching against idol worship and leading many to Christianity through his miracles [1][2].

St. Takla Haymanot's ministry was characterized by his ascetic lifestyle and his role as a spiritual father to many monks. He founded a monastery in the Amhara region, which became a center for preaching and monastic life. His dedication to prayer and fasting was profound, and he often spent extended periods in the wilderness, especially during the fasting seasons. His life was filled with miraculous events, including raising the abbot of his monastery from the dead, which further solidified his reputation as a holy man [2][3].

Throughout his life, he faced significant opposition and persecution, particularly from those who adhered to pagan practices. However, he remained steadfast in his mission, moving from city to city to spread the Gospel and combat sorcery and idol worship. His legacy continues to inspire many, and he is often depicted with six wings, symbolizing his angelic nature and divine favor [1][2].

lived a life of purity and chastity; and when his parents urged him to get 
married, he refrained, proclaiming his desire to live a celibate life . However, 
when they forced him to do so, he lived with his wife like brother and sister 
until she reposed in the Lord. Then, the metropolitan of Ethiopia ordained him 
as a priest. His mother reposed on the 22 nd of Mesra, and his father followed 
her after only four days. 
This young priest lived in his parent’s house for another seven years. Then, 
it happened one day when he went out to hunt animals, that the Archangel 
Michael appeared to  him and told him that such action is not befitting for a 
priest, but he should instead dedicate h is life to prayers, to the study of the 
Holy Bible and teaching. He told him also that God has granted him the gift of 
healing of the sick and performing miracles, and that his name from now on 
would not be Fish Hazion, but Takla Haymanot. It was also said that the Lord 
Jesus Christ put His hand on him and blessed him after calling him to the 
preaching work and promised to be with him and support him . The saint then 
distributed all his parents’ wealth on the poor , bid farewell to the inhabitants 
of his city, and set forth to preach. 
His Preaching and Monastic Ministry: 
St. Takla Haymanot set forth to the region of Katata, where its inhabitants 
worshipped the idols, the trees, and the sun. There, the people were stirred up 
against him, mainly that they heard the voice of the devil from the tree, their 
idol, seeking from them to send him away. As for him, he stood afar, faced the 
East, raised his hands, and prayed, asking God to destroy that tree. So, the tree 
was uprooted and moved toward the saint, and then the devil confessed 
publicly that he was leading the people to vanity. On his hands, God performed 
so many miracles, which caused many to believe and be baptized in the water 
of the River. The region’s prince was saddened by uprooting that tree because 
it was producing a high income for him. And, when he came to inspect it, he 
found out that the saint ordered to use its wood to build a church. However, the 
prince fell ill , and the saint healed him in the name of the Holy Trinity . This 
miracle made him, his wife Acrocina and his three sons, get baptized , and the 
children's names were replaced with Christian ones. Together with them, many 
other people were also baptized . His ascetic life merged with his preaching 
work, so he was a true hermit who spent most of the forty days fasting period 
in the wilderness in a robust ascetic way, to come b ack to his brethren and 
children to care for them with stronger love. 
The people got so attached to him, but in obedience to the Lord’s 
commandment, he had to move from one city to another in Ethiopia, to preach 
the Gospel, and to oppose the idol worship a nd the works of sorcery . So, he 
faced significant troubles and opposition; but God supported him with the

miracles and the healings He performed through him. 
Besides his preaching work, he lived as a Father to so many monks . In the 
monastery which the sain t founded in the Amhara region, he practiced the 
monastic life with the spirit of worship and watching the nights, in addition to 
serving the others and ministering to the poor . The monks of the area 
considered him as an angel and not as a normal human bei ng. The monastery 
turned into a center of preaching. It was said that the Abbot of that monastery 
died, and he was bitterly mourned by all . Here, St. Takla Haymanot came to 
where the corpse was and prayed to God, who raised the monastery ’s Abbot 
from the dead. The nephew of the risen man was a priest, and he came rushing 
to cry at the feet of the saint seeking his forgiveness. He confessed to him that 
he used to envy his uncle on what God has granted him of gifts, and how badly 
he was aspiring to occupy his  place as the Abbot of the monastery after his 
death. And, asked the saint to pray on his behalf, and commended him for his 
holy life and his love even for those envious people. 
When the saint felt that temporal glory would chase him after raising that 
monastery’s Abbot from the dead, he cried out to the Lord to take him away 
from that place. The Archangel Michael advised him to go to the monastery of 
St. Istifanos (Steven), headed by ‘Iyasus Mo’a’ ( =Jesus overcomes) . He 
forsook the region of Amhara, until he reached the river, where the angel 
walked along with him on the water to reach that monastery. 
St. Takla Haymanot dedicated his time to worship and making metanoias 
with incredible perseverance that the Lord allow ed him to see the heavenly 
Jerusalem and the thrones of glory prepared for those who strive. There, he 
heard a voice calling his name, telling him that he would be counted among 
the 24 priests and was given a golden censor to raise incense with them, and to 
praise the Lord along with them . From that monastery , he moved to the 
monastery of Abuna Aregawi on the high mountain of Debre Damo. There, he 
met with Abbot Yoĥannes (John), the Abbot of the monastery and the spiritual 
mentor of Iyasus Moʹa. Abbot Yoĥannes clothed St. Takla Haymanot with the 
monastic Great Eskeem, and he remained there for 12 years practicing the 
ascetic life. Then, after bidding the Abbot of the monastery and the brethren 
farewell, they tied him to a rope to bring him down from the monastery on the 
top of the mountain to the valley below. However, during that process, the rope 
was torn, and everybody assumed that the saint would fall to his death . But, 
behold! They watched how amazing wings emerged out of the saint’s back to 
let him fly and get down safely. That is why he is often portrayed like a Cherub 
with six wings. Then, the saint kept moving from one monastery to another; 
and the power of God kept working with him and within him.  
It was also said that he went to Jerusalem, where he met with the 78th Pope 
of Alexandria, St. Gabriel III (12 68-1271); he got the blessing of the Holy

her the good news that she would be granted a child who would be a cause of 
blessing to so many.  
In the morning, she put on the royal attire and was escorted to the king who 
greatly rejoiced to see her . He rewarded the soldiers with precious gifts and 
sought from them to bring her to the idols’ temple to hold an official celebration 
of their marriage. The king came into the temple, worshipped before the idols; 
while she stood waiting for God to rescue her . Then, suddenly a lightning, 
thunder and earthquakes took place; and the Archangel Michael came down to 
carry her to the church, where she used to pray with her husband the priest. 
On seeing how splendid she looked in her royal attire with her face covered 
with a veil; her husband assumed that she was one of the royal household. She 
revealed her identity to her husband and told him about all that God did for 
her. They both glorified God and gave Him thanks to His great mercies. In the 
evening, Sarah saw a lighted pillar in the middle of her house, with its top in 
heaven and embracing many dive rse birds; and toward which many peoples 
and kings looked with marvel. The priest, on the other hand, saw as though a 
shining sun was underneath his bed, surrounded by many stars that shone on 
the whole universe. In that very night, Sarah conceived the blessed child, who 
was born on the 24th of the month of Kiahk. 
His Childhood: 
In the biography of St. Takla Haymanot, many events were mentioned about 
God’s work within him during his childhood. Among these was that: after his 
parents sold all that his mother Sarah brought from the palace of the king from 
splendid attire, gold, silver, and pearls and distributed their price on the poor , 
the land went through a severe famine, and so many people were suffering . 
The mother was crying bitterly longing to give something more to the poor . 
The suckling baby, seeing her tears, pointed his little hand toward a small cup 
of flour and touched it . The flour started to flow heavily from that cup . His 
mother hastened to bring all that she had in her kitchen for the suckling to 
touch with his hand to let her have plenty to give to the poor.  The little child 
was baptized, and called by the name ‘Fish Hazion ,’ (meaning: the Joy of 
Zion), to be raised in a life of piety and worship with a spirit of asceticism, 
along with humility and love for everyone. 
His Ordination: 
Having reached 20 years of age, the metropolitan of Ethiopia Abba ‘Girguis 
II’ ordained him as a deacon in the days of the 75 th Pope, St.  Cyril III of 
Alexandria (1235-1243). During the ordination, the metropolitan kissed him, 
declared that he would be beloved by God and that the angel of the Lord would 
always accompany him with a sword of fire in his hand . St. Takla Haymanot

218 
 
her in her small cell until the day she  would depart. She remained there for 
only two weeks, then she became ill and delivered her soul to God, leaving for 
us a great living example of the e levated work of God within the life of 
humans, no matter how evil or defiled their lives may be. 
 
TAKLA HAYMANOT, THE ETHIOPIAN, ST. 
St. Takla Haymanot occupies a prominent standing in the Ethiopian Church 
as being one of the pillars of the Ethiopian monastic life . He lived during the 
years 1215-1313 and was the cause of salvation to so many . His father, the 
priest Tsega Zeab (=Gift of Faith), was married to a charming and rich girl by 
the name of Egzie Haraya ( =Choice of God) or Sarah  in Hebrew. They both 
lived a life of piety, loving the poor and the needy. Not having any children, 
Sarah sought from her husb and to distribute all their possessions on the poor 
and to release all their slaves and maidservants . After asking her not to have 
them act in a rush  on that matter,  her husband , the priest , found her still 
persistent in her position. So, he rejoiced in he r counsel and did according to 
her heart’s desire. The slaves and the maidservants were intensely grieved, for 
they used to feel as members of the household , and some of them sought to 
remain with them in the house as brothers and sisters, which they did. 
When the pagan Ma tolomy became the king of Ethiopia, he started to 
persecute the Christians. He sent his soldiers everywhere around to apply their 
acts of violence against the Christians . One of the soldiers reached the house 
of the priest and planned to kill him with his spear. But, the priest managed to 
flee from his ho me and dived into a lake . The soldier stood by on the shore , 
waiting for him to come out of the water to kill him. After spending a long time 
waiting, the soldier assumed that the priest ha d already drowned. However, it 
happened that when the priest dived in the lake, he found the Archangel 
Michael covering him as though in a tent . Later on, when he came out of the 
water, he found that his wife was taken as a captive and the church was 
devastated. He then cried bitterly. 
It happened that when the soldiers realized how beautiful the wife Sarah 
was, they brought her up to their king as a precious gift . He ordered them to 
keep her in one of his houses and adorn her with gold, silver, expensive jewelry, 
and magnificent attire. On the other hand, she abstained from the superb food, 
and her tears never ceased to flow. By night, when all went to sleep, she took 
off the precious attire and put on her simple garment, prayed to God seeking 
salvation fro m that evil situation . And, she asked the intercession of the 
Archangel Michael, whose feasts she used to celebrate every month, by giving 
many gifts to the poor. Then, God sent his archangel to comfort her and to give

Ĥabib was a first -class ecclesiastical man who elaborately knew by heart all 
the Church hymns and sang them with the spirit of prayer in a very touching 
voice. With that beginning, Yousef Ĥabib became the teacher of the Church’s 
young men and boys and let them absorb the spirit of the Fathers . He raised 
them on the love of the church and her hymns. Then, when the church came to 
have a cantor, her beautiful choir of deacons and her affairs started to settle 
down. Yousef Ĥabib withdrew himself in humility and self-denial and shifted 
his whole effort towards a new field to revive our ecclesiastical heritage.  
Yousef Ĥabib, for a long time, has been fond of the biographi es of the 
Saints, in particular of those whose fragrant life stories had not been published 
before. He started to travel to the desert monasteries to search in their libraries 
treasures about what was hidden, and he brought to light tens of biographies 
and rare stories. He also used to research in the libraries of the Coptic Museum 
and the library of the Patriarchate, etc.  He even purchased a permanent train 
travel permit to go back and forth to Cairo twice a week for that purpose . He 
used to translate, res earch in the biographies of the Saints and their sayings , 
then returned home to publish them in small booklets, to the benefit of ministry, 
and for the improvement of the souls. 
In his extreme asceticism, he used to spend all his retirement income on 
these tasks with joy, and save nothing of it for himself . The many books and 
booklets he published on his own did not bring him any funds. He always lived 
poor without any possessions, ascetic , and a hermit in his appearance, food, 
drink, and attire. And, in this, he lived until he departed from this world. 
With the establishment of the church of Abba Takla Haymanot  in the 
borough of Ibrahimieh, Alexandria; he considered it his responsibility and 
without hesitation, he took upon himself to minister in the new ch urch. In all 
the Holy Liturgies and eves, he carried out the duties of the cantor and the 
deacon, with a steadfast spirit and self-denial. 
It so happened once, during raising the evening incense, while the church 
was at its beginning, and her books were no t complete; sometimes, they did 
not find a Holy Bible to read the Gospel of the Prime hour in Arabic. So, he 
simply took the Coptic Katamarus ( Καταμερος) book and read to the people 
the Arabic Gospel, directly translating it from Coptic to Arabic.  
His Life Style: 
He lived by himself, dwelt alone, and always he would say: “My 
supplication from my Lord Christ, is to give me the great grace to continue 
walking on my feet until the day of my departure from this world. I do not want 
to burden anybody with serving me or looking after me.” God granted him his 
wish, for he was never inflicted by any disease which would make him in need 
of help from anyone. His firm principle of life was to refrain from having any

passages.text:
157 
 
church. And, if one of his disciples happened to ask him about some thought 
that came to his mind, he would answer him, then seek from him to leave him 
alone, saying: “I fear that after I utter edifying words, we would slide down 
into strange talk. Hence, I keep you away from me." 
Even so, he was bed -ridden for several years because of illness; he never 
allowed himself to think about his cell nor to look at its contents; although lots 
of people have visited him and brought him so many gifts because of his 
illness. And, whenever his disciple ‘John’ entered into or came out of his cell, 
the saint kept his eyes shut, so as not to see him avoid having his mind 
distracted by anything around him, to keep it perpetually contemplating in the 
celestials. He once put about 50 bushels of wheat in the sun to dry. However, 
he noticed something he considered harmful. So, before the wheat had a chance 
to dry, he told his disciples: “Let us abandon this place." On seeing that they 
became sad, he said to them: “Have you become sad for the sake of the bread? 
I truly see monks who forsake their cells and their manuscripts without even 
closing the doors, but they leave them open". So, he cared to escape from any 
stumbling-block, whatever was the cost! 
[Benedicta Ward: Sayings of the Desert Fathers; pp. 26-27] 
 
AMON AL-TUKHY 
(The martyr) 
This Saint was of the city of ‘Tukh’ in the Benha. He lived a pious life with 
a conscious evangelic mind, with a total discard to the worldly matters, and his 
heart was kindled with the love of Heaven. The call to martyrdom came to him 
in a night vision, in which he saw the Archangel Michael calling him to go to 
Ansenah, to testify to the Lord Christ before its governor, to receive the crown 
of martyrdom and to make many pagans believe in the Lord Christ. 
In Ansenah: 
Joyfully, Amon set forth to Ansenah, as though running to his wedding. 
There, he met with the governor, who ordered his torture. They started with 
scourging him, followed by burning his body by hot iron rods and then by 
squeezing him in the Hinbazeen. Having reached the height of suffering, he 
was not forsaken by the Lord Christ. The Lord publicly appeared to him, 
surrounded by a multitude of angels. He touch ed His saint and healed him 
instantly. This glorified appearance made many pagans proclaim their faith in 
the Lord Christ. At this point, the governor ordered the saint ’s head to be cut 
off, and he received the crown of martyrdom. Julius Al-Aqfahsy, the author of 
the biographies of the martyrs, was present there, and he took the body,

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 79
passages.text:
79 
 
the Great. He practiced the life of solitude in the Western Desert, in the  
province of ‘El-Ashmonein.' He lived in a cave in which he shot himself in to 
contemplate. Despite his strict asceticism, he did not cease to practice the 
handwork to give to the poor. He also cared to counsel the brethren, and God 
granted him the gift of  performing miracles. In other words, his solitude was 
founded on an open heart full of love for God and men. His disciple ‘Ephraim’ 
gave us a concise account of his life. 
His Life as a Monk: 
The saint was born to Christian parents; they raised him on the fear of the 
Lord. He grew loving the life of seclusion and contemplation, together with 
his love for the needy. 
While still a young man, he spent a lot of time among the monks and was 
trained on the ascetic life and the handwork to be able to give alms to the poor. 
When he became a monk, his love for solitude grew stronger that he lived in a 
very dark cave, where God granted him a fountain of water to drink from. He 
trained himself on fasting, by eating once a day in summer and once every two 
days in winter . He practiced the perpetual prayers and was making 300 
metanoias by day and 300 by night until his skin stuck to his bones and came 
to be as a burnt stick. 
A Spiritual Center: 
Despite his great love for the life of solitude, he did not shut off his heart 
nor his cave in the face of his brethren. But his dwelling place turned into a 
center of spiritual radiation. The elder monks residing on the mountain used to 
come to seek his counsel, and he used to inflame their hearts with longing for 
the Christian perfection in the Lord. 
His Prophesying About the Death of the King: 
His disciple once saw him sad, and on asking him about the reason, the saint 
told him that on that day, the soul of emperor Theodosius the Great was sought, 
and the bonds of the State order w ere about to come apart. The disciple made 
a note of the prophecy date, and after some time, when he descended to the 
world, he came to know that the emperor has died on that exact day. 
Examples of His Miracles: 
1- A priest once came to him inflicted with a s kin disease that exposed the 
bone of his forehead. And, despite the persistence of his disciple in seeking 
from the saint to come out and pray for the sick priest, he did not pay 
attention to him. Finally, he explained to his disciples that, because the 
priest has defiled the house of God by adultery and taking the church money 
to spend on his evil desires, he had no liberty to seek healing from God. 
Later on, he had compassion on him and asked his disciples to tell the priest

264 
 
to execute the saint, along with three women who were following him … As 
the order was fulfilled, the two birds flew off the scene . Afterward, prince 
Lucius convinced his partner, not only to receive faith but to enjoy martyrdom. 
So, they both sailed to Cyprus, where they proclaimed their faith before its 
governor and partook with bishop Theodore the crown of martyrdom. 
 
THEODORE, BISHOP OF EGYPT, ST. 
This St. Theodore was one of the monks of the monastery  of St. Macarius 
in the 8th century. He was ordained as a bishop of Egypt, most probably during 
the papacy of the 43rd Pope Alexandros II (704-729). Bishop Theodore was at 
advanced age when Michael I was ordained as the 46 th Pope (743-767 AD)... 
The 44th Pope Cosmas I (729-730 AD) and the 45th Pope Theodore I (730-742) 
resided on the throne for about 12 years, whereas Pope Alexandros II lived on 
it for 24 years and nine months. St. Theodore endured so many persecutions 
and sufferings from the rulers, and he stood by Pope Michael I (Khael I) during 
the persecution of the Church in his papacy. 
 [Maged Fr. Tadros: Biography and Miracles of St. Tadros El-Shotby, 1982] 
 
THEODORE, BISHOP OF PENTAPOLIS (The martyr) 
When Diocletian stirred up the persecution, he sent a prince by the name of 
Pilate to north Africa. Pilate heard that St. Theodore, who was ordained as a 
bishop on the Five Western Cities (west of Alexandria) by the 16 th Pope St. 
Theona (282-300 AD), was holding the Christians fast onto their faith, and was 
urging them not to deny their Christ. So, he called him in and sought from him 
to offer a sacrifice to the idols . The saint replied: “Every day, I do offer a 
sacrifice to the Creator of these idols.” The prince said to him: “You mean that 
Artamis, Apollon and the other gods have a Creator, and therefore, they are not 
gods?” The bishop answered him: “Yes! My Lord Jesus Christ is the Creator 
of all.” Provoked to anger, the prince ordered his men to torture him. So, they 
spent forty days beating and scourging him, squeezing his body and crucifying 
him. Having held fast to his faith and grew bolder, the prince ordered to cut his 
head off . And, he received the crown of martyrdom . The Coptic Church 
celebrates the martyrdom of St. Theodore on the 10th of Abib... 
 [Renet Basset: Le Synaxaire Arabe; Abib 10] 
 
THEODORE, BISHOP OF TYANA 
Bishop was a friend and a countryman of St. Gregory of Nazianzus (329-

barefooted on the live coal. The saint did not hesitate to take his sandals off 
and walked steadily on the live coal, as though on a lawn grass. Then, he started 
to rebuke the governor, that he should confess the Lord Christ who can turn 
the live coal into dew. The governor, however, accused him of sorcery.  
Finally, when the saint entered into a debate with the governor , he ordered 
to cut his head off, in Via Labicana, 3 miles away from Rome . The Western 
Church celebrates the feast of the martyr Tiburtius on the 11th of August. 
 
TIGRIUS, THE PRIEST, ST. 
This saint’s name is bound to that of Eutropius the reader; both of them had 
suffered great tribulations on account of their friendship to St. John 
Chrysostom (349-407 AD). St. Tigrius was a priest in Constantinople and a 
close friend of the archbishop John Chrysostom. Tigrius initially used to work 
as a slave in a house of one of the elites and they made him eunuch . Later on, 
owing to his faithfulness and piety, his master rewarded him by giving him his 
freedom. St. Tigrius had an exalted love toward the poor and he led a holy life 
that made him loved by everyone . Then, he was ordained as a priest; despite 
being eunuch1. As a priest, he showed an intense zeal in shepherding his flock 
and great love toward the poor and the strangers. St. Tigrius attended the Oak 
Tree Council, which condemned his friend, the archbishop John Chrysostom. 
And, after the later was sent into exile, the governor Optatius who was a pagan, 
called him and made him taste intense sufferings, in an attempt to please 
empress Eudoxia. Accusing him and Eutropius, of being trouble -makers and 
that they were behind burning the magnificent cathedral down . He was so 
violently whipped that his bones were exposed, his body was combed by sharp 
iron combs, and was finally exiled to Mesopotamia. 
 [Fr. Tadros Y Malaty: St. John Chrysostom, 1980, pp. 98-100]  
 
TIKHON, BISHOP OF AMATHUS, ST. 
St. Tikhon (Tychon) is considered one of the early bishops of the city of 
Amathus. That city was located where the city of Limassol is now on the 
southern coast of Cyprus. He was a man of the 5th century, and the inhabitants 
of the island honored him as being ‘The Wonder -Maker’ and considered him 
as ‘The Intercessor of the Vine-dressers’, for which the island is famous… 
Two amazing things were known about him: The first that while he was

he was a slave… However, the See of Alexandria does not allow such ordination…

310 
 
whose fame will spread all over the earth .” That was soon realized; as the 
young ‘Barsumas’ having reached the age, he left his parents and headed to the 
Euphrates River, where he dwelt for some time with a saint named ‘Ibrahim’ 
and became his disciple. 
‘Barsumas’ loved the solitude, so he dwelt in seclusion on the mountain, 
where a multitude of pious people came to become disciples under his 
guidance. He was so se vere in his monastic  life that he som etimes ate only 
once every week and was given by God the grace of performing miracles . A 
great famine came on the land , and he prayed to God who lifted it . Also, the 
salty water on the mountain  where he dwelt, by his prayers to God, became 
sweet. 
He was contemporary to St. ‘Simon the Stylite ’ (St. Samåan el-Ămoudi), 
and when he heard about him, he went to visit him , and they both had one 
another's blessings. Having been an opponent to the ‘Nestorian heresy,’ he took 
part in the council of Ephesus by invitation from emperor ‘Theodosius II’ (402-
450 AD), who honored him much. 
When the awful Chalcedonian c ouncil has been held in the year 451 AD, 
the emperor ‘Marcian’ (450-457 AD) sought to ban his attendance. However, 
the saint strongly opposed the council' s decisions, and he encountered great 
anguish and troubles for doing so. 
Four days before he reposed, an angel came to let him know when he was 
going to depart. So, he gathered many of his disciples together, urged them to 
hold fast to the Orthodox f aith, and then reposed. At the time of his repose , a 
ray of light was seen at the entrance of his cell. 
               [The Synaxarion: 9 Amshir] 
 
BASADI, THE MARTYR 
(The martyr) 
The Coptic Church celebrates the feast of the martyrdom of the seven 
hermits of ‘Mount Tounar’ on the 29th of Paona. Their names were: ‘Basadi,’ 
‘Cotolus,’ ‘Ardama,’ ‘Moses,’ ‘Esey,’ ‘Parcalas,’ and a monk with the same 
name: ‘Cotolus.’ 
The angel of the Lord appeared to the hermit priests ‘Basadi’ and ‘Cotolus,’ 
and urged them to seek the crown of martyrdom by confess ing their faith in 
their Savior. At once, the two priests set forth to the governor, e lated in spirit, 
anticipating their crown. There, they met with five hermits coming by ship to 
the governor to get their crowns as well . The seven got together with one 
accord, testified to their Savior before the governor, who tortured them, tied 
rocks to their necks, and cast them in prison.
