PAUL, THE MONK 
One of the desert fathers told this story about a monk by the name of Paul  
(Boulus) from somewhere in Lower Egypt and he lived in Thebes:  
He used to hold a serpent by his bare hands and split it into two . Some of 
the brethren made metanoia before him, and said: “Tell us brother; what did 
you do that made you qualified for such a marvelous grace ?” He answered 
them: “Forgive me, fathers. Once the man acquires purity, everything would 
submit to him and obey him. Like the way , Adam was in Paradise before he 
disobeyed the Divine commandment.” 
 [Light Publications: Sayings of the Elder Fathers, 1983, p. 258 (Arabic)] 
 [Bendicta Ward: The Sayings of the Desert Fathers] 
 
PAUL, THE SIMPLE, ST. 
This saint was a marvelous example of a simple man, who by the grace of 
God, could strive to reach a high ascetic level, even though he started it at his 
60th years of age. This St. Paul (Boulus) was a very simple and pious farmer 
who got married to a very beautiful girl . After living together for so many 
years, he started to take notice o f so many rumors about his wife' s evil 
behavior. However, whenever he inquired fr om her about the matter, she 
would pretend to be a pure woman . Eventually, by himself, he saw her in the 
evil act . On that day, he forsook the house to her and set forth to Abba 
Anthony the Great, hoping to become one of his disciples. 
Getting to know that this simple farmer was sixty years old, Abba Anthony 
advised him to go back to his field and plow; on account of that it would be 
difficult for him to practice the monastic life at his age . Before his 
persistence, he sought from him to join a monastery in  the valley to practice 
with the brethren what suit his old age; but the old man persisted on not 
leaving that mountain. 
Here, Abba Anthony had no other choice but to put him under tough tests; 
and was amazed by his endurance, perseverance , and obedience . Among 
those tests that he left him four days without food or drink while watching 
him lest he would collapse. He s ought from him to  remain a whole week 
outside his cave, under the heat of noon and the severe cold nights, without 
leaving his place; and sought from him, after weaving eight meters of a cord, 
to loosen it and weave it anew . In all that he was obedient, worked with joy 
and extreme simplicity. 
On seeing his persistence with the spirit of piety, Abba Anthony accepted 
him as a recluse and sought from him to build for himself a cell on the way 
between the base of the mountain and his own cell.

of St. Paul, and shook their heads as if they were asking St . Anthony what to 
do. St. Antony knew that they were sent from God. He marked the place on 
the ground and they dug the grave with their claws ; according to St. Antony's

St. Anthony carried the garment of palm t ree fibers and presented it to

In the location where St . Paul the First Hermit used to live, a monastery

PAUL, THE MONK 
About Abba Ur (Hur), we know that he had a disciple by the name of Paul 
(Boulus) who cared much for the life of prayers, even though he 
misunderstood its meaning . He considered his prayers as a race to recite the 
greatest number of church praises. H e was eventually corrected by St . 
Macarius.  
About him it was said: 
He did not approach the hard handworks or the assignments of selling and 
buying; except for the littl e things he eats every day . However, he was very 
advanced in one thing, which was praying without ceasing. He set for himself 
a rule; to pray 300 prayers every day. He used to put some little pebbles in his 
pocket, and then he used to hold in his hand one of them for every prayer he 
prayed. One day, he came to St . Macarius, saying: “Father, I am very sad .” 
When the elder monk asked him the reason for his anguish, he answered: “I 
heard about a virgin who spent thirty years of her monastic life, reciting 500 
prayers every day . On hearing that, I despised myself, for I am not able to 
pray more than 300 prayers every day.” 
Here, St. Abba Macarius told him: “I lived for sixty years in the monastic 
life, reciting only fifty prayers every day; work ed for  what was e nough to 
earn my need of food; and receive d the brethren who come to seek my 
counsel. Now, here you are who pray 300 prayers every day, condemned by 
your thoughts. You probably, either do not pray them with purity; or you can 
do more of other things and you do not want to.”

THECLA OF PALESTINE (The martyr) 
This St. Thecla was mentioned by the historian Eusebius, the bishop of 
Caesarea. She was martyred in Gaza along with her brother Agapius the soldier 
in the 2nd year of the persecution stirred up by Emperor Diocletian (304). After 
they confessed their faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, she was condemned to death 
by being devoured by the wild beasts, and she received the crown of 
martyrdom. Whereas her brother Agapius suffered many tortures in Caesarea 
of Palestine and was also martyred [Martyrs of Palestine 3:6]. The martyrdom 
of this saint is celebrated by the Coptic Church on the 26th of Mesra. 
 [Eusebius: Martyrs of Palestine, 3:1] 
 
THECLA, ST. PAUL’S DISCIPLE 
This St. Thecla was a disciple of St. ‘Paul the Apostle. She was considered 
as the first female martyr in Christian history, in the same way, St. Steven was 
considered as the first male martyr. She endured so many mortalities, ev en 
though her blood was not shed. Many Fathers viewed her as a small model of 
the Virgin Church adorned with every virtue, coming directly after the Virgin 
St. Mary. And, some of the Fathers used to commend any great female saint by 
calling her: The New Thecla. 
This saint raised in  Iconium in Asia Minor . She was known for her great 
beauty, high ethics , and great fortune beside her excellent education. Her 
father, who was one of the elites of the city, cared to educate her that she 
excelled in philosophy, poetry; and was eloquent, daring, yet full of decency. 
Many young men wished to propose to her, but her parents chose for her a 
wealthy young nobleman by the name of Thamyris. 
In the year 45 A D, St. Paul and St. Barnabas passed through the city of 
Iconium, i n their first preaching trip (Acts 13:51) . Thecla happened to be 
sitting on the window sill of her house when she saw St. Paul. Then, the Spirit 
of God drew her to be intrigued by his words about the Lord Jesus. She met St. 
Paul, listened to him, proclaimed her faith, and then got baptized.  
During her continuous association with St. Paul, she felt a great longing for 
a life of virginity. Then, she cast off her vain adornments and stopped caring 
for jewelry, banquets , and worldly celebrations . This change in her life 
confused her mother, who tried hard to convince her to resume her early one 
and to get married  and have children who would s upport her in her old age . 
But, the saint firmly proclaimed her desire for virginity for the Lord’s sake . 
Here, the mother started to threaten her and resorted to Thamyris to help 
convince her daughter to get married . The man flirted with her, counting he 
could draw her heart to the pleasures of the world . Yet she persisted on her

wondered within themselves whether there were any others out there, who 
surpassed them spiritually to learn from them and follow their path. Among 
those Fathers were St. Anthony the Great, to whom the Lord revealed the 
existence of St. Paul the First Hermit, St. Zosima th e Priest, whom the Lord 
guided to St. Mary the Egyptian, and St. Macarius the Great,  to whom the 
Lord revealed the two married women in Alexandria, who lived by the spirit 
of love, sanctity, and asceticism. 
A Married Couple Living better than a Monk: 
Such a thought came upon one of the saintly elder monks, and a Divine 
voice informed him that there was a virtuous wife called Mary living with her 
husband Ephcharistos in a village in Egypt at a spiritual level higher than 
him. By the guidance of an angel, the elderly monk set forth to that village, to 
meet with that couple who did surpass him spiritually. Knocking at their 
door, the woman opened for him, while her husband was still away 
shepherding a flock of sheep. In the evening, Ephcharistos came home and 
joined in welcoming their guest. After they prepared dinner for him, the 
monk refused ultimately to eat until they would tell him about what was 
going on in their lives. Ephcharistos did not want to talk about their private 
life together. He just said: “I a m a shepherd, and this is Mary, my wife.” The 
elder monk persisted on knowing more about them and revealed to the man 
that it was God who sent him to them. Here, the man started talking with the 
fear of the Lord. He said: “I shepherd the sheep we inherited  from our 
parents, and whenever we make a little profit by the help of God, we divide it 
into three portions: one for the poor, one to accommodate the strangers and 
the third for our personal needs. Since we got married, my wife lives with me 
like a sister . Each of us sleeps separately. At night we wear sackcloth, and 
during daytime, we put on our regular attires. No one knows anything about 
our lives.” Here, Mary looked down and supplicated to the elder monk to 
keep their life secret until they repose.  
 
MARY MAGDALENE, ST. 
The Lord Christ healed St. Mary Magdalene (from ‘Magdala’) by driving 
seven unclean spirits out of her. She was one of the women who served the 
Lord in Galilee (Luke 8:1 -2). She also was present when He was crucified 
and went to His tomb  along with two others, to find the grave empty. 
According to the Gospel of St. Mark, she was the first to see the Lord Christ 
after His resurrection (Mark 16:9), and St. John added that the Lord entrusted 
her to carry a message to His brethren (John 20:11-18). 
Among the women who were mentioned in the Gospel, there was “The

A Favorite Disciple of St. Jerome: 
She was the daughter of St. Paula, the 3 rd of 4 daughters, yet the only one 
who followed the monastic life of her mother up till the end. 
Paula was of a noble family in Rome. When her husband Toxotius died, she 
dedicated her whole life to God in simple living, voluntary poverty and 
faithfulness, while spending all her time in worship and works of love. On 
seeing her mother doing all that, Eustochium, who was a 12 years old young 
girl at the time, absorbed her mother’s kind of behavior. And when St. Jerome 
came to Rome from the East in the year 382 AD, the two of them put 
themselves under his spiritual guidance. Such action stirred up Hemetus, the 
girl’s uncle, and his wife against them. They e xerted all effort to change the 
little girl’s mind from that monastic way of living and to lure her toward the 
pleasures of this world. The young girl Eustochium did not listen to them; on 
the contrary, she put on the attire of virgins; and she became the first dedicated 
virgin among the noble ladies of Rome. In the year 384 AD, St. Jerome wrote 
a beautiful long letter to this saint concerning ‘The Virgin Life1,’ an important 
message that concerns all virgins in general and not just St. Eustochium. 
When St. Jerome decided to travel to Palestine because of the troubles 
which he had in Rome, Paula agreed to join him. She was accompanied by 
Eustochium and some other women. In Palestine, they visited the holy sites in 
the Holy Land, before they set out t o Egypt where they had a chance to meet 
with the monks of Nitria. Finally, they settled in Bethlehem. 
In Bethlehem, three monastic congregations of nuns were established under 
the leadership of Paula, helped by her daughter Eustochium. They both helped 
St. Jerome in translating the Holy Bible to the Latin language (The Vulgate). 
And according to their request, he wrote comments on some of the books of 
the Holy Bible, and even dedicated some of his books to them, saying, “These 
two ladies are capable of judg ing books more so than most men.” In the year 
403 AD, St. Paula fell ill, and her daughter Eustochium kept serving her and 
praying for her in the cave of Bethlehem. And when she reposed on the 26th of 
January in the year 404 AD, Eustochium threw herself on her reposed mother, 
kissing her eyes and longing to be buried together with her. St. Jerome 
comforted her and tasked her to work in the service of the nuns’ convents. 
Her Departure: 
After her mother reposed, Eustochium took upon herself also the 
responsibility of caring for the congregation of the dedicated and widowed 
women in Bethlehem. She was in charge when a mob invaded their house,

557 
or St. Abu-Sefein the Martyr? He went to his house with such bitterness in his soul that he 
fell asleep in his chair …  and in his sleep he saw the heavens open, and the Lord of Glory 
seated on His throne, and Fr. Bishoy Kamel going forth to welcome  the saints to paradise 
and present them to the Lord Christ; and Fr. Bishoy exulted in those martyrs. The soul of 
the servant from Sydney rejoiced, and he telephoned me to tell me how much the late Fr. 
Bishoy cares while in Paradise and how he rejoices in the martyrs. 
When a church named after Pope Cyril VI was founded in Los Angeles, someone said 
to me that a person came forward bearing an envelope with a large sum of money and told 
the Coptic priest: “A group of us, Christians and Indians, gathered together and learned that 
this is the Church whose members were  martyred in Libya because they were Christians . 
Thus, we consider the establishment of your church in this area to be a blessing for us all.” 
1441. How does St. John conclude the Book of Revelation , regarding the Day of the 
Lord? 
St. John concludes the Book of Revelation by describing the heavenly Jerusalem  — or 
as St. Augustine  calls it, “The heavenly Church ”1360 — the glories and blessings of the 
heavenly Church, and the desire of our Lord Jesus Christ to come quickly (Rev. 22:20 –21) 
to take His bride the queen to His throne.  
Many authors, poets, and philosophers such as Plat o depict ideal cities  (in their 
estimation) prescribing for them  laws, arrangements,  and principles dictated by  their 
philosophy and way of thinking . However, very soon, mistaken or unrealistic principles  
infiltrate their models, and their ideal cities turn out in fact to be  deficient and riddled with 
shortcomings.  
St. John does not imitate their example but rather, ascending by the Spirit, his vision is 
of a true, ideal, and immortal Church, which is in essence “ the tabernacle of God … with 
men” (Rev. 21:3). As this was difficult to depict or express in human language, he recorded 
for us what he actually saw, but in simple symbols that leave it to us to go deeper into them 
and savor the nature of  this singular, heavenly city ; so far as  our spiritual stature allows us 
to comprehend through the guidance of the Holy Spirit. 
1442. What is meant by “a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the 
first earth had passed away” (Rev. 21:1)?  
The earth in which we now live and the heaven under which w e live witness to the 
power of our Creator and His sublime care. He has not left us wanting for anything. For the 
earth with all its laws, resources, and marvels is there to serve us,  and the sun, moon , and 
 
1360 Cf. St. Augustine of Hippo, City of God 20.17 (NPNF I/2:436).

up, resulting in keeping him awake in prayers. As for fasting, he trained himself 
to fast the whole week and eat only on Saturdays. His prayers and fasting got 
to hand in hand with his intense love for the word of God. He memorized most 
of the Holy Bible by heart. The Book of ‘Jeremiah’ had a special place in his 
heart; that it was said that he used to se e the prophet Jeremiah during his 
reading of his Book; that he was called ‘Bishoy the Jeremian.’ 
He considered hand-work as a significant part of building his spiritual life. 
He believed in the saying : “If anyone will not work, neither shall he eat. ” (2 
Thess. 3:10). His friend Abba ‘John the Short’ said about him that when a rich 
man brought to him plenty of gold as a donation, he told him: “The dwellers 
of the wilderness have no need of gold and should not have any of it. Go instead 
to the villages of Egypt and distribute it to the poor. God bless you.” After the 
man went his way, and the saint returned to his cell, Satan came to him, saying: 
“You fatigued me so much, O Bishoy .” And, the saint answered him: “Since 
your fall, and all your fatigue is in vain.” 
His Fellowship with our Lord Jesus; 
Through his pure heart, he used to meet often with the Lord Jesus Christ on 
a friendship level . He used to see Him, to talk with Him , and to enjoy His 
Divine proclamations. It was said that, having been so persiste nt in his great 
ascetic life and prayers that the Lord Jesus Christ appeared to him, saying: “My 
chosen vessel ‘Bishoy,’ peace be with you; I saw your labor and strife, and 
behold, I shall always be with you!”  
Another time, as our saint remained a long time fasting, the Lord appeared 
to him, saying: “You labored too much, My chosen vessel Bishoy!” The saint 
answered Him: “It was You O Lord who labored for me, but I have not labored 
at all!” 
A third time, the Lord appeared to him, saying: “Rejoice, My chosen vessel 
Bishoy. Do you see this mountain? I shall send you monks to fill that mountain 
to worship Me.” The saint asked Him: “Will You sustain them, Lord, in such a 
barren wilderness?” The Lord answered: “If they love one another and keep 
My commandments, I shall sustain them in everything!” The saint asked Him: 
“Will You save them from all the anguishes and afflictions mentioned in the 
Gospel?” The Lord answered: “Whoever fears, obeys Me and keep My 
commandments; I shall save him from all temptations! ” He then blessed him 
and ascended. 
Again the Lord appeared to him surrounded by angels. The Lord comforted 
him and blessed him . The saint worshipped Him and washed His feet with 
water in a basin, then the Lord ascended . St. ‘Bishoy’ drank from that water 
and left a portion for his disciple . The saint sought from him more than once 
to drink it, but the disciple was too slow. Then, when St. ‘Bishoy’ went to check

with great honor in heaven.’” 
His Love for the Salvation of All Souls: 
Saint ‘Bishoy’ had a disciple named ‘Isaac,’ who descended to the world 
and was seduced by a Jewish woman to forsake his faith, and he was converted 
to Judaism and lived with her . When he happened to encounter some monks, 
he asked them to tell St. ‘Bishoy’: “Your son, the Jewish ‘Isaac,’ has fallen and 
seeks from you to pray on his behalf to God to save him.” On hearing that, the 
woman said: “Even if ‘Bishoy’ come to me, I shall seduce him.” On returning 
to the monastery, the monks forgot what happened. Then, they were asked by 
the saint: “Has someone asked you to tell me something? ” They answered in 
the negative. The saint asked them whether they have encountered the Jewish 
‘Isaac,’ so they told him what happened and what ‘Isaac’ and the Jewish 
woman said. At that moment, they saw the saint retreat three steps backward 
and make the sign of the Cross on himself at each stage. Astonished, the monks 
said; “Even you, father, fear that woman?” St. ‘Bishoy’ humbly answered: “My 
children, the woman was the cause of the fall of ‘Adam,’ ‘Samson,’ ‘David’ 
and ‘Solomon.’ Who would be the poor ‘Bishoy’ to challenge her?!  Nobody 
can overcome the tricks of Satan in wo men, except that one whom God is 
with.” He kept praying and fasting for the sake of his son ‘Isaac’ until God 
saved him, and he came back and repented. 
Forsaking Scetis: 
In the year 407 AD, the first attack of the Berbers on the wilderness of 
‘Scetis’ took place. At that time, the monks escaped from the desert. St. ‘John 
the Short ’ asked St. ‘Bishoy’: “ Do you fear death, O man of God? ” He 
answered him: “No, but I fear a Berberian would kill me and goes to hell 
because of me!” 
St. ‘John the Short ’ went to mount ‘Kalzam,’ near the monastery of Abba 
‘Anthony’ where he reposed . Whereas, St. ‘Bishoy’ went to ‘Ansena’ (the 
village of ‘Sheikh Abbadah’ near ‘Mallawy’), and he lived in the mountain . 
There, he formed a close relationship with ‘St. Abba ‘Paul of Tamouh,’ and 
sought from the Lord not to be separated from him when they would repose , 
and God granted them their wish. 
St. ‘Bishoy’ remained in his expatriation until he reposed on the 8th of Abib 
in the year 417 AD, after reaching 97 years of age. He was buried in the castle 
of ‘Meniat el-Saqar’ near ‘Ansena.’ When St. ‘Paul of Tamouh’ reposed, St. 
‘Athanasius’ of ‘Ansena’ gathered the two saints'  bodies and buried them 
together in the monastery of abba ‘Bishoy’ in ‘Ansena’ (Monastery of El -
Bersha). The bodies of these two saints were returned to the wilderness of 
‘Scetis’ during the patriarchate of the 52nd pope Abba ‘Yusab I’ (831-849 AD).

BISHOY, ST. ABBA 
Our great saint abba ‘Bishoy’ represents the simple life striving in the Lord, 
that was founded upon the love fellowship with the Lord Jesus Christ. He had 
a personal relationship with Jesus that broke the obstacles down to open up the 
heart by the Holy Spirit that the Heavenly Groom would transfigure within it 
and reign with power and dominion! 
St. ‘Bishoy’ was born in ‘Shansa,’ a village in the governorate of ‘El-
Menufyia,’ around the year 320 AD. He was one of six brothers, whose father 
reposed when they were relatively young, and their mother raised them  up. 
One day the mother saw an angel who came to tell her: “The Lord says to you: 
‘Give Me one of your children to serve Me all the days of his life. ’” She 
answered: “Sir, they are all for the Lord. Let Him take whomever He chooses.” 
The angel put his hand on this saint, and said: “This is a good laborer for the 
Lord.” Being weakly built and frail in the body, his mother asked the angel to 
choose another one; but he answered her: “The Lord said ‘My strength is made 
perfect in weakness.’” (2 Cor. 12:9). 
In Scetis (Shiheet): 
Having reached twenty years of age in the year 340 AD, the young ‘Bishoy’ 
set forth to the wilderness of ‘Scetis,’ where he became a disci ple of Abba 
‘Bemwah’ (Bemen), the disciple of St. ‘Macarius’ (300-391 AD). There, he 
worshipped in seclusion for three years without going out of his cell. He grew 
in virtue and had his heart inflamed with love for God. 
Life in Seclusion: 
When Abba ‘Bemwah’ reposed in the Lord, his two disciples Abba ‘Bishoy’ 
and Abba ‘John (Yeĥness) the Short,’ spent the whole night praying to seek the 
guidance of God . An angel appeared to them and said that Abba ‘John the 
Short’ should remain alone in that location . In obedience, Abba ‘Bishoy’ left 
the place forsaking his friend, and d ug for h imself a cave near the southern 
rock, about two miles away from Abba ‘John the Short.’ 
His Strife: 
As he loved prayer, he made a hole in a high spot on the cave wall, then he 
fixed a wedge in it and tied one end of a rope around it . Then, he used to tie 
the long hair of his head with the other end of that rope; so that whenever his 
head would get heavy and drop down due to sleepiness, the rope would pull it

Millennialism (Chiliasm)1199 
The Book of Revelation speaks symbolically about the state of the Church during her 
struggle on earth until the day she meets our Lord Jesus her Bridegroom . It then begins to 
tell us of her heavenly matrimonial home  — that is, the eternal kingdom, prepared for us 
since the foundation of the world. This kingdom is not alien to the true believer but is rather 
an extension of what he enjoys here on earth as a token of heaven, and it is what he lives by 
in paradise from the moment of  his departure. Thus, in the last three chapters , the book 
begins to speak about the kingdom in which we live here, and  about the authority that we 
have over Satan and his soldiers as the beginning of an eternal journey  and a heavenly 
meeting with our heavenly Father face to face. 
1372. What is meant by Satan being bound for a thousand years (Rev. 20:1–3)? 
“Then I saw an angel coming down from heaven, having the key to the bottomless pit 
and a great chain in his hand. He laid hold of the dragon, that serpent of old, who is the 
Devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years; and he cast him into the bottomless 
pit, and shut him up, and set a seal on him, so that he should deceive the nations no more 
till the thousand years were finished. But after these things he must be released f or a little 
while” (Rev. 20:1–3) This angel who came down from heaven , has authority over hell, and 
is able to lay hold of and bind Satan is a symbol of the angel of the covenant: our Lord 
Jesus (Mal. 3:1) who came down from heaven and was nailed to the cr oss for the sake of 
humanity, having wiped out the handwriting of iniquity that was written against us. Thus, 
the devil has no place in us, and thus the believer is able to trample on Satan and his power. 
And as the Holy Bible says:1200  
“… now the ruler of this world will be cast out” (John 12:31).  
“Having wiped out the handwriting of requirements that was against us, which was 
contrary to us. And He has taken it out of the way, having nailed it to the cross. Having 
disarmed principalities and powers, He ma de a public spectacle of them, triumphing over 
them in it” (Col. 2:14–15).  
“And He said to them, ‘I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven. Behold, I give you 
the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and 
nothing shall by any means hurt you’” (Luke 10:18–19).  
“Because the ruler of this world is judged” (John 16:11).  
 
1199 See Fr. Tadros Yacoub Malaty, The Book of Revelation, trans., Victoria Malaty and Ramzy Malaty 
(Sporting, Alexandria: St. George’s Coptic Orthodox Church, 1996): pp. 219 –226.  
1200 See Fr. Pishoy Kamel, The Millennium (Our Orthodox Church Faith, no. 3) (Arabic).

he regretted it badly and was in bitterness for his disobedience. 
As the monks knew that the saint would see the Lord now and then; they 
sought from him to intercede for them to enjoy seeing Him as well, so the Lord 
promised to appear to them on the mountain at a particular time. The brethren 
greatly rejoiced , and all of them set forth toward the mountain . The saint, 
because of his old age , was at the rear . There, he encountered an old er man 
overcome with weakness and frailty, not able to walk, and none of the passing-
by monks cared to help him. Saint ‘Bishoy’ asked if he may carry him, and he 
did carry him and walked without feeling any labor . However, the older man 
started to get heavier and heavier; and the saint perceived that He was no one 
but the Lord  Jesus Christ Him self. He then looked at Him and said: “The 
heaven is not wide enough to accommodate You, and Your majesty shakes the 
earth; how can a sinner like me carry You? ” To this, the Lord  Jesus Christ 
smiled at him and said: “Because you carried Me, My beloved ‘Bishoy,’ your 
body will never see decay!” Then, He disappeared. St. ‘Bishoy's’ body is still 
kept in his monastery without de terioration up to this very day . Once the 
brethren knew about what happened, they grieved deeply for passing by that 
Old Man and not gaining the blessing of carrying Him. 
An Encounter with St. Ephraim the Syrian: 
By a Divine arrangement,  Mar ‘Ephraim the Syrian ’ came once to meet 
with Abba ‘Bishoy.’ As St. ‘Ephraim’ talked in the Syrian tongue, while St. 
‘Bishoy’ talked in the Cop tic tongue; the later sought from God to give them 
both the ability to understand each other without the need for an interpreter, 
and God granted them that, and they managed to spend a tremendous spiritual 
time together. St. ‘Ephraim’ learned from St. ‘Bishoy’ about the monast ic 
experiences of the Egyptian fathers, particularly of St. ‘Macarius the Great.’  
After a week, St. ‘Ephraim’ left. Then, a brother came to seek St. 
‘Ephraim's’ blessing, but when St ‘Bishoy’ told him that he just left, the brother 
started to run to catch him. St. ‘Bishoy’ called him and said he would never be 
able to because St. ‘Ephraim’ was carried away by a cloud. It was also said that 
St. ‘Ephraim’ has left behind his stick, in front of the cave of St. ‘Bishoy.’ 
Emperor Constantine visited Him: 
St. ‘John the Short’ once went to visit his friend St. ‘Bishoy,’ and while he 
was still outside his cell, he heard him talking to someone inside. Knocking on 
the door and entering, he found no one with the saint. Asking him with whom 
he was talking, he answered: “Emperor Constantine came to visit me and told 
me: ‘I wish I have abandoned my kingdom and became a monk; for I did not 
imagine how the monks enjoy such an honor and great glory . I see how those

The second interpretation: In St. Augustine’s1224 view, the war here is a spiritual war, 
rather than a physical one. The antichrist and his supporters Gog and Magog will use all 
methods of cruelty, violence, and deception to kill th e saints as they attempt to force them 
to stray from their faith.  However, God will support the two faithful witnesses Elijah and 
Enoch with the heavenly fire of the Holy Spirit that burns error, casts out fear, and sustains 
faith. By this fire the faithful will stand fast during the days of the two witnesses, and even 
more so after their martyrdom and the killing of the antichrist, and the Holy Spirit will 
rebuke many of those who followed the antichrist and resisted the Church that they might  
repent and turn from their evil. As for the devil, his end will be with the beast and the false 
prophet, when the wicked are cast into the lake burning with fire. 
1379. What is the millennial kingdom? And what is its true meaning? 
The Book of Revelation tells us that our Lord Jesus will rule on earth for a thousand 
years (Rev. 20:1 –15). During this period, Satan, who had previously entered into a battle 
against the Church, would be bound; and he, his angels, and his followers will be defeated 
in the Battle of Arm ageddon. Some have fallen into erroneous interpretations here because 
they failed to distinguish between the symbolic material contained  in the Book of 
Revelation and the literal, material interpretation of that material. Origen,1225 St. Dionysius 
of Alexand ria,1226 Methodius of Olympia ,1227 St. Basil of Caesarea ,1228 St. Gregory 
Nazianzus,1229 St. Epiphanius of Salamis ,1230 St. Jerome ,1231 and St. Augustine1232 all 
resisted this incorrect thought. 
This literal interpretation is adopted by  the Jehovah’s Witnesses, who believe that 
Christ will reign materially for a thousand years and establish an earthly kingdom. They  
also reject the doctrines of the Holy Trinity, the sacraments of the Church , and the 
veneration of saints. 
We need to understand that the Book of Revelation hides divine mysteries behind the 
veil of symbols. This leads us to the following conclusions: 
First: It is clear that the period of a thousand years is symbolic. St. Peter says, “But, 
beloved, do not forget this one thing, that with th e Lord one day is as a thousand years, and 
a thousand years as one day” (2 Pet. 3:8). The biblical millennium refers to the victory of 
the Church and the fulfilment of the message of the Gospel throughout the whole world.  It

is a prophecy of the establishm ent of God ’s reign over hearts , where Satan is bound and 
greatly weakened by people’s acceptance of the true faith and the enlightenment of all 
nations by the Gospel in the last times. 
Second: This millennium will be brought to an end  by Satan when his chains will be 
released for a while in the time of the antichrist; but the Lord Christ, in His second coming, 
will judge Satan and his evil angels and servants. After the Last Judgment, believers will 
enjoy the all-blessed kingdom of God, while unbelievers wh o insisted on not repenting will 
be expelled. 
Third: When the governor Pilate accused the Lord Christ of setting Himself up as a 
king, the Lord did not deny that He was a king, but said to him , “My kingdom is not of this 
world” (John 18:36). Is it plausibl e that  the King of kings and the Lord of lords (Rev. 
19:16) will change His mind and make Himself the king of an earthly kingdom? 
Fourth: The Book of Revelation warns us against straying from its words:  “For I 
testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: If anyone adds to 
these things, God will add to him the plagues that are written in this book; and if anyone 
takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall tak e away his part from 
the Book of Life, from the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book. He 
who testifies to these things says: ‘Surely I am coming quickly. ’ Amen. Even so, come, 
Lord Jesus! The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen” (Rev. 22:18–21).

After several years, the first Armenian version of the Holy Bible was 
translated from the Syriac language. It was said that St. Mesrop was the one 
who brought the New Testament and the Book of Proverbs to the Armenian. 
These translations were revised in Edessa (El -Roĥa) by two of his disciples. 
Then, a final revision was made by comparing them to the Septuagint version 
of the Old Testament. Also, they managed to translate the Holy Liturgies into 
the Armenian language.  
St. Mesrop preached and taught in Armenia and Georgia, established 
schools, and set another alphabet for Georgia, then he returned to his 
hometown. There, he created a particular school by the encouragement of St. 
Isaac, and he supervised its operation. In this schoo l, he translated so many 
books from the Greek and the Syriac languages to the Armenian language 
with the help and guidance of so many other saints. St. Mesrop reposed when 
he was eighty years old, on the 17th (19th) of February 441 AD.  
 [Butler: February 17 (19)]  
 
METHODIUS, BISHOP OF OLYMPUS (The martyr) 
The Western Church celebrates st. Methodius (Eubilis) on the 20 th of June 
and on the 18 th of September. St. Methodius became the bishop of Olympus 
in Lycia in the southern part of Asia Minor, then became the bishop of Patara. 
He has martyred in the year 311 AD in Chalcis in Greece. He was forgotten 
or disregarded by the historian Eusebius of Caesarea, probably because he 
opposed Origen. This saint was not the same as Methodius, the bishop of 
Petaris in Syria or the bishop of Phoenicia, who was martyred in Syria.  
His Culture and Views: 
St. Methodius seemed to have read Plato's works and admired his dialogue 
style since he authored his essays using the same method. He opposed 
Origen's views about the prior existence of the souls, the resurrection of the 
bodies with the spirit, and that the body is a prison for the soul.  
His Martyrdom: 
According to St. Jerome, St. Methodius received the crown of martyrdom 
during the last days of the persecution stirred up by Emperor Diocletian (284-
305 AD). However, others insisted that he was martyred at the time of 
Emperors Decius (249 -251 AD) and Valerian (253 -260 AD) in Chalcis in 
Greece. Yet, other scholars dismiss the idea of St. Methodius early 
martyrdom, on account of  that he was briefly mentioned by Eusebius of 
Caesarea (265-339 AD), as being one of his contemporaries.

him: “If you dwell somewhere, do not place in it anything under your name. 
Do not go out for meetings or eat in happy banquets, because this generates 
in you a false appearance which would bring you sorrow and restlessness. 
People are so anxious to find so mebody like that.” The brother asked him 
again: “Then, what can I do ?” The elder father answered: “Wherever you 
dwell, behave the same way as all the others. Whatever the trustworthy pious 
are doing, you do too ; then, you will find comfort. Humility is to be equal to 
everybody, for when the people see you r work according to the law and not 
deviating from it, they will view you on the same level as all the others , and 
they will never disturb you.” 
Being Pleased with People Hostile to Him: 
Fr. Motius's discip le Fr. Isaac told about his mentor that the older saint 
first built a monastery in Arakla, then moved to another location, where he 
also made a monastery. In that second location, there was a brother who 
always opposed him and disturbed him, and became lik e a thorn in his side. 
The elderly saint abandoned that location and went to his village, where he 
built a monastery which he closed on himself. Eventually, the elders of the 
monastery which he deserted came to him along with the brother who was 
hostile to him and planned on asking him to accept him in his new monastery. 
When they approached the place where Fr. Motius was and knocked on the 
door, the elder put a ladder and looked down from the window. Recognizing 
them, he asked: “Where is your luggage?” The y answered: “We left it with 
the brother so & so. ” Once Fr. Motius heard the name of the brother who 
used to disturb him, he broke the door open out of joy and ran to where the 
brother was. He worshipped before him, brought him into his cell, and 
honored him for three days. The brother was so pleased with such an attitude, 
which he did not expect. Later on, the brother left with the rest of the visitors.  
St. Motius was ordained as a bishop, on account of that he had the grace to 
perform signs and miracles, so was his disciple Isaac, who was ordained as a 
bishop as well.  
[Publications of the Light: The Sayings of the Elder Fathers, Lebanon 1983]  
 
MUCIUS (The martyr) 
St. Mucius (Mocius) was a Christian priest who was martyred in the 
persecution stirred up by  Emperor Diocletian (284 -305 AD). His biography 
indicates that he was a prominent sermon -giver who preached in Amphipolis 
in Macedonia.  
It happened that during the feast of god Bacchus (Dionysus), this saint

They followed him to the mountain, but they did not descend to the valley. The 
devil, in the form of an old monk went to St. ‘Christodolus,’ and told him: “At 
the summit of the mountain, there are monks who lost their way, they are 
exhausted, and almost perishing of thirst; let us go to lead them down here to 
eat, drink and live.” As it is the custom of the monks, the saint made the sign 
of the cross on his fa ce before proceeding, and at that moment the devil 
instantly turned into smoke and disappeared. So, it was always his way to 
overcome the devil, by the sign of the Cross. 
His Repose: 
He kept striving unceasingly until he reached old age. When it was time for 
his departure from this world, the three hermits whom he met previously came 
to him, prayed with him, blessed one another, and said to him: “The Lord sent 
us to you to tell us your story for the benefit of the brethren.” After telling them 
all that he went through, he fell ill for a short time, then reposed in peace. They 
prayed over him and buried him. 
       [The Synaxarion: 14 Kiahk] 
 
 
CHRISTODOULAS 
(The martyr) 
This saintly father martyr accompanied Abba ‘Bidaba’ and Fr. ‘Andrew’ 
(whose biography cam e under abba ‘Bidaba’), to martyrdom, in the era of 
‘Arianus,’ the governor of ‘Ansenah;’ and he received the crown of martyrdom 
together with them. 
       [The Synaxarion: 19 Abib] 
 
 
CHRISTODOULUS, The 66th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA 
An Anchorite and a Wonder-Maker: 
This pope was initially been from ‘Burah;’ a village on the west bank of the 
Damietta Nile Delta branch. Since his youth, he became a monk under the 
name ‘Theodore,’ in the ‘Enaton’ monastery (Dayr el-Zujaj), near Alexandria. 
The first recorded event in his life was about castrating himself. This happened 
when an Arab community descended on the monastery, and one of their maids 
tempted him. After yielding to her, he castrated himself in repentance and was 
saved from bleeding to death by the Abbot of the  monastery. After that, he 
moved to the ‘Baramus’ monastery in the wilderness of ‘Scetis.’ Then, he

A wonderful role model for the Eastern girl who is inflamed with the fire of 
the Divine Love, who goes above all obstacles setting forth to the spiritual 
work with a solemn Evangelic Ecclesiastical mind.” 
Her grandfather Flavius Ablabius was an influential governor of 
Constantinople and a very close friend to Emperor Constantine I  (306-337 
AD). After the death of the emperor, when Ablabius sided with the 20th Pope 
of Alexandria St. Athanasius the Apostolic who had powerful enemies at the 
court of the new pro -Arian E mperor Constantius II  (337-361 AD); he was 
dismissed from the imperial court and Ablabius retired to his estates in 
Bithynia. In 338 AD, Constantius II condemned Ablabius to death following 
false accusations of intending to usurp the throne . The emperor had her 
grandfather Ablabius executed in front of his own house . However, St. 
Olympias' father Seleucus, was also a governor.  
She was born around the year 368 AD , and when she became fatherless 
while still a young girl, she was cared for by her uncle Procopius, a friend of 
St. Gregory of Nazianzus . She was raised and educated by Theodosia, the 
sister of St . Amphilochius, the bishop of Iconium, a close friend of St . Basil 
the Great . She was influenced, as well, by the great St . Melania the Elder 
(341-410 AD). 
Known for her exalted beauty and riches, she got married while she was 
sixteen years old to Nebridius governor of C onstantinople, who soon died . 
When Emperor Theodocius I (379-395 AD) intended to get her married to his 
relative Elpidius; she firmly refused, saying: “If God wanted me to live as a 
wife, He would not have taken from me my husband Nebridius .” To apply 
pressure on her, the emperor held all her possessions in trust for her until she 
would reach thirty years of age; he also denied her seeing the bishops or 
partaking of the c hurch worship. She wrote to thank him for relieving her of 
the trouble of managing her wealth and to tell him that she would be happier 
if he would distribute all her possessions on the poor . The emperor was 
impressed by her message, and in particu lar, that she set forth to the e ast to 
practice the monastic life with a kindled zeal for four years. So, the emperor 
gave her back all her possessions in the year 391 AD. 
St. Olympias went to St . Nectarius, the archbishop of Constantinople 
(381-397 AD), to declare her wish to dedicate her life to God . So, he set her 
as a deaconess, although she was  still young. Since that time, she established 
a house for virgins (located between the Church of Peace and the Church of 
Hagia Sophia). She also cared for the service of the poor and the sick that so 
many people sought her help.  
As St. John Chrysostom was ordained as an archbishop of Constantinople 
(398-404 AD), he had high regard for St . Olympias since he found in that 
deaconess widow a fiery heart who generously gave all her possessions to

martyrdom. That night, the Virgin St. Mary appeared to them and told them 
that the Lord Christ has prepared for them an eternal place in heaven . That 
vision strengthened their faith a great deal. 
Their Trial: 
In the morning, the governor called them and attempted again to seduce 
them to burn incense before the idols . In the meantime, Mother ‘Dolagi’ kept 
crying out, proclaiming her and her children’s Christian faith, saying: “We are 
Christians, who believe in the Lord Christ the Creator of heaven, earth, seas, 
rivers and everything in them .” Following her lead, her children kept crying 
out: “We are Christians.” and they refused to worship the false gods. 
Their Martyrdom: 
Provoked to anger, ‘Arianus’ ordered cutting their heads off . They forced 
‘Dolagi’ to sit down and started to slay her children one by one on their 
mother’s knees. While they were slaughtering her children, she kept praying 
and singing. Finally, they cut her head. The pure bodies of these saints are still 
kept to this very day in the church , which carries their name in the city of 
‘Esna.’  
The Church celebrates the feast of their martyrdom on the 6th of Bashons. 
The original small church of Mother ‘Dolagi’ remained underground level 
for some time, until the reposed Brigade-General ‘Abadir Adib’ built a church 
at the same location above ground level. 
 [Talaat Ayoub Armanius: Mother ‘Dolagi’, 1991] 
 
DOMADIUS, THE SYRIAN 
(The martyr) 
Receiving Faith: 
This saint was raised in Persia, where he was taught astrology. He had a  
strong desire to be a Christian. So, it happened that in the market place, he met 
with a Persian monk called ‘Aughalis,’ from whom he learned the way to God. 
He was so jubilant that he kept teaching his household the way to faith. Then, 
he got baptized. 
His Monastic Life: 
Later on, he went to a monastery and became a monk . He lived a great 
ascetic life that brought on him the envy of some brethren . When he sensed 
what was happening, he left them and went to the monastery of St. ‘Sergius,’ 
where he became a disciple to one of their hermits for ten years. During all that 
time, he ate nothing cooked.

DINAH, PAUL, AND LONGINOS 
(The martyrs) 
The church celebrates their martyrdom on the 24th of Baba. 
[The Synaxarion: 24 Baba] 
 
 
DIOCLES, ST. 
(The martyr) 
At his 28th year of age, he was a scholar in philosophy and Coptic language 
grammar. He was filled with the grace of God, and he left everything and lived 
in a cave for 35 years, worshipping God unceasingly. Among his sayings: “The 
mind which strays away from the contemplation in God, would become either 
a devil or a beast.” By that, he meant that the mind which does not continually 
contemplate in the Celestial would be delivered to the demon of evil desires or 
would develop beastly lusts from within. 
When he was asked: “How would it be possible for the mind to be unceasing 
with God?” He answered: “The mind which lives in fear of the Lord under any 
circumstances, whether in thoughts or deeds; is perpetual with God.” 
[The Garden of Saints, p. 50 
 
DIODORE, BISHOP OF TARSUS 
‘Diodore of Tarsus ’ was a Christian bishop, a monastic reformer, and a  
theologian. A strong supporter of the orthodoxy of Nicaea. ‘Diodore’ 
(Theodotus) played a significant role in the Council of Constantinople and 
opposed the anti-Christian policies of Emperor ‘Julian the Apostate’ (360-363 
AD). ‘Diodore’ founded the School  of Antioch, which was one of the most 
important centers of Christian thought in the Early Church, and many of his 
students became notable theologians in their own right. However, while the 
School of Alexandria adopted the symbolic (spiritual) interpretation approach 
of the Holy Bible, the School of Antioch adopted the literal (historical)

MARY (The martyr) 
This saint was born in Atrib. Later on, she got married to a good man 
called Theodore and gave birth to a son, whom they called Sergius. When her 
son went to the governor Kyriacos and confessed h is Christianity, the 
governor tortured him, brought the statue of an idol, and ordered him to 
worship it. The young man, instead, kicked the statue and it fell down 
shattering into pieces. Before such a scene, the governor Kyriacos instantly 
believed in Christianity, saying, “A god, who cannot save himself, how could 
he save others? ” The minister Ohius then came forward and took over 
torturing Serguis with fire and other means. When Serguis’ mother and sister 
arrived at the torturing spot, they kept weeping for seeing him in that manner. 
However, that minister ended up having Serguis’ head cut off by the sword. 
His mother, Mary, his father, and his sister then came forward and 
confessed the name of the Lord Christ, and had their heads cut off by the 
sword too. They all received the crowns of martyrdom on the 13th of Amshir. 
 [Female Martyrs of Christianity, p. 91] 
 
MATHOY, FATHER 
Ordained as a Priest: 
It happened that the elder Mathoy (Mathos) once came out of Raythu to go 
to Magdelon with his brother. The bishop of the area took hold of him and 
ordained him as a priest. Afterward, while they were having dinner together, 
the bishop said to him, “Forgive me, father, I know that you did not want 
that, but I dared to do it to be blessed through you.” The elder Mathoy 
humbly answered, “To some extent, my mind did wish it, however, 
something was disturbing me, that I do not want to get separated from my 
brother because I am not used to do my prayers alone.” The bishop  told him, 
“If you think he is worthy, I may ordain him as a priest too.” Fr. Mathoy 
answered, “I do not know if he is worthy or not; all I know is that he is much 
better than me.”  
The Concept of Perfection: 
Fr. Jacob told the following story about Fr. Ma thoy, “I was once visiting 
Fr. Mathoy, and when I intended to leave, I told him, ‘I wish I could visit the 
“Cells.” He answered, ‘Please, Greet Fr. John , for me.’ When I conveyed the 
message to Fr. John, he said, ‘Fr. Mathoy is an Israelite indeed, in whom  
there is no deceit”  (John 1:47).’ A year later, when I conveyed the good

monks, martyrs , and bishops. In the book of ‘A Dictionary of Christ ian 
Biography,’ by Smith & Wace, 122 names came under Theodorus, meaning: 
“The gift of God).” 
Tadros the Bishop:  
The one thing we know about this saint is that he wrote to St. Augustine 
(354-430) requesting his advice about what to do with the priests who 
apostatized from the heresy of Donatism. That heresy caused a dis agreement 
in the Church, and assume d that the power of baptism depended upon the 
holiness of those who performed the Sacrament and that dissent also rejected 
the repentance of the sinners. 
St. Augustine asked the bishop to receive the priests who apostatized from 
this heresy with the proper compassion . Yet he should, at the same time, 
proclaim clearly to them that he did not accept their previous  opposition and 
that he despised th at heresy. However, he should not disregard the Name of 
God they carry; and should proclaim to them that he believed in their baptism, 
their priesthood, and their vows of virginity . He should accept them, but not 
their sins. St.Augustine requested from bishop Theodorus to show his letter 
[#61] to the others for them to be aware of his point of view concerning that 
subject. 
 
THEODOSIA (The martyr) 
St. Theodosia (Thaodosia) was originally worshipper of idols. She was the 
mother of the martyr Proconius (Aproconius/Procopius) of Jerusalem, and 
after his Christian father Christophorus passed away, she offered precious gifts 
to Emperor Diocletian (284 -305 AD) to appoint her son as a governor on 
Alexandria. The emperor did make hi m a governor and commanded him to 
persecute the Christians there and torture them . However, on his way from 
Antioch to Alexandria, the Lord Jesus talked to him from heaven, and a Cross 
of light appeared to him . So, he believed in the Lord Christ, and his p agan 
mother did report him to the emperor . The emperor asked the governor of 
Caesarea to investigate the matter and to handle his torture if needed. 
St. Proconius was put through so many tortures until he was on the brink of 
death. And, when he was cast in  prison, the Lord Christ appeared to him and 
healed him. When he was called from prison the next morning, and his mother 
St. Theodosia saw him without any wounds, she realized the magnificent 
power of his faith in the Lord Christ. Then, she proclaimed her faith in the Lord 
Christ, and she was joined by two princes and 12 other women in declaring 
their faith in the Lord Christ. All those who joined her had their heads cut off 
on the 7 th of Abib, in a martyrdom procession that preceded the saint’s, who

records.answer:
The passages provided do not specify the exact year when St. Barbara moved to Egypt or the specific location where she lived there. However, they do mention that she was born in a village near the city of Nicomedia and that she is associated with the region of Galatia, where her martyrdom took place. Additionally, it is noted that her body is now kept in a church under her name in Old Cairo, and some historians suggest she might have been martyred in Heliopolis, Egypt [1][2].

courage, talked to him about her faith in Christ.  
St. ‘Barbara’ was then whipped until her b lood started pouring. They also 
tore her flesh by hitting her with sticks full of sharp nails. During that time, she 
kept silent and continued praying to her God. Then, they clothed her in rough 
sackcloth over her torn body full of wounds, and she was cast  in a dark 
dungeon. 
While she was suffering from her wounds, the Lord Christ appeared to her 
in the dungeon, comforted her, and healed her completely. 
When the governor called for her on the next day, he was astonished to find 
her exultant with no traces o f any wounds on her body. He grew much more 
violent and sought from the executioners to comb her body with sharp iron 
combs, to put flames on her sides, and to cut off her breasts. Then, he ordered 
them viciously to lead her naked along the streets of the town. At this point, 
she cried out to the Lord to cover her nakedness, and God responded by 
engulfing her in Divine light. 
On seeing her amid her incredible sufferings, a girl by the name of ‘Juliana’ 
bitterly cried; and the governor ordered to torture her along with St. ‘Barbara,’ 
and to cast them together in the same dungeon. There, they kept praying all 
night long. 
Their Martyrdom: 
Governor ‘Martinianus’ gave the command to cut the heads of the two saints 
by the sword. While being lead to the arena outsi de the city, they kept on 
praying. And once they arrived there, ‘Dioscorus’ sought from the governor to 
let him kill his daughter by himself, and he was allowed. So, both St. ‘Barbara’ 
and St. ‘Juliana’ finally received the crowns of martyrdom. Their bodies were 
placed in a church outside the city of ‘Galatia.' 
St. ‘Barbara's father perished shortly after their martyrdom, and so did the 
governor who tortured her. The water of the basin that had the cross over it in 
the bathhouse had the power to heal everyone who washed with it. 
The body of St. ‘Barbara’ is kept now in a church under her name in Old 
Cairo. And, according to some historians, she might have been martyred in 
Heliopolis, Egypt. 
 
BARBASYMAS, THE BISHOP , ST. 
(The martyr) 
St. ‘Barbasymas’ (Barba'shmin) succeeded his brother St. ‘Shahdost’ as a 
bishop on the diocese of ‘Seleucia-Ctesiphon’ in the year 342 AD. 
This saint was inflamed with zeal on faith and the care of God’s people, and 
this stirred up the devil to consider him of being an enemy of the  Persian

they allowed those two hermits to worship another God on that same mountain. 
Forty young pagan men dedicated themselves to kill the two hermits, but God 
kept them safe and hid them away from their sight. 
Their Martyrdom: 
Then, it happened that ‘Maximianus, the partn er of Emperor ‘Diocletian,’ 
came to Egypt to supervise by himself the persecution and to enjoy seeing by 
his own eyes the shedding of the blood of Christians. 
The priests of the great idol went to complain to the emperor about what 
took place, and how thei r god declared his anger because of the presence of 
those two hermits on their mountain. At the same time, the Archangel 
‘Michael’ appeared to the two saints to tell them that the emperor would be 
seeking them and that the heavenly crowns were prepared for  them. The two 
saints then set forth from the mount to the messengers of the emperor and went 
with them to proclaim their faith before him. He gave the order to cut their 
heads off, and they received the crowns of martyrdom on the 7 th of the month 
of Kiahk. 
 [The Synaxarion; Edition of Rene Basset] 
 
 
BARBARA, ST. 
(The martyr) 
Saint ‘Barbara’ has gotten great fame in the East and the West; she endured 
so much to hold dearly to her faith. The Coptic Church celebrates her feast on 
the 8th of Kiahk and the Western Church as well as the Greek Church on the 
4th of December. 
Her Upbringing: 
She was born in the village of ‘Gamis’ near the city ‘Leopolis’ in 
‘Nicomedia,’ at the beginning of the 3rd century AD, during the days of 
Emperor ‘Maximinus I ’ (235-238 AD). He r father ‘Dioscorus’ was a firm 
believer in his pagan worship and strongly hated Christians.  
On seeing how beautiful she was and worrying about the corruption of that 
time, her father built for her a high tower and surrounded it by guards, and 
filled it with idols and all kinds of entertainments. He also provided her with 
great teachers who cared for her advanced learnings. 
‘Barbara’ having been a lover of meditation, she used to lift her eyes to look 
at the sun, the moon, and the stars, praising the God who created the earth with 
everything on it for the sake of humans. 
One day, some of her Christian servants told her so many good things about

156 
 
Gethsemane. While they were going in their way, some Jews came and tried 
to prevent them from burying her. When one of them stretched his hands to 
hold the coffin, his arms separated from his body and remained hanging until 
he believed and showed remorse on his evil deed. By the supplications of the 
saintly disciples, his arms were attached back to his body.  
It happened that Thomas the Apostle was not present at the time the Virgin 
St. Mary reposed. However, in his way back to Jerusalem, he saw her 
shrouded body being carried by the angels to be taken up to heaven; and he 
was advised by one of the angels to hasten and kiss her pure body,  which he 
did. When he arrived to join the disciples, and they told him about her 
departure, he said to them, “I shall not believe unless I see her body, for you 
already know how I doubted the resurrection of the Lord Christ.” They took 
him to her tomb and  were shocked and surprised to see it empty. However, 
Thomas, the Apostle, told them how he saw her pure body with the angels 
carrying it up to heaven. The Holy Spirit told them that God did not intend 
for her pure body to remain on earth, and the Lord Chr ist promised his pure 
disciples to let them see her in the flesh again, and they waited for this true 
promise until the 16 th of the month of Mesra when it was fulfilled. She lived 
on earth 60 years: she spent 12 years in the Temple, 30 years in the house o f 
the righteous Joseph the Carpenter, and 14 years in the house of St. John the 
Evangelist, according to the commandment of the Lord, who said to her: 
“Woman! Behold your son,” and to John: “Behold! Your mother” (John 
19:26-27). The first church, which was  built in the name of the Virgin St. 
Mary, was in the city of Philippi, in Greece. That happened after the 
preaching of St. Paul and St. Barnabas to the Gentiles in that city, and when 
many of them believed, they built that church. 
The Virgin St. Mary prov ided twice special blessings to the Land of 
Egypt. The first time when she fled to Egypt with the infant Jesus and St. 
Joseph the Carpenter, running away from king Herod who intended to kill the 
infant. the second time when she appeared in spiritual ways, inside and 
outside the domes of the church consecrated in her name in the area of El -
Zeitoun, in the suburbs of Cairo on the 2 nd of April 1968 (24 Baramhat 1684 
AM). Her appearances continued for many consecutive nights. 
The Church celebrates the Birthday of St. Mary on the 1 st of Bashons, her 
Entrance into the Temple on the 3 rd of Kiahk, her Departure on the 21 st of 
Toba, the Ascension of her body to Heaven on the 16th of Mesra, Building the 
first Church in her name on the 21 st of Paona, Consecrating the church in her 
name in the ‘Muĥarraq’ monastery, which the Lord Christ blessed by his 
presence along with His Apostles, on the 6 th of Hator and her Apparition in 
the church of El-Zeitoun on the 24th of Baramhat.

In the year 1961, Pope Cyril VI  (1959-1971) made mother Kyria the 
mother-superior of St. George Convent in Old Cairo. As a mother-superior, she 
cared for the spiritual activities and established a library for the convent, which 
included so many manuscripts. She was known for her generosity, even for the 
stray pets like dogs and cats, and for distributing monthly help to the unknown 
poor families. God granted her the grace of knowledge about so many events 
before they happened. Also, St. George the martyr appeared to her to inform  
her about the time of her departure from this world.

and the serpent you shall trample underfoot. ” (Ps. 91:13). Then, God took 
away the wild nature from the serpent and turned it into a companion of the 
saint for the following 20 years. 
As the sw eet fragrance of Christ spread from the saint, multitudes came 
from all over the country, seeking his blessings and prayers. 
His Support for those in Anguish: 
In his days, the church passed through very intense anguish, at the end of 
the 8th Mamluk reign of the sultan ‘Khalil ibn-Qalawoon’ (1260-1293 AD). He 
closed the churches all over Egypt, except for those in Alexandria, and he 
issued a decree that did commit all Christians to wear blue turbans . As for St. 
‘Barsum,’ he kept praying in the church, refusing to wear a blue turban. When 
some reported him to the ‘Sultan,’ he ordered him to be whipped, cast in jail, 
then released him to dwell on the roof of the church, where he kept praying 
with metanoias  and tears to God, to take His wrath away from his peopl e, 
forgive their sins, and make compassionate those who ruled over them.  
When he was reported again to the ‘Sultan,’ he was whipped and cast in jail, 
then released to set forth to the monastery of ‘Shahran’ in the vicinity of the 
‘Press of Helwan,’ where he lived a very harsh monastic life; but was supported 
by God, who granted him the grace to perform miracles and signs . So, many 
of those who were suffering came forth to find in him a heavenly comfort, and 
by his prayers, God eventually lifted the anguish.  
On the 5th day of the Coptic little month of ‘Nasie’ (the forgotten days), the 
saint reposed in the Lord at 60 years of age. 
 [Library of ‘Mahabah’: Abba Barsum El-Ărian, Cairo 1978 
  – including many of his miracles] 
 
BARSUMA, BISHOP OF NASSIBINS 
He wa s a Nestorian bishop on ‘Nassibins’ (Nisibis), before whom the 
Persian king opened the doors of his palace to spread the Nestorian heresy. He 
attempted to make ‘Nassibins’ an independent diocese from the diocese of 
‘Selucia–Ctesiphon,’ and he also established a theological school there. 
 
 
BARSUMAS, THE SYRIAN ABBA, ST. 
The Coptic Church celebrates the feast of the repose of St. ‘Barsumas’ the 
Syrian, the abbot of the Syrian monks, on the 8th of Amshir. He reposed in the 
year 458 AD. His family was from the region of ‘Samosata.’ Before his birth, 
a saintly man of God prophesied to his parents: “You will produce a good fruit,

150 
 
and then she crossed the river walking on the water. Seeing that miracle, the 
priest Zosimus attempted to bow before her. She cried out loudly, “O Father 
priest, what are you doing? Did you forget that you are carrying the Holy 
Sacraments?” She then approached, worshipped with reverence, took the 
Holy Sacraments, then raised her hands toward heaven, crying out: “Lord, let 
your servant depart in peace, for my eyes have seen Your Salvation .” (Luke 
2:29-30) She asked him to come to her in the following year, in the same 
place, to pray for her. She made the sign of the Cross on the river, crossed it 
back walking on the water, and disappeared from his sight. 
Her Departure: 
In the following year, and in the appointed time, the priest se t forth to the 
designated place, where he found the saint worshipping to the ground, with 
her face directed toward the East, and her hands motionless. Perceiving that 
she was already dead, he worshipped beside her, cried, and prayed on her the 
funeral prayers. Up to this moment, he realized that he did not even come to 
know her name; but when he got close to her, he found a written message 
saying, “Father Zosimus! Bury here the body of the miserable Mary and 
leave to the dust this sinful body. Pray on my behalf.”  
Fr. Zosimus realized that she died the year before after she had the Holy 
Sacraments he brought for her. It is believed that she reposed in the year 421 
AD. Returning to his monastery, Fr. Zosimus kept saying to himself: “Indeed, 
the tax -collectors, the sinners and the adulterers will precede us to the 
Kingdom of Heaven.” St. ‘Mary’s life was a big motivator for so many to 
expand their spiritual strive. The Coptic Church celebrates her feast on the 
16th of Baramouda every year. 
[Fragrant Bouquets from the Biographies of the Righteous and Saints, pp. 249-253] 
[The Vita of St. Mary of Egypt written by St. Sophronius, the patriarch of 
Jerusalem (634–638 AD)] 
 
MARY, THE ISRAELITE (The martyr) 
During the early life of St. Mary, the Israelite, she did not know the Lord 
Christ, and she led a sinful life. When she wanted to repent and to return to 
the righteous life, the Lord sent to her a saintly man who preached her and 
revealed to her the way of  salvation through believing in the Lord Christ. He 
told her that the soul would have to give an answer for all her deeds on the 
Day of Resurrection. After death and departure from this world, everyone 
will be rewarded according to his deeds. The man explained to her the fearful 
punishments for the evildoers. She asked him: "What are the proofs to what 
you have said to me since the ‘Torah’ that God gave to ‘Moses the Prophet’

389 
 
daughters. 
Paula's heart was day by day i nflamed with the longing to the Heavenly 
life; while the atmosphere in Rome was suffocating for her because of the 
fame of her noble fami ly and the criticism she got from her family elders , so 
she planned to leave Rome and go somewhere else to worship God in 
tranquility and peace away from her family and her old friends. 
In the year 385 AD, she sailed along with her daughter Eustochium  to 
Cyprus. There, they visited St . Epiphanius, the bishop of Salamis , and from 
there, they sailed to Antioch, where they met with St . Jerome. Then all of 
them set forth to the Holy places in Palestine , and from there, they went to 
Egypt to see some of its desert monks and hermits. 
In Egypt: 
St. Paula accompanied St . Jerome on his trip to Egypt and was most 
probably with him when he met with St . Didymus the Blind, the d ean of the 
School of Alexandria. She studied at his school for one month; then set forth 
together with St . Jerome to the wilderness of Nitria. In Nitria , they stayed a 
long time . St. Jerome described the effect of that period on the life of that 
saintly widow, he said that she was excited and joyful to see these saints and 
longed to imitate their lives. The fathers received her with joy, for which she 
glorified God and felt unworthy of such an honor . She met with the two 
Macariuses, St. Serapion and others . She visited them in their cells, 
prostrated herself at their feet, feeling that the Lord  Jesus Christ was in every 
one of them. She tolerated the harsh traveling between the cells and spen t the 
nights in the open wilderness with joy and enthusiasm beyond the endurance 
of any woman . She forgot her fatigue and all her needs because of her 
spiritual joy. 
In Bethlehem: 
In the next year, she set forth to Jerusalem to live in Bethlehem. There, she 
built a guest -house to gi ve hospitality to strangers, a monastery for monks 
and a convent for the nuns. 
In the convent, she  lived along with her daughter Eustochum  a serious 
monastic life, and according to the convent' s rules, all practiced the work of 
the hand, particularly sewing for the nuns or those outside. 
Paula lived among the nuns as a mother who drew them with her love, 
tenderness and she was their role model . Even though she and her daughter 
partook of ministry and work, yet she was firm . If, for instance, she noticed a 
nun talk too much or showing anger ; she would ask her to separate herself 
from the congregation, to pray outside , and to eat her meals alone for a 
certain period.

668 
ascetic life in a small hut in a village for about ten years under the guidance of an ascetic. He 
longed for solitude, and so he moved to Scetis and a cherub accompanied him on the way. 
He loved worship and asceticism, so many came from the East and the West to the wilderness 
to become his disciples. 
St. Shenoute the Archimandrite: He was the abbot of the White Monastery in Athribis 
(or Atripe), in the wilderness of Thebes for over fifty-six years (fourth or fifth century A. D.). 
He led 2200 monks and 1800 nuns. He was called the “Archimandrite” as he practiced 
solitude from time to time, and he encouraged the monks at his monastery to retreat to the 
wilderness after practicing the life of fellowship. In the year 431 A. D., he accompanied St. 
Cyril the Great to the Ecume nical Council of Ephesus. He is known for  purifying Coptic 
literature of Hellenistic cultural influences, and did not allow any foreigners to join his 
monastic communities. For this reason, he was regarded as a political leader and a social 
reformer, besides the depth of his spirituality. 
Amma Sarah : The first monastic group of women in the world was in the city of 
Alexandria, following the rule of St. Syncletica. St. Athanasius documented her biography 
and teachings. Moreover, St. Pachomius established two convents for nuns, while many nuns 
lived in solitude in the desert. Many mothers came from foreign convents to Egypt, like St. 
Melania the Elder (374 A. D.) and her granddaughter Melania the Younger (418 A. D.). Also, 
we cannot forget to mention St. Mary of Egypt who repented in Jerusalem and lived for forty-
seven years in the wilderness across the Jordan not seeing the face of another human being, 
except St. Zosima twice in the last two years of her life.  
Many nuns were given the gift of true leadership and spiritual discernment, like St. Sarah 
of whom it was said that she lived for sixty years on the banks of a river, but never lifted her 
eyes to look at it. Many of her sayings were preserved in the sayings of the desert fathers and 
mothers.  
St. Hilaria: In the fourth century, the daughter of Emperor Zeno fled to Scetis where she 
led a life of asceticism in the attire of a male monk. When her sister, Theopiste, was possessed 
by an evil spirit, the elders of the wilderness sent her to St. Hilaria to pray for her, and did 
not know that St. Hilaria was a woman. She prayed all night for her and embraced her. 
Theopiste was healed, and she told the emperor about the monk, “Hilarion,” who healed her 
and was embracing her, so her father was disturbed. He called for her to come to the palace, 
where she revealed to him that she was his daughter after he had promised not to prevent her 
from going back to her cave. 
St. Syncletica: Some historians regard her to be the equal of St. Anthony, the star of the 
wilderness; for as St. Anthony was the father of all monks, St. Syncletica was a mother to 
that group of virgins which transformed the fertile valley of Egypt into a dwelling place for 
the grace of God. She was born to noble parents who settled in Alexandria to be close to the 
School of Alexandria. They had two sons and two daughters, so they wanted to educate them 
in all sciences, which were only offered in the School of Alexandria. This family was shocked

passages.label: قاموس آباء الكنيسة وقديسيها, p. 357
passages.text: دعوة للانضمام إلى روما كان من بني مصر الذين اقتنصهم الكاثوليك بعيدًا عن كنيستهم الأصلية، ورسموه أسقفًا باسم كيرلس مقابل الأنبا كيرلس الخامس البابا المائة والثاني عشر. حالما تسلم هذا الأسقف مهامه الرعوية نشر رسالة وجهها إلى الأرثوذكس الأوفياء لكنيستهم في مصر وفي إثيوبيا يناشدهم فيها الانطواء تحت زعامة البابا الروماني بادعاء أن مرقس ما هو إلا تلميذ لبطرس. وعلى الفور أصدر البابا الوقور بيانًا مسهبًا أوضح فيه العقيدة الأرثوذكسية في جلائها، ثم أثبت أن مار مرقس هو أحد السبعين تلميذًا الذين اختارهم الرب للكرازة كما دعى الاثني عشر تمامًا، وقد طُبِع هذا البيان ووُزِع في جميع أنحاء مصر وقرأه الكهنة في الكنائس على مسامع الشعب. لما وجد كيرلس مقار أن البيان البابوي بلغ هدفه وبالتالي فشل هو فيما استهدفه، قصد إلى إثيوبيا وهناك أصابه فشل ثانٍ لأن الإمبراطور منليك الثاني كان شديد التمسك بالأرثوذكسية. وبعد شهور من تلك الزيارة جاء وزير إثيوبي إلى مصر وذهب لينال بركة الأنبا كيرلس الخامس فسأله عما حدث، ووصف له الوزير ما جرى وانتهى بقوله: "إذا توطدت أقدام البعثات الدينية في أي بلد شرقي أضاع استقلاله شيئًا فشيئًا، وإذا به على غير علم منه قد وقع في قبضة من زعموا تمدينه وتعليمه". بطريرك للكاثوليك فعودة للكنيسة ثم رفعت روما هذا الأسقف إلى مرتبة بطريرك، وبعدها فوجئت بما لم يكن في الحسبان، لأن الأنبا كيرلس مقار كان دائم البحث والإطلاع فلم يلبث أن عاد إلى الأرثوذكسية. ظن في بادئ الأمر أن البابا المرقسي الأصيل لن يقبله ضمن أبنائه بسبب كتاباته السالفة ضد الكنيسة القبطية، فسافر إلى الإسكندرية وقابل البطريرك فوثيوس للروم الأرثوذكس وصارحه برغبته في الانضمام إلى كنيسته. وفرح البطريرك الرومي هو ومجمعه بقبول الطلب ولكن رجال الدولة اليونانية رفضوا الموافقة رفضًا باتًا، وبينما كان كيرلس مقار في الإسكندرية وضع كتابًا في جزءين عن العلامة السكندري أوريجينوس بالفرنسية. فلما رُفِض طلبه سافر إلى بيروت حيث انشغل بالكتابة، فوضع كتابين على جانب كبير من الأهمية إذ يقدمان الدليل الواضح الصريح على مدى اقتناعه بالأرثوذكسية، وهذان الكتابان بالفرنسية أيضًا، أولهما: "الوضع الإلهي لتأسيس الكنيسة" وهو في جزءين، وثانيهما: "أخيرًا الحقيقة". ثم أتبعهما بكتاب ثالث عنوانه: "أخيرًا نتكلم"، ردّ به على بعض ما نشره الكاثوليك في مصر. قد تبعت ثمانون عائلة كاثوليكية بطريركها وانضمت إلى الكنيسة القبطية الأرثوذكسية وأشهرها عائلة "العتر"، وعلى إثر ذلك أصبح فرنسيس العتر أرشيدياكون الكنيسة البطرسية التي شيدتها عائلة بطرس غالي. ثم حدث أن تقابل بعض من أراخنة الأقباط مع فرنسيس العتر ودار بينهم الحديث حول كيرلس مقار، وفي اليوم التالي ذهبوا لمقابلة الأنبا كيرلس الخامس، الذي ما أن علم به

passages.label: قاموس آباء الكنيسة وقديسيها, p. 357
passages.text: عائلة "العتر"، وعلى إثر ذلك أصبح فرنسيس العتر أرشيدياكون الكنيسة البطرسية التي شيدتها عائلة بطرس غالي. ثم حدث أن تقابل بعض من أراخنة الأقباط مع فرنسيس العتر ودار بينهم الحديث حول كيرلس مقار، وفي اليوم التالي ذهبوا لمقابلة الأنبا كيرلس الخامس، الذي ما أن علم بهدف زيارتهم حتى قال لفوره: "اعلم يا فرنسيس أن هذه كانت أمنيتي من أول الأمر ولكنكم تسرعتم في طرق باب الكنيسة اليونانية، وإذا كنت لم أحرك ساكنًا يومذاك فما ذلك إلا محافظة على المحبة التي تربطني بالسيد فوثيوس". كو َّن البابا المرقسي لجنة برياسة الأنبا مكاريوس مطران أسيوط ليذهب 320

passages.label: قاموس آباء الكنيسة وقديسيها, p. 538
passages.text: ✞ غالي المعلم جمع الضرائب كان كاتب محمد بك الألفي أحد أمراء المماليك، ثم أسند إليه محمد علي منصبًا كبيرًا بعد غضبه على المعلم جرجس الجوهري، وكان المعلم غالي يسهل لمحمد علي أمر تحصيل الضرائب، ولكن هذا الأمر انقلب وبالاً عليه في النهاية. فكان جشع محمد علي في تحصيل الضرائب لا يقف عند حد، فقد طلب الباشا محمد علي من المعلم غالي ألف كيسًا، فقسم جمعها على المباشرين والكتبة وجمعها في أقرب وقت. محمد علي يغدر به كان جمعها بسرعة موجبًا لغير ما كان يتوقعه المعلم غالي، وسببًا في جلب الغدر عليه وعلى غيره، فإن الباشا بعد قليل أمر بمحاصرة بيته، وبيت المعلم جرجس الطويل، وأخيه حنا، وفرنسيس أخي المعلم غالي، والمعلم فلتاؤس، واثنين آخرين وأخرجوهم من منازلهم بصورة منكرة وسمّروا دورهم، وأخذوا دفاترهم وحبسوهم، وبعد أيام أفرج عنهم على شرط أن يدفعوا سبعة آلاف كيس فقاموا بدفعها. ولم تمضِ سبعة شهور حتى قبض عليهم ثانية وحبسهم في القلعة وختموا على دورهم، ثم عفا عنهم وأعاد المعلم غالي إلى منصبه، على شرط أن يدفعوا أربعة وعشرين ألف كيسًا. وتكرر حدوث ذلك من محمد علي، فكان يغضب عليه تارة ويعزله من منصبه ويرميه في السجن ويضربه مئات الكرابيج، ثم يعيده إلى منصبه بعد دفع مبلغٍ طائلٍ. وعندما أراد محمد علي تغيير هيئة الدواوين واستبدالها بغيرها، لتكون أقدر منها وتفوقها في النظام، حتى تعود بالفائدة على الخزينة، لم يتردد في الإفراج عن المعلم غالي والاستفادة من خبرته وكفاءته، مادام هذا يعود بالفائدة على الخزينة. وبعدما كلّف المعلم غالي بذلك، قسم المعلم غالي البلاد إلى مديريات وأقسام، والأطيان إلى أحواض، وابتكر أشياء كثيرة وحسابات تحقق مقدارًا وافرًا من المال، ولذلك يُنسَب للمعلم غالي تأسيس مصلحة المساحة، كما كان له دوره في تشجيع صناعة الأسلحة محليًا. ومن أعماله الجليلة أيضًا اقتراحه على محمد علي حفر قناة بين بحر الروم وبحر العرب ولكنه لم ينفذ. ونتيجة لنجاحه الكبير قابله محمد علي بالرضا وأثنى عليه ومن ثم َّ اتخذه كاتمًا لسره وخصّه مباشرة الأعمال الحسابية التي ابتكرها، فكانت يده فوق يد الجميع حتى حكام الأقاليم. أطلق إبراهيم باشا رصاص مسدسه عليه استمر المعلم غالي في هذا المنصب حتى مايو سنة 1882م، حين أطلق إبراهيم باشا رصاص مسدسه عليه في مدينة زفتى، أمام ابنه طوبيا فخرّ صريعًا. وهكذا ألقى المعلم غالي جزاء أمانته ووطنيته وخدمته، بعد أن أدى أجلّ الخدمات لمحمد علي ولإبراهيم باشا قاتله. وقد بقيت جثته ملقاة مدة يومين لا يجرؤ أحد على القيام بدفنها حتى استأذن رزق أغا حاكم الشرقية في دفنها، فأقيمت الصلاة على المعلم غالي بكنيسة أبي سيفين بزفتى ثم دفن بجوارها. 32

passages.label: قاموس آباء الكنيسة وقديسيها, p. 1816
passages.text: ✞ يوحنا بن زكريا ابن السباع هو أحد مشاهير الرجال في القرن الثالث عشر. كان لاهوتيًا ضليعًا وضع كتابًا بعنوان: " الجوهرة النفيسة في علوم الكنيسة " في 113 فصلاً، أوضح فيها طقوس الكنيسة وتعاليمها. وقد تضمن التعاليم عن التثليث والتوحيد وخلق الملائكة والعناصر والإنسان، ثم شرح الآيات الجوهرية في سفر التكوين والوظائف الكنسية وممارسة السيد المسيح لها على الأرض، فالأسرار المقدسة والبخور والأيقونات والمجمرة والمعاني الرمزية لهذه كلها وكذلك الأعياد الكنسية. وقد وصف المستشرق الألماني جراف يوحنا بن زكريا بأنه من كبار العلماء وبأن كتابه من المؤلفات المسيحية ذات العبارة الفصيحة ودقة البحث. قد طُبِع الكتاب طبعة قديمة وله طبعة حديثة سنة 1902م قام بها الرهبان الفرنسيسكان بالقاهرة. وللأسف لا نعرف شيئًا عن بقية حياته. وطنية الكنيسة القبطية وتاريخها، صفحة 178 . قصة الكنيسة القبطية، الكتاب الثالث صفحة 146 . ✞ يوحنا صاحب الإنجيل الذهبي رهبنته وُلد هذا القديس بمدينة رومية من أب غني يسمى أطرافيوس. ولما كان يوحنا يتلقى العلم طلب من أبيه أن يُجَلِد له الإنجيل الذي يقرأ فيه بالذهب، فعمل له ما أراد ففرح به كثيرًا. واتفق أن أحد الرهبان قد نزل عندهم عند ذهابه إلى بيت المقدس فطلب منه يوحنا أن يأخذه معه، فأعلمه أنه ذاهب إلى القدس وليس إلى الدير، ثم عرفه أنه صغير السن ولا يتحمل عيشة الرهبان التقشفية، غير أن يوحنا كان صادقًا في عزمه فسافر وحده في سفينة إلى دير ذلك الراهب. ولما رآه الرئيس لم يرد أن يقبله لصغر سنه وافهمه أن عيشة الرهبان شاقة على من هو مثله. ولما ألح يوحنا عليه ورأى فيه الرئيس ثبات العزم وقوة اليقين حلق له شعر رأسه والبسه ثوب الرهبنة المقدس، فأجهد يوحنا نفسه بنسكيات وتقشفات زائدة، وكان الأب الرئيس ينصحه قائلاً: "ترفق بنفسك وسِر مثل سائر الاخوة" فكان يقول له: "إن قوة الله وصلاتك عني تعيناني". عودته إلى بيت أبيه بعد سبع سنوات رأى في رؤيا من يقول له: "قم اذهب إلى والديك لتأخذ بركتهما قبل انتقالك من هذا العالم"، وتكررت هذه الرؤيا ثلاث ليالٍ متوالية، فأعلم الرئيس بها، فعرف إنها من الله وأشار عليه بالذهاب. 271
